entries.c7a498982725699755007cd3fb17808907cefe2d: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water to the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater, carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance.
entries.8f841ecc6d0fe023a583061f3614c22f490f8c28: The Library Directorate provides daily transportation of documents (books, audio-visual documents and video games) between the 46 libraries in the network and facilities of the Shared Services Centre - Libraries Division. To support these operations, the network uses a fleet of reusable handling bins for circulation and redistribution of collections. In recent years, operational practices have evolved to meet occupational health and safety requirements.
entries.b09f39c966e87afdab6c1eccc8c9d11701222531: On April 26, 2012, the sports facility called Le Taz, located at 8931 Papineau Avenue, became a municipal equipment. Since this acquisition, OTC contracts have been awarded to the organization Le TAZ, a multidisciplinary and community centre also operating under Le TAZ (the Agency) to manage all the operations of the sport facility. All these contracts were carried out to the satisfaction of the Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs (Service).
entries.637978e40a70facad3217dbb3bc3bb3acaa00cf5: On April 26, 2012, the sports facility called the TAZ, located at 8931 Papineau Avenue, became municipal equipment. Since this acquisition, OTC contracts have been awarded to the organization Le TAZ, a multidisciplinary and community centre also operating under Le TAZ (the Agency) to manage all of the operations of the sport facility, namely the management of programming and activities, the reception and safety of users, the supervision and routine and preventive maintenance of the building. Since the changes made to the management model in 2021 to clarify the responsibilities of the City and the obligations of the Organization while respecting the regulations in force, a specific agreement for the rental of the restaurant space of this sport facility must be concluded with the Agency.
entries.90ac68a48a5ca10309f99ab2df97d9929aa2cd2e: The organization Le TAZ, a multidisciplinary and community-based centre also operating under Le Taz (the Agency) is an organization whose mission is to promote the practice of inline skating, skateboarding, BMX cycling and scooter. It works on prevention and social integration of young people through the practice of action sports, as well as cultural and social activities associated with the lifestyle related to the practice of these sports. The organization offers in the municipal sports facility Le Taz, located at 8931 Papineau Avenue, a sports concentration project for high school students.
entries.0296b212ba38c7081a350ce437c76ce32698a99d: The Service de la culture, des sports et des loisirs (Service) is responsible for the health maintenance activities of the Stade de soccer de Montréal (Stade) since its opening in 2015. The current contract expires on December 31, 2026, a new agreement must be granted to provide the health maintenance services of the Stade. Without the necessary human resources, the Service wishes to award an over-the-counter contract to the current supplier, the organization Potential Placement inc..
entries.6f224f36af4952ec6a89aa3d63000b5e92e4cbbb: On April 26, 2012, the facility called Le TAZ became a municipal equipment. During this acquisition, contracts were awarded to the organization Le TAZ, a multidisciplinary and community centre to manage all operations of the facility including household maintenance. Due to legislative changes, responsibility for maintenance was removed from the facility management contract with the organization and will now be under the control of the City.
entries.daeea64976f2d6137863eb994e2f841bb2293e1b: On April 26, 2012, the facility called Le TAZ became a municipal equipment. At the time of this acquisition, a contract was awarded to Le TAZ to manage all the operations of the facility, namely the management of programming and activities, the reception and safety of users, the supervision and routine and preventive maintenance of the building. The business model of the TAZ was revised in 2021 to clarify the city's responsibilities and obligations while respecting the regulations in force.
entries.e04bce61e5d597017fd1bddc97988ac4d6859c21: Since 2008, the City of Montreal (City) has had an emphyteosis granted by the Société québécoise des infrastructures (SQI) covering a portion of Place des Festivals, located in Quartier des spectacles (QdS). This emphyteosis has allowed the City to develop and enhance the land forming an integral part of Place des Festivals. A proposed amendment to emphyteosis provides for an extension of its term for an additional ten (10) years, until January 31, 2038.
entries.316ba9b1f55a90e9f88a9208438420772ae20a33: Under the terms and conditions of the bilateral promise of sale between the City of Montreal (the City) and Société 9519-5228 Québec inc., as predecessor to Édifices Industriels Notre-Dame Ltée (the Seller), signed on July 31, 2025 (the Promise), the City committed itself to acquire vacant land corresponding to Lot 6,723,940 du cadastre du Québec, located at the intersection of Avenue Saint-Pierre and Rue Notre-Dame in the district of Lachine (the Building), for the purpose of redevelopment of Avenue Saint-Pierre. L'Immeuble is the subject of a lease signed on June 14, 1999 (le Bail) for the benefit of Groupe TDL Corporation which operates an establishment in the Tim Hortons food chain as a franchisee. According to the Promise, the Seller must be able to confirm to the City, upon signature of the deed of sale, the termination of the Lease affecting the land to be acquired by the City.
entries.51f0c90bbb7af47e7efeb7ef56c44b90d6a0974f: In 2023, the Supply Service launched a public tender No. 23-20176 for a service of domestic maintenance of the Biodôme and Planetarium. Household maintenance of the Biodôme and Planetarium is generally provided by a private company. The purpose of this dossier is to exercise the first year of option, from 1 February 2027 to 31 January 2028.
entries.54b8910d63a696f1b15806147172662511b7e8b6: In 2022, the Supply Service issued a public tender No. 22-19592 for a housekeeping service of common areas at the Marché Bonsecours, located at 350 rue Saint-Paul Est. The household maintenance of the Marché Bonsecours is generally provided by a private company. This file aims to exercise the second year of option, from February 1, 2027 to January 31, 2028.
entries.c2518812b201e9d5543ef42d5b5e89be68d7b4d4: The Road Infrastructure Service (SIRR) continues its mission to plan and carry out the necessary interventions to maintain and improve the level of service of the Montreal road network. These interventions are aimed at preserving the lifespan of municipal assets, improving the safety and comfort of users, as well as ensuring the smooth movement of people and goods. Investments in the rehabilitation of the arterial and local road network demonstrate the City of Montréal's commitment to maintaining safe, efficient and sustainable infrastructure.
entries.b2e8976df84b37bc58c05db297ee85b20b469e47: The Lachine-Est sector is part of the major strategic planning area Turcot–Lachine-Est designated by the Plan d'aménagement et de développement de l'agglomeration de Montréal and is a priority of the municipal government in urban planning. It corresponds to an industrial sector in decline of approximately 70 hectares, located on the edge of the Lachine Canal and near Old Lachine, which the City wishes to requalify for diversified activities (residential, employment, commercial, public space network, etc.). A specific urban development programme (PPU) was adopted in 2023 to mark the redevelopment of this sector.
entries.f4ba6f189946d3487e87ea4b2dbdf57e2b382c32: In its usual practices, the City of Montreal maintains an inventory of equipment for the traffic light system in order to meet the maintenance, modification and installation of new systems. To ensure optimal management of these requirements, it is necessary to conduct continuous acquisitions of equipment, thus allowing an inventory of essential equipment to be maintained and project schedules to be met. To this end, the Innovation and Travel Management Division of the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) regularly solicits the market by entering into framework agreements to ensure consistency and ease of supply while building profitable economic stocks.
entries.46cbc7b890d7ad9789e63597b705c3b9db9b9c59: The Innovation and Travel Management Division (DIGD) has chosen to establish a framework agreement in order to respond quickly and efficiently to the needs of traffic lights and adapt to their constant evolution. This approach aims to support the continuous upgrading of traffic light infrastructures to ensure the sustainability of the equipment, while maintaining high standards of safety, mobility and sustainable development. The framework agreement will run for up to thirty (30) months, from January 2027 to June 2029, or until the available credits are exhausted.
entries.8045295a8d01fdabe675ed005119fffd4f5b6988: The purpose of this file is to conclude a contract for the establishment of a Standards Access Portal (SOP), primarily designed to provide municipal engineering business units with centralized access to technical standards required for planning, design, maintenance and implementation of municipal engineering projects. This contract will be managed by the Supply Service but made available to all business units in the City of Montreal engaged in municipal engineering. In February 2026, the contract for the establishment of a Standards Access Portal (SOP) was awarded in accordance with bid solicitation documents submitted through written invitation 25-1745879 to the lowest compliant bidder, namely Nimonik Inc., for an estimated total amount of $114,975, including taxes.
entries.cc2d64919b1dc2a1bb0984d910340158ff083fdc: On September 24, 2026, the Regulations Prohibiting Inappropriate Behaviours against Members of the Staff of the City of Montreal (RCG 26-015) were adopted by the Conseil d'Agglomeration (1266750001). In essence, these proposed regulations prohibit anyone from intimidating, harassing, threatening, injuring or insulting a member of the staff of the City of Montréal acting in the course of their duties or from engaging in offensive, humiliating, abusive, violent or aggressive behaviour against them. The authority responsible for enforcing these regulations is defined in this regulation as "a police officer of the City of Montréal, with its personnel holding the title of Director or any other person entrusted with the administration of these regulations."
entries.0355497a0ebfbc7de62ea13aea714bd3d5051478: The Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM), in collaboration with the Service de la Stratégie immobilier et de l'habitation (SSIH), incorporated the right of preemption into its real estate strategy in 2018. In this context, the City Council adopted Regulation No. 18-066 concerning certain urban planning areas, including that of the Railway Edges, and made it subject to this right a hundred buildings. In order to continue implementing its real estate strategy and to ensure the necessary land control for the maintenance of certain municipal functions in this area, the City wishes to designate Lot 3,361,892 of the Québec cadastre as an immovable covered by the right of preemption.
entries.537758cd9243487e3ad8fa03a59948b97c9d292f: This file is a complementary step to Decision 1268172002 on the Saint-Jacques cliff ecoterritory, which will be submitted for approval to the Council of Agglomeration in November and the purpose of which is: "To adopt a regulation amending the schedule to the Order respecting the agglomeration of Montréal (1229-2005, December 8, 2005), by which the City removes from the list of equipment of collective interest, Lot 4 145 012 located in the ecoterritory of the Saint-Jacques cliff, in the arrondissement du Sud-Ouest".
entries.2af61f7a89325da635825f6ea996bb6b8b5670b5: In order to improve its efficiency and provide the best possible services to the population at the lowest cost, the City of Montreal consolidated the rolling stock function on January 1, 2017 (CM16 1267). Valid for a three-year period, the repatriation of competency was renewed for the first time in 2019 (CM18 1310), then in December 2021 for a one-year period (CM21 1388), in December 2022 for a 30-month period (CM22 1485), in June 2025 for a 12-month period (CM25 0795) and in June 2026 for a six-month period (CM26 0733). The activities that have been grouped under the direction of the Rolling Stock and Workshops Service (SMRA) are as follows: Acquisition, maintenance and management of the fleet of vehicles and rolling equipment; Management of all mechanical workshops in the territory; Training of operators and operators of vehicles and rolling equipment (since 2022, repatriated to the borough cooperation and civic experience service – CM22 1490); Fuel management.
entries.e8332a9b81001ff4aa0526249620266a5ec6dbaa: Jos-Montferrand Park is located in the borough of Ville-Marie, within the quadrilateral formed by Frontenac Street, Le Havre Street, Sainte-Catherine East and De Maisonneuve Boulevard East. The northern portion of the park is currently occupied by basketball courts, while the southern portion has been temporarily hosting a swimming pool for seasonal recreational activities since 2022. Considering the temporary nature of this facility and the borough's willingness to provide its citizens with quality facilities, a project to permanently refurbish the southern portion of the park is planned.
entries.5a2ab6a5bde4c8f318d7e95a00aa3a78a1eea61d: The financial reserve for municipal capital expenditures had a balance of $86 million as at December 31, 2025, including an amount of interest of $1.8 million. Budget 2026 authorized a new allocation to this reserve of $297.7 million for a total of $383.7 million. The purpose of this file is to make a partial cash payment for the year 2026 of $324.3 million.
entries.04d0b4c5d25392ad5e41582bd9fb7daee14911a9: The Saultsic-au-Récollet Community Garden is located in the Parc-nature de l'Île-de-la-Visitation, in the district of Ahuntsic-Cartierville. It is part of the services offered by the Municipal Community Gardens Program of the borough, which manages it since its inception. The site includes 64 individual gardens and two common plots for collective use.
entries.88aae0c6cda48e7173a651e017d01b54858cd6ec: By resolution CM22 0366, the City imposed the right of preemption for residential purposes, a series of buildings in Montreal territory. Since this imposition, certain buildings located in the borough of Ville-Marie and South-West have been subdivided into condominiums or developed by their owners without any transaction having been concluded. Accordingly, the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service recommends that notices of subjugation be cancelled.
entries.8b9d147b81b77c6810c07f17a0a808888cd72da8: In accordance with section 85.1 of the Charter of the City of Montreal (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), this file recommends acceptance of the service provided by the Technical Services and Logistics Support Division to the facilities in the Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve district. For several years, the Technical Services and Logistics Support Division has been providing services to the boroughs of the City of Montréal and Central Services, both in workshops and on the territory of its clients.
entries.26a8bcfccb0b11a6f2875a08283b1c894979e090: In the summer of 2025, steps were taken to sell to the not-for-profit organization Managing its Neighbourhood (GSQ), two buildings known and designated as Lots 1,380,819 and 4,141,147 du cadastre du Québec, located at 2661-2663 Centre Street, Montreal and 701 rue du Couvent, in the borough of Sud-Ouest (Buildings). On September 25, 2025, pursuant to resolutions CG25 0632 and CG25 0633, the City of Montréal undertook to sell to GSQ. Furthermore, GSQ intended to transfer the rights granted to it under the bilateral promise to a non-profit organization.
entries.1fe3851a8ce9dbbe58b3601d0ea269c9094fc4f3: The Sainte-Catherine Street East project includes extensive surface development and replacement of underground infrastructure in the Village area, between Berri Street in the West and De Lorimier Avenue in the East. The complete redevelopment of Sainte-Catherine Street East, between Berri Street and De Lorimier Avenue, aims to consolidate the role of this emblematic artery as a commercial, cultural and identity destination for the Village. Interventions will notably improve the comfort and experience of pedestrians and pedestrians, foster commercial and cultural dynamism and create a more inclusive, user-friendly and accessible public space for the population at large.
entries.8bce938695ff3c02c5a24a6d3f2356fa79c80a48: The Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS), through the Division of Innovation and Travel Management (DIGD), is responsible for planning, designing, integrating and evolving technological solutions supporting smart travel management, covering the entire life cycle of projects, from systems architecture to their implementation.The deployment of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) in Montréal is a continuation of investments made over more than a decade to modernize mobility infrastructure, improve the performance of the road network and support integrated travel management.
entries.a93815b4b0a32960e434c90a6674520ea02545dd: Regulation 8932 establishes a joint pension fund that allows several City of Montreal pension plans to pool some or all of their assets. The common fund allows participating pension plans to pool their assets in order to benefit from collective management of investments. Assets are administered by a Commission acting on behalf of the participating pension committees, which develops and implements investment strategies in accordance with applicable laws and policies.
entries.972d36a460f8fad3cb032181f028597e50081fb7: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshops Service (WMS) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. This requirement led to the launch of the public tender No. 26-21374. It was published in Le Devoir and in the Electronic Tendering System (EOTS) for thirty-three (33) days, from May 6, 2026 to June 9, 2026.
entries.02a0d947b836e7f46f6dee66b9dd05c10d0165aa: The purpose of this file is to conclude two framework agreements for the provision of personal protective equipment (PPE) on demand, primarily for the protection and safety of employees of the City of Montreal in the performance of their duties. These framework agreements will be made available to all business units of the City of Montréal. In February 2026, two contracts for the supply of personal protective equipment (PPE) were awarded, in accordance with public tender documents 25-21164, to the lowest compliant bidders, namely Canadian Bearings ltd and Acklands- Grainger Inc., for an estimated total amount of $964,946.32, taxes included as part of a new consolidation for these items.
entries.9284c645f4e42fe12c4fe087fbbb110cea13f0c0: The City of Montreal has a team of Organizational Development Advisors (DOs) within the Human Resources Service (HRS). However, this team's capacity does not meet all of the organization's needs. In 2023, HRS launched a public tender (23-20178) to enter into framework agreements for the provision of professional services in organizational development (DOs) upon request.
entries.9aea55cf9db3e7abe55f7e4b0ca4e838615bb71c: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services in a safe and environmentally responsible manner. The purpose of this file is to meet the City of Montreal's fleet's supply requirements for flexible HD rubber tracks as well as Prinoth-branded genuine vehicle parts (OEM). These assets are required to ensure the preventive and corrective maintenance of Prinoth-branded vehicles used in snow removal operations.
entries.e01bc86a382a606a8eb2649b558b2725a1403112: This file concerns an application for a financial contribution in the amount of $97,500 to the City submitted by the École des entrepreneurs du Québec (ÉEQ) for the project "29th edition of the Défi OSEntreprenir dans la région de Montréal". L
entries.8b832fa47addc9ac6bac6727bd22715adfad7122: To meet its climate, ecological transition and economic prosperity commitments, the City of Montreal has set itself the goal of doubling its circulatory index by 2030, from 3% to 6%, reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 55% and moving towards zero waste. To support this transition, in April 2025, it tabled Action Plan 2025-2027, which emerged from the Montreal Circular Economy Roadmap 2024-2030. Action 10 of this plan provides for the implementation of structural initiatives to stimulate ecosystems in the five priority sector value chains, including construction, renovation and demolition.
entries.4bb84a49dd1112f5b2b29cdaef27c366590ee1b6: The Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH) has been mandated by the Space for Life, Large Parks and Mount Royal Service (SEPVGPMR) to acquire from Mr. Ramzy El-Kassouf and Mr. Jason Serfaty (collectively Seller), a wooded land, located east of Phillips Avenue and the Grand Parc de l'Ouest (the Building), in the Village of Senneville (the Municipality), as shown on the plans attached to this file. The Building is situated in a permanent agricultural area governed by the Land Protection and Agricultural Activities Act (LPTAA). Any person wishing to dispose of any part of the lot, i.e. a subdivision of the lot, in a designated agricultural area, must obtain prior approval from the Commission de protection du territoire agricole (CPTAQ).
entries.8f6fac2d7faa8761058efdee968b735cf9302a35: The Information Technology Service (IT Service) is a key player in the digital modernization of the City of Montreal. By positioning technology as a strategic lever, it designs and deploys solutions tailored to internal needs to improve the performance and quality of services for citizens and municipal staff. Its role is to align technological initiatives with the City's objectives by promoting accessibility, efficiency and service quality.
entries.1804807841d265eae7403156090b9eb65705d1a0: In 2022, the Supply Service issued Public Bid No. 22-19608 for a service of inspection and maintenance of portable fire extinguishers, fire hoses, emergency lighting and exit signs for various buildings in the City. This type of service is normally carried out by a private company for these buildings. The purpose of this file is to exercise the second year of option for lots 1 and 2, from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2027.
entries.c29f4e96914f9b7803d1abb69ac2f2fd73b95353: In 2025 and 2026, the City carried out construction work on Boulevard Henri-Bourassa Est in order to develop a fast bus service and cycle paths between Rue Lajeunesse and Avenue des Recollets, which are part of the Henri-Bourassa Sustainable Mobility Corridor (CMD) project. As part of this project, the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) wished to remove certain bus stops and the addition of bicycle lanes necessitated moving others. As a result, trips, additions and removals of shelters are required, as well as the connection of some of them.
entries.f23901d4cceec734585510760f961126a14213d7: Due to the number and scope of real estate transaction projects (purchase, sale, exchange), construction or renovation of buildings (neighborhood post, fire stations, libraries, etc.), the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH) and the Property Management and Planning Service (SMPI) are required to use specialized firms to carry out environmental characterization and geotechnical studies mandates, which must be carried out upstream in order for ISS and SGPI to have the data necessary for decision-making in relation to transactions and project planning.
entries.f8d40fa9d61949a8b234cec994dc432426f66190: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. To ensure the production of drinking water, the Drinking Water Directorate (DEP) of the Water Service operates six (6) potable water production plants and 24 pumping tanks/stations that produce and distribute drinking water to the Montreal community. Atwater Drinking Water Production Plant provides nearly 40% of total drinking water production while providing the water needed for fire protection in the areas it serves.
entries.2bed8467463294171823dd84157838b8f20e4d8d: The Urban Planning and Mobility Service ("SUM") mandated the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service ("SSIH") to undertake the acquisition of a land owned by Hydro-Québec as part of the construction of the Réseau express métropolitain (the "REM"). The Acquisition is necessary for the development of a new north-south access road incorporating active transportation, between Highway 40 service track and Brunswick Boulevard, in order to adequately serve the future Fairview-Pointe-Claire station with respect to transportation. The development as a traffic lane of the vacant land covered by this acquisition, located near the Pointe-Claire pumping station, constitutes a portion of the extension of Jacques-Bizard Boulevard, which is identified in the Plan d'aménagement et de développement de l'agglomeration de Montréal (2015).
entries.339e6bf17879861e91b6e3b4141b2288757ca9cf: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment, today and for future generations. Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant treats all of Montreal Island's sanitary wastewater as well as some of the stormwater from unit systems. To improve the quality of discharged water and reduce microbiological contamination of the St. Lawrence River, an ozone disinfection process will be added at the end of the existing treatment chain.
entries.b2aec3b0e3e7879637362e2149191d90f1636b9f: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment, today and for future generations. Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant treats all of Montreal Island's sanitary waste water as well as some of the rainwater from unit systems. To improve the quality of discharged water and reduce microbiological contamination of the St. Lawrence River, an ozone disinfection process will be added at the end of the existing treatment chain.
entries.32edef900c464cb0c04dfedf7460f37b0bcd4411: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water to the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. The Ville de Montréal's Drinking Water Directorate (DEP) operates six (6) potable water production plants that produce and distribute drinking water to all Montrealers. Four (4) of these plants use a coagulant, aluminum sulphate, in a phase of the production process to treat water prior to its distribution to citizens.
entries.a98a6e7b7f2afeeec7347c36f26b06704699a4e1: In 2022, LOBNL Habitation 1370 was formed as an organization related to the Société d'amélioration de Pointe-Saint-Charles (SOCAM), whose mission is to acquire and renovate buildings to provide quality housing for low- and middle-income households. Habitation 1370 carries out community housing projects in collaboration with Groupe Bâtir son quartier, a group of technical resources that contributed to the implementation of nearly 480 projects representing approximately 16,000 dwellings.
entries.7b7a8c5a342bd64a8a56f7694f32e8ae9ae7850b: To support these operations, the Service must maintain a continuous supply of batteries to meet the maintenance and replacement needs of its fleet of vehicles and motorized equipment. Batteries covered by this approach are stored in inventory at SMRA workshops in order to support maintenance operations and reduce immobilization periods for vehicles and equipment.
entries.8b408105a53c0484f6d180739861a36763c40aaf: The Department of Culture, Sports and Recreation wishes to respond to the issues and needs specific to the cultural leisure and amateur arts sector (CACPA), which have been widely documented in recent years. These findings demonstrate that this sector is underfunded and lacks resources. New funding was made available in 2026 to provide support to certain organizations for projects that meet the following objectives: To support the vitality of the ACPAA ecosystem, local communities and neighbourhood life; To support structural initiatives responding to issues identified by the ACPAA community (accompaniment, mobilization, consultation, sharing of good practices, etc.); To increase the capacity of organizations to generate positive impacts through their actions; To strengthen the alignment between supported projects and the needs of the environment.
entries.399f06a771377f4fdcc4eb836a1f77a509a6c825: All materials quality control services must be provided by the Expertise and Technical Support Division (DEST) for all civil engineering projects (construction, rehabilitation, repair) of the Urban Infrastructure Projects Implementation Directorate (DRPIU), as well as other departments and districts of the City of Montreal. These qualitative control services are entirely provided by consultants. In order to meet the needs of construction sites, during the short period of construction in which these services are required at the same time on all construction sites, the tendering and mandate-giving process cannot be completed for each project within the short timeframes imposed, and therefore DET must use private firms through framework agreements to respond promptly and adequately to the request of its applicants.
entries.0255de3dd8e6f1355de99def9b06c6e19f49aa5b: Created by the City of Montreal in 2015, the MTL SME network is the main municipal lever for supporting and financing private and collective enterprises established on the territory of the agglomeration. Through its six service hubs, the network provides specialized support to entrepreneurs at all stages of their development and contributes to the realization of the city's priorities in terms of economic development, innovation, social economy and territorial development. In December 2023, the city council authorized the granting of a financial contribution to the six organizations of the MTL SME network for the period from 2024 to 2026 in order to consolidate the offer of accompanying services dedicated to Montréal entrepreneurs.
entries.a5aea2deab55f0ebf3ef7453240923d129659146: The mission of the City of Montreal's Water Service is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater, to ensure public health and safety, and protect the environment today and for future generations. To ensure the production of drinking water, the Drinking Water Directorate (DEP) of the Water Service operates six (6) potable water production plants and 24 pumping tanks/stations that produce and distribute drinking water to the Montreal community. The DEP continues its activities to modernize, rehabilitate and upgrade drinking water production and distribution infrastructure.
entries.a27f937598a239c50ff244fd57bf2d7cf20555a4: The contract awarded to the firm 9248-5523 Québec inc. (DXP Postexperts) for the provision of printing, insertion, shipping, stationery supplies and envelopes for the Human Resources Service will expire on December 31, 2026. This contract covering services during the period 2024-2026 provides for the possibility of extending the agreement for an additional two years. The volume of shipments made by the Human Resources Service is constantly decreasing in connection with the arrival of the new Simon+ HR solution.
entries.5435c8b75864cb15f8a87b99346a439a336b44b8: In 2018, the City of Montreal awarded a contract for professional services to Desjardins Insurance for the administration of the collective insurance plans offered to elected and elected municipal officials, employees, retirees and retirees of the City of Montréal with the exception of guarantees in case of accidental death and mutilation for a maximum period of nine and a half years (9.5), from July 1, 2019 to December 31, 2028. Subject to provisions allowing the City to terminate the contract in the event of default by the successful tenderer, the contract is initially five and a half years, ending on December 31, 2024, plus four years of options divided into two blocks of two years, that is, from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2028. The original contract provides that in order to exercise the contract renewal clause, the City of Montreal must make known its intention in writing to Desjardins Assurances and obtain the latter's consent.
entries.861a51fdd09537a3cac39adb9178d9f802f11e1e: The City must use a third party to obtain specialized services to provide the employer's representatives with ongoing professional support in terms of collective insurance. Whether it is the actuarial services normally required for the management of collective insurance contracts, when determining the value of the actuarial obligation as well as cost accounting elements according to CPA Canada public sector standards, regarding future benefits other than those arising from pension plans, during negotiations or, in litigation. Since the contract in force with Normandin Beaudry, Actuaires consultant inc. ends on December 31, 2026, the City requested the contract from July 6 to August 13, 2026 to obtain the provision of consulting services effective January 1, 2027.
entries.ec9d84554e4fd0e9a1a14cc5fe9eda8757c5dc7e: The City of Montreal's Water Service (WS) is responsible for providing drinking water to the Montréal community, managing stormwater and cleaning wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protecting the environment today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate (WSD) is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater, carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance. In this context, WSD plans to carry out construction work during the years 2027-2028 on a 900 mm diameter main water line under Victoria, Sainte-Claire, Waverley and Lakeview Avenues, to Saint-Jean Boulevard, on the Ville de Pointe-Claire territory.
entries.e9c06d1e3817521858409979842f6016334a13f8: The Regulations Prohibiting Inappropriate Behaviours Against Members of the Personnel of the City of Montreal (RCG 26-015) were passed on September 24, 2026 by the Council of Agglomeration (1266750001). In essence, these Regulations prohibit anyone from intimidating, harassing, threatening, injuring or insulting a member of the staff of the City of Montréal acting in the course of their duties or from engaging in offensive, humiliating, abusive, violent or aggressive behaviour against them. The authority responsible for enforcing these Regulations is defined in the regulations as "a member of the Police Service of the City of Montreal, the personnel of the City of Montréal having the title of Director or any other person responsible for administering these Regulations."
entries.2907783a4231254ed8098922d5023f1fd93f87c1: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. Under the Montreal Reflex Framework Agreement, the Department of Municipal Affairs and Habitation (MAMH) provided financial assistance to the City of Montreal in fiscal year 2019-2020 to support green infrastructure investments related to water management. The funding from this grant is currently being held in the cash payment reserve to finance capital expenditures under agglomeration jurisdiction.
entries.60c4432d585731801baca5a6897b3a9d0d5b6306: The increased access of young people to the Internet and social networks exposes them to serious dangers such as lure, extortion, sharing intimate images and online sexual exploitation. Faced with a rapid increase in these crimes, police forces must act quickly. To strengthen the fight, an integrated coordination team to combat the sexual exploitation of children on the Internet (ESEI) has been set up to coordinate the efforts of different police services and better identify sexual predators on the Internet.
entries.d00151e6d082b37769ad3a7bb5f6124b83d98920: Frédéric-Back Park, located in the Saint-Michel district of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension district, is the most ambitious urban environmental rehabilitation project to date in Quebec. From quarry to landfill site to metropolitan park, the rehabilitation of this site offers recreational, sporting and cultural activities to the population. With a total area of 153 hectares, this metropolitan park identified with the Green and Blue Trame of the Plan d'aménagement et de développement de l'agglomeration de Montréal, is still under development.
entries.bf6c0f2faf4c232c656cb34fc7ed9a28198f7fd3: Confronted with the effects of climate change, the City of Montreal is intensifying its efforts to provide resilient and sustainable natural environments to the population. Among the tools put in place to protect natural environments and reach the target of 10% of protected land as indicated in the Montréal agglomeration's planning and development plan, the City is acquiring ecologically relevant land to increase the area of protected natural environments, sustain ecosystems and provide new places of contact with nature for the population.
entries.0b08f207255cad2a0827915b72e50b4a748fee26: Confronted with the effects of climate change, the City of Montreal is stepping up its efforts to provide resilient and sustainable natural environments to the population. Among the tools put in place to protect natural environments and reach the target of 10% of protected land as indicated in the planning and development plan for Montréal's agglomeration, the City is taking steps to acquire ecologically relevant land. These transactions increase the area of protected natural habitats, sustain ecosystems and provide new places of contact with nature for the population.
entries.9740007f0e8ac8e8276eab84f5e877afe9bf3a4e: The financial reserve for capital expenditures related to agglomeration skills as at December 31, 2025 had a balance of $246.5 million, including an interest amount of $7 million and $150 million from a green infrastructure (Water) grant. Budget 2026 authorized a new allocation to this reserve in the order of $175.9 million for a total of $422.4 million. The purpose of this file is to make a partial cash payment for $2026 of $245.5 million.
entries.2ceea9678eb158b35eebcfc2fbbdb801bb6497c4: By resolution EC 25 1959, the Executive Committee of the City of Montreal exercised its right of preemption to acquire the building located at 1085-1095 Avenue Hôtel-de-Ville for social housing purposes. Following the acquisition of possession of this building, its management was entrusted to the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM). The terms and conditions under which the SHDM took over residential buildings acquired by the City were first established in a management agreement concluded between the parties (CG23 0084).
entries.0452666db96cbe69a72bd0f1877f56bcf7ee093a: By resolution CG20 0141, the City imposed a right of preemption for social housing purposes, a series of buildings on Montreal territory. Since this imposition, certain buildings located in the borough of Ville-Marie, Villeray - Saint-Michel – Parc-Extension and the South-West have been subdivided into condominiums or developed by their owners without any transaction being concluded. Accordingly, the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service recommends that notices of subjugation be cancelled.
entries.1d4d87478ca4a79fcc68e597789418ba80d98db8: An application for the construction of a five-storey residential building has been filed. The site, with an area of approximately 573 m2, is located on Lot 2,243,374. The nature of the project, which aims to allow the construction of a building for accommodation for persons in need of assistance and assistance, makes it eligible for assessment and authorization under section 89, paragraph 4, of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (C-11-4), by the agglomeration council of Montréal.
entries.a002b82c282b0a1933661620ac67fbdfa71b7191: Through its mission, the Water Systems Directorate (WED) of the Water Service is responsible for the transportation of drinking water throughout the Montréal agglomeration. To do so, it must intervene on the main water system in order to increase its reliability, ensure adequate renewal of assets, reduce the number of breaks and losses in drinking water and improve the structural state of the network. It is therefore necessary to construct new pipes connected with hydraulic needs and replace or rehabilitate existing pipes.
entries.ed3f22875482c05f79db01dd8fea162eb2019905: On March 25, 2026, the Government of Quebec passed Order No. 510-2026, under which the Société d'habitation du Québec (hereinafter "the SHQ") was authorized to grant a grant of $25,997,294 and an interest-free loan of $13,763,051 to the Immobilier collectif – Point commun (hereinafter "the Agency") to carry out the Triangle Nord project, which provides for the operation of 395 affordable and affordable intermediate housing units in the borough of the Southwest (hereinafter "the Project"). The terms and conditions for granting this financial assistance were established in an Agreement between the SHQ and the Organization on Implementation, Operation and Financing signed on March 26, 2026, pursuant to Order No. 510-2026 (hereinafter "the Agreement"). The Organization is seeking the City of Montreal for a financial contribution of $13,151,528 under the Project.
entries.ea125701840be46b4c346ba14fae33aebafc248e: As part of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Implementation Plan (GEP), the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the City of Montreal (Ville) signed a grant agreement on March 28, 2022 (Agreement) to enable the latter to carry out certain measures in its Climate Plan 2020 - 2030 (Climate Plan) responding to the MOP. The Agreement contributes in particular to supporting the financing of decarbonation projects for 32 buildings identified by the Building Management and Planning Service (SMPI) as one of the largest emitters of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in municipal real estate (Parc), whose long-term objective is to reduce its emissions by approximately 7,000 tonnes CO2 eq., or about 25% of the GHG emissions from that park. The 25th Barrack Decarbon Project is part of Action 30 of the Climate Plan to transform 100% of the Park into operational zero carbon park by 2030.

entries.1f771b657fc7b5ab6a8877dc35fabc989cfae412: Councillor Richard Deschamps, as chair of this commission, tabled the report of the Commission on Finance and Administration entitled "Study of the Annual Report of the Auditor General of the City of Montreal for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 - Report and Recommendations", and the Board took note of it.
entries.3da0d9ab82b94cbe6bb13a799aedddab86e6164b: 1 - expresses its full support for the victims, families and relatives of civilians and police officers who have been killed or injured in mass shootings, and offers condolences to those affected by mourning;
entries.3111bf939586af16fe0d070f25b1577a0c4fd4f5: 2 - joins the groups of victims and survivors of mass shooting to affirm that weapons designed for war do not belong in the hands of civilians, and that the government must take concrete steps in order to give priority to public security;
entries.7da8245ae4942448fd8b4f696a4f04c63709629d: 3 - Urges the Government of Canada to deliver on its electoral promises to complete the ban on assault-type weapons, remove them from civilian traffic and limit access to high capacity shippers as soon as possible.
entries.90a610cdfae2012eebfc6601c0d7c267b5628998: Whereas RCMP data show that most of the weapons used to commit crimes, including mass shootings, are shoulder weapons and not illegal handguns;
entries.38b94c9945b08809c35aa1fbba4767f2146ad73c: Whereas one or more assault-type weapons were involved in mass femicide at Polytechnique, as well as during mass shootings at Dawson College and the Québec mosque;
entries.e629d739205a26a03f1fd1a49586e461cf40dbbf: Whereas the majority of police officers killed in the course of their duties in Canada were using long, typically high-power weapons, as was the case at Côte-des-Neiges in June 2026, and in several other Canadian cities where tragedies occurred in which police officers were shot;
entries.ec847b1a259cb45c699356d27fe521465d78e7a3: Whereas, despite the insistent demands of various groups of victims or survivors of mass shooting, including PolySeSuivre and Dawson Families for arms control, it is still lawful to purchase and possess military-type assault weapons in Canada with a Canadian Possession and Acquisition Licence (CPP);
entries.7b6300af89471c9f449a91557419c947c4d6eb43: Whereas it is the responsibility of governments to adopt laws that help protect the civilian population as well as members of the police forces across the country, who accept daily exposure to danger in order to ensure the safety and well-being of citizens;
entries.43122ad007c0a5ad560c8c864c7b4efc4850cb52: Whereas after the 2020 mass shooting in Nova Scotia, Ottawa banned 1,500 models of military-type weapons and added additional models to the list of prohibited weapons in 2024 and 2025, but did not prohibit SKS, a Soviet-designed military weapon that has been the most widely used in mass shootings and killings of police and police officers in recent years across the country;
entries.089bdffa14232c980805dd256cd433e816666d1f: Whereas, in 2022, the Canadian government tried, in vain, to ban SKS through amendment G-46 to former Bill C-21;
entries.f165246073d61b1ccb596dbcca3b4c0f85e95501: Whereas New Zealand purchased and removed assault weapons from civilian traffic less than six months after the Christchurch killing, and Australia did so in the year following the Port Arthur killing, while it was more than six years ago that the process began in Canada.
entries.3adb99a70aad1fb4de75ceee4e08dd62f2d25497: The Chair of Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.6e4bec3e27d2f90b46419180105503bc590a870f: From the outset, the Mayor of Montreal commemorates the 20th anniversary of Dawson College's shooting and pays tribute to Anastasia De Sousa, who died during this tragedy. In particular, she recalls that this event deeply affected the Montreal community and fostered a lasting reflection on the place of firearms in society. Also referring to the recent shooting at Côte-des-Neiges, which claimed the lives of Agent Mohamed Lamine Benredouane and Michel Mizrahi, Ms. Martinez Ferrada stressed the need to strengthen measures to prevent armed violence. In this regard, she called on the federal government to complete the ban on assault weapons, withdraw those already in circulation and further restrict access to high-capacity shippers.
entries.591dddc0a131a0f9a834cfb7d69059a11425e05b: In conclusion, the Mayor of Montreal highlights the commitment of PolySeSuivre and the Dawson Families to arms control, whose efforts help advance the debate on firearms control.
entries.b5d66fe68abe2809503ba80670bee17a974ff24a: The Chair gave the floor to Councillors Stephanie Valenzuela, Émilie Brière and Carla Beauvais, respectively.
entries.4f7fe73c0c88422fbee40e97377f5c2f20b4caeb: Speaking in turn, Stephanie Valenzuela mentioned that the tragedies of Polytechnique and Dawson College illustrate the devastating consequences of armed violence. Convinced that assault-type weapons do not belong in society, and like the Mayor of Montreal, she asked the Government of Canada to strengthen firearms supervision and reiterated her support for organizations calling for a ban.
entries.770396c828286b28fe6bd2df6678460081f2d28f: As for Counsellor Émilie Brière, she greeted the people present and said that, as a member of the Polytechnique community, she remained particularly sensitive to this issue. According to her, the impact of these tragedies had been magnified by the weapons used and, although control of firearms was not within municipal jurisdiction, local authorities were responsible for relaying the concerns of the population.
entries.8558897c84ab8c2bc89c4c2cb8bdfa57fadb9c4e: Finally, Carla Beauvais argues, among other things, that a weapon designed for war has no place on the streets.Responding to PolySeRevenient's claims, she argues that there is a need to establish a clear timetable for the withdrawal of SKS-type weapons and to provide the resources required to implement this measure.
entries.633574c13d240c95d8cf0c4aea9b7ca0051245d3: The Chair thanked Board members for their interventions.
entries.464aab3043ba350b86a6d0a1a94d61ffc3a28c80: 1- that the City of Montreal observe National Day of Truth and Reconciliation on September 30 each year in tribute to residential school survivors, missing children and affected families and communities;
entries.928abd052116eee83d933354622e1cd3943e42da: 2- that the memory of residential schools, the recognition of the past, present and future Aboriginal presence in the Greater Montreal area and the transformation of municipal practices through concrete gestures of reconciliation are at the heart of the City's action as a metropolis of reconciliation;
entries.38a661fd5393e457d08c49b80858c5848cd45255: 3- the City of Montreal reaffirms its commitment to combat, in collaboration with indigenous nations and communities, all forms of racism and systemic discrimination faced by Aboriginal Montrealers while promoting their development in all spheres of society;
entries.c3e185af3572e439eb3fa45e51c38558723e5274: 4- that the City of Montreal continue its efforts towards reconciliation with indigenous peoples through its public policies and action plans, as well as through its initiatives in economic development, urban planning, housing and social and cultural fields;
entries.c2d493f42eec1abf8b3000db01628b935a81a37a: 5- that the City Council invites Montrealers to join Aboriginal communities in celebrating the richness of their culture by participating in activities organized as part of National Truth and Reconciliation Day.
entries.ac6ffb3ddeef34943fa74ba2fec0edd8e8c4d9c9: Whereas the City of Montreal recognizes itself in a thousand-year indigenous territory, a place of meeting and diplomacy among peoples as well as the Treaty of Great Peace, and thanks the Kanien'kehà:ka nation for its hospitality in unceded territory;
entries.197d3b7f576a40d2698fc463a74efb3627b4253f: Whereas National Truth and Reconciliation Day is observed on September 30 of each year in Canada, and is intended to pay tribute to residential school survivors, missing children, families and communities affected;
entries.7abd783264ed12aad39628a6a13471d591d7509f: Whereas a formal public commemoration of the tragic and painful history of residential schools remains an essential component of the reconciliation process;
entries.c4d23cd894a27c0c458aadfaeb3ff17faee0391a: Whereas more than 150,000 Aboriginal children were sent to the approximately 130 residential schools that operated in Canada between 1831 and 1996, of which more than 4000 never returned;
entries.0d3b12a6023bb2668d28df46931dba132eb65eb3: Whereas the National Day of Truth and Reconciliation has been held every 30 September since 2021, and is one of the calls for action by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission;
entries.b4d68f7321e5b7fb2fe4b7e9609b46e4d4e4494c: Whereas the date of September 30, aligning with Orange Sweater Day - each child counts, is an opportunity for people from across the country to reflect and participate in educational and commemorative activities to learn more about the richness of First Nations, Inuit and Métis cultural heritages and stories;
entries.e0867e7cac411632543cf177d5d282f781438a41: Whereas the various indigenous nations and communities contribute to the development and influence of the City of Montreal in all spheres of society and that the reconciliation process places at the heart of its priorities the promotion and respect of their history, languages, knowledge, traditions and cultures;
entries.a4bebd6d402875df2011e07dd287fd544472e7f3: Whereas the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples adopted by the General Assembly of the United Nations on 13 September 2007 was unanimously endorsed by the City of Montreal on 21 August 2017;
entries.fc8cbd551fbe4b6e37e51eabb35d355619b87ff5: Whereas several actions put forward by the municipal administration demonstrate its commitment to reconciliation with Aboriginal peoples, including the creation of a position of Commissioner for Relations with Indigenous Peoples, the integration of white pine in the town's coat of arms and flag, as well as the translation of the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities into Kanien'kéha;
entries.c0cbca17116b33bbcccab062a9a638c2ca6c1953: Whereas the first Strategy for Reconciliation with the Aboriginal Peoples of the City of Montreal was published in 2020, and whereas the second draft, currently in preparation with the collaboration of Aboriginal partners, aims to better meet the realities, expectations and priorities of the day, as expressed by Montréal's indigenous communities;
entries.9850d44c806f60cec0f4c995974db908eab08772: Whereas these strategies are being developed with Aboriginal communities to guide the decisions of the Authority and to evolve relations between the City and Aboriginal communities and governments in a spirit of respect, justice and humanity.
entries.54cb02186fa25d3965b865055211df937a25e0aa: The chair of the council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Josué Corvil for the presentation of the Declaration and then to the head of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus.
entries.612f8a17ee69a51e8d29613e02ea1039b7e3491a: From the outset, Councillor Josué Corvil announced that National Truth and Reconciliation Day is a time to remember, listen and reflect on our collective responsibility. He affirmed that truth was a first step towards reconciliation and stressed the importance of listening to survivors, learning more about the history of indigenous peoples, respecting their rights and valuing their languages and cultures.
entries.420514ad379e769ac2c8705ed951f3a8f33a8dae: In this regard, Mr. Corvil adds that reconciliation must continue on a daily basis and be translated into concrete actions and, as such, he recalls several actions taken by the City of Montreal since 2017, including the addition of white pine to the Town's flag, the inauguration of Tiohtià:ke Otsira-Kéhne Park, the adoption of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and the launch in 2026 of a first call for projects for indigenous organizations. In conclusion, he recognizes the 325th anniversary of the Great Peace of Montreal and affirms that reconciliation is a shared responsibility that begins with truth, continues with respect and takes shape through action.
entries.b4a41b3ca0b58027f5b7c4ed50804b5f6245a88d: In turn, the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, joins her voice with that of her colleague in support of the Declaration and invites the public to meet with First Nations communities, offering, among other things, a visit to exhibitions and cultural venues to gain a better understanding of their history and reality. She also invites the population to wear the orange colour on September 30 and stresses the importance of remembering, establishing links with Aboriginal communities and showing openness and curiosity about them.
entries.0c91e92d9d831c161d4c9dd9cece77e0954c5b24: 1- that the City of Montreal, on September 15, celebrates International Day of Democracy and reaffirms the importance of democratic values, citizen participation and respect for fundamental freedoms for the development of just and inclusive societies;
entries.9088783edf9c92ec942a600a91810e6f54e60871: 2- the City of Montreal stresses the importance of various bodies and mechanisms for citizen participation that allow Montrealers to make their voices heard in the development of projects that transform their living environments;
entries.391d1bccb3f4d050f57ffcbff1fd3bce1b1b2f9d: 3- that the City of Montreal continue its efforts to ensure open and transparent access to municipal public data in order to foster citizen participation, innovation and trust in institutions;
entries.b62732b8c585db0f72afbac51b68062dac0d7619: Whereas the International Day of Democracy was proclaimed by the General Assembly of the United Nations on 15 September 2007 in a resolution to encourage Governments to strengthen and consolidate democracy;
entries.f8e212bbfd213d70cea6c0836c7849becf7d2e11: Whereas this day is part of the follow-up to the Universal Declaration on Democracy adopted by the Inter-Parliamentary Union in 1997, which highlights the fundamental principles of democratic rule;
entries.08767f83129cf8e1a71bdfdaaa873b7606c4acf3: Whereas the objective of the International Day of Democracy is, inter alia, to recall that democracy is a process that is evolving and requires permanent commitment from States, institutions and citizens to ensure its proper functioning;
entries.43413e5fee8afa1192709cc48abf44dc771c88fa: Whereas this day also provides an opportunity to reflect on the threats facing democratic systems, including disinformation, polarisation and erosion of public confidence in democratic institutions;
entries.bfc8ad29a9022953da7602a47c690ac4c8c3c991: Whereas freedom of expression is a fundamental human right enshrined in article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights;
entries.dd942e82bee311f834577b791084f3fb1a252a36: Whereas democracy is based on the active, informed and inclusive participation of citizens in public life and that local governments play an essential role in strengthening public confidence in democratic institutions;
entries.0b0d0cc1ca85db69a27c54ffc31e4e94e3bbe615: Whereas the City of Montréal encourages Montrealers to make their voices heard, both in electoral processes and at local democratic bodies, such as city council and borough councils meetings, commissions and public consultations, as well as citizen forums;
entries.0e9b861b454f41c0c0af9cbaa6e52153bcacb656: Whereas the City of Montreal promotes democratic vitality in its territory by supporting citizen participation, including through initiatives such as Realize Montréal, which allows residents to contribute directly to the selection of collective projects in boroughs;
entries.d0968293688eb113bfd3006f71465f804f2add22: Whereas, as part of its Open Data Policy, the City of Montreal contributes to strengthening democracy by promoting transparent and free access to municipal data, thereby enabling the public to better understand and participate in public action.
entries.14da83b79e92a095ff7d1fa6af0785777beb634e: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Maude Théroux-Séguin for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.d51cf8f2d78ec5c10f2e47eb98469184f81c2359: From the outset, Councillor Maude Théroux-Séguin points out that the International Day of Democracy, celebrated on 15 September, proclaimed by the UN in 2007, is based on the constant commitment of institutions, governments and citizens who make it live on a daily basis. She states, among other things, that at this time marked by false information, social divisions and declining confidence in institutions, the important thing is to reaffirm our commitment to democratic values that are embodied in dialogue and citizen participation.
entries.b9a13a020c6297c6ad40fa193a24e0bb7c1a3e96: In addition, Ms. Théroux-Séguin mentioned that the City fosters citizen participation and transparency by increasing opportunities for people to express themselves and facilitating access to municipal information. She also believes that freedom of expression and public listening are essential foundations of democracy, as they promote dialogue, public debate and civic engagement. Finally, she invites people to exercise their right to vote in the run-up to the next provincial elections.
entries.d6b70ad719ed39b53ea31d3b9b0b4e448ed3ee6a: The Chair thanked Councillor Maude Théroux-Séguin for her intervention.

entries.c5e2c6c1e56db07198bc5607f268dac342e410c4: 1 - the city council on 15 September as International Day of Democracy;
entries.add5e05a732a7d1037134ab4c59460c6722d306d: 2 - that the municipal council reaffirm the importance of local democracy, transparency, access to information and citizen engagement in Montreal's development;
entries.870dd9b05d0c32635542b1960efdf5a814cf87bd: 3 - that the municipal council recognize the contribution of citizens, community organizations, public institutions and community partners who actively participate in Montreal's democratic life;
entries.a7e20d411d2cb79352b97d619336abedf1a65320: 4 - the municipal council stresses the importance of citizen participation mechanisms that enable people to contribute to the development of municipal projects, policies and priorities;
entries.1d9d2f77f9fb58c4e837266ebd2fd97f342d9466: 5 - that the City of Montreal undertake to retain all measures facilitating citizen participation, public consultation and accountability of persons elected to residents. In particular, by not reducing periods of citizens' questions;
entries.2f4c9861e19e360e9468dc343fdd73821db9eda3: 6 - that the municipal council undertake to make a full assessment of the democratic losses caused by the dissolution of Concertation Montréal and propose concrete compensatory measures to compensate for the losses measured and observed by the said valuation;
entries.8001786644f8619aae2f6cae2809b1b1f7651daa: 7 - that the City Council undertake to invest the necessary funds to carry out all projects selected in the Participative Budget of the City of Montreal;
entries.0b50fcc06c3814ddc6a04ca86b016c1254a77b5b: 8 - the municipal council undertakes to re-establish the Participative Budget as soon as possible or to introduce a citizen participation tool with an ambition and equivalent scope in order to deepen quality and expand democratic tools available to residents;
entries.8fd5eb46a19167fad5d55c3478e3779ef29db42a: 9 - that the municipal council reaffirm the importance of periods of accessible, inclusive and sufficiently long citizens' questions, both on-line and on-line, in order to foster direct dialogue between the population and its democratic institutions;
entries.ac47b43d9d024ac570c6bfd4fae98f0ff3603b92: 10 - that the municipal council should recall that the ability to ask questions to elected persons and municipal governments, as well as to obtain clear and timely answers, is a fundamental element of democratic participation;
entries.3921bb1be405e32f5f29865c0fe5f7ec675b6d17: 11 - that the municipal council reaffirm the importance of ensuring adequate public access to the City's consultations, commissions and other participatory bodies, in particular by providing for reception capacity and dissemination arrangements enabling as many citizens as possible to monitor and participate in the work;
entries.9e6f1be9502ae87a6afd404eca71cb55cac26ffd: 12 - the city council should continue and strengthen efforts to make municipal information more accessible, transparent and understandable to the general public, including by preserving mechanisms of public participation that allow citizens to ask questions and obtain answers in public sessions;
entries.ad470c212b7552a790da67f1b9985edcff5bd144: 13 - that the Office of the President undertake to make public as soon as possible, all evaluations, reflections, studies, internal and external communications as well as supporting documents which led to the implementation of the pilot project for the Citizens' Question Period at the City Council on 24 and 25 August 2026;
entries.f6cbe7aa4b93a542718f63c7fa1362a7e192c6b2: 14 - that the City Council reiterate the City of Montreal's commitment to democratic principles, citizen participation and open governance.
entries.ce24a59c49f81d8754e606671761bb2c4cdfab01: Whereas in 2007 the United Nations proclaimed 15 September "International Day of Democracy" to promote democratic principles worldwide;
entries.0efead97765ecbcd9263935af06eda19b880f93d: Whereas this day is an opportunity to recall that democracy is based on the active engagement of citizens and on institutions accessible, transparent and responsive to their communities;
entries.85c6fd50c4693aef8ae79a2c65e8145504048738: Whereas Montreal is distinguished by the diversity of its population and by the richness of its community, institutional, cultural and associative fabric, which actively contribute to the democratic vitality of the metropolis;
entries.60876516791ed9e50b5cea3e430b60eb2b910c7f: Whereas the City of Montreal has 103 elected members of the city council, the agglomeration council and its 19 boroughs, and that these local elected representatives play an essential role in local democratic life;
entries.d578b1a05736f495b92c41065797db437722fe79: Whereas one of the pillars of citizen participation in a democratic society is access to clear, accessible and high-quality information; whereas this includes timely public notice, accessible decision-making bodies, adequate periods of citizen issues and rigorous and independent public consultations;
entries.d246ef64e470269da3d91ff648cb20e6570f4108: Whereas Question periods at public meetings of municipal and borough councils are one of the main mechanisms for citizens to directly question their elected persons and the municipal administration;
entries.0159e94c718cf2da0ce915bf4bc5fc2dfe781e18: Whereas reducing the length of question periods, limiting the number of questions that may be asked or imposing more restrictive rules on their formulation may have the effect of diminishing the capacity of citizens to make their concerns heard;
entries.74b1df67c4311dc8d276d1d3240fa9136a850e70: Whereas certain changes in the way citizens participate on-line or on-line may have the effect of limiting opportunities for citizens to ask questions or obtain answers from municipal authorities;
entries.f8d9d17e9fd3851c082c676cdf73f3d07ec64cde: Whereas citizen participation is fully meaningful when citizens not only have the opportunity to ask their questions, but also to obtain comprehensive, accessible and timely answers from public bodies;
entries.7873dc0cd7febf418257f810e65f084a1c2aa355: Whereas public access to consultation sessions and public commissions is an essential condition for full democratic participation;
entries.e365c48d2c7615bc40fd107acf69ea441d79400d: Whereas certain meetings of municipal councils or public commissions have aroused a citizen interest exceeding the capacity to accommodate the places held, thus preventing persons wishing to attend the deliberations and exchanges from participating in them due to lack of available places;
entries.d4acb4f7d7f9490531b85aaa9d443a5659d5b9f2: Whereas we observe, in several respects, a erosion of certain democratic practices, of consultation and citizen participation and that it is important to remain vigilant in order to protect our institutions and the mechanisms favouring them;
entries.b3e857baa88aac26da02214741018f9ae11513d2: Whereas the Participative Budget is a democratic mechanism in place to facilitate citizen participation, transparency of political processes and support a sense of trust among constituents in elected officials;
entries.d06d60836e4f1dcfc8d3bc1e75031135c217eab1: Whereas the Participatory Budget is a recognized tool to facilitate the democratic contribution of young people and historically marginalized populations;
entries.6c26cd732998f10a9e4dce688d7fead117e30d1c: Whereas the Participatory Budget has contributed to achieving the City of Montreal's climate goals, not only through priority projects, but also through the mobilization of tens of thousands of Montrealers and Montreal women around environmental issues;
entries.ca77c487ddd408b7f80dfa2645b3c707296bdb1d: Whereas the dissolution of Concertation Montréal represents a loss of immeasurable expertise that contributed significantly to citizen participation in the democratic and political life of Metropole and Quebec;
entries.60d2b9dfb6dc9d3bb47d7072cd665e5a92790ec4: Whereas citizen participation is a fundamental element of effective municipal governance and contributes to strengthening the relationship of trust between the population and public institutions;
entries.1f3f11663e7599ab6e011ce98658033c294eea3a: Whereas the City of Montreal has, over the years, put in place various mechanisms for public participation that enable citizens to contribute to the identification of the needs of their communities and the development of municipal policies, programs and projects;
entries.80cd18ca5b51667f990756b4c75553c9bcd53b13: Whereas mechanisms of citizen participation are all the more important in a context where democratic institutions must continually demonstrate their transparency, openness and ability to respond to the concerns of the population;
entries.e16de97e5f5dc632a35a54351f6503b784b87b36: Whereas community bodies, consultation tables, local associations and public institutions play an essential role in promoting citizen engagement and democratic dialogue;
entries.317c642842cc5a911fdcc45ddefa28c623634c6c: Whereas all these initiatives and actors contribute to bringing municipal institutions closer to the population and to promoting meaningful citizen participation in public affairs;
entries.9041b9b84933e4564e96ff0c73b6f9bd786b5c50: Whereas the City Council has emphasized André Berthelet's memory as the first person elected non-Mayor or mayor to preside over the city council, and therefore to welcome citizens who wish to avail themselves of the new right, also established by the RCM, to ask a question to the mayor or other persons elected from the executive committee;
entries.dcb1ac80321e80df846c60f4a194b3e1a54774b7: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, Councillor Olivier Demers-Dubé.
entries.73acc9fdc81cf574d53574e68e73fcad16ca3f7f: In summary, Mr. Demers-Dubé articulates his presentation around three fundamental democratic tools: consultation, dialogue and participation. He believes in the success of this citizenry approach by giving the people the necessary levers to implement the ideas that result from his commitment. And, in honour of the 20th International Day of Democracy, he quotes the Secretary-General of the United Nations: [...] faced with the crises that threaten us, it is our duty and the need to strengthen the democratic foundations and preserve the spaces that enable people to participate in public life.
entries.eaa9b1d7648d74877db6b1fa85c905761301b9a6: On the administration's side, Councillor Maude Théroux-Séguin went on to say that this motion would not be supported by the majority and that some of the issues raised should be contextualized. She also felt that democracy needed a nuanced dialogue and great listening before the elected people took decisions.
entries.a6bdfa9984f0584be59bed7249164b6329d7a951: She agreed with the substance of the motion. However, she shared certain reservations, particularly when it was suggested that the municipal council should interfere in democratic affairs within the boroughs' jurisdiction, and recalled how essential respect for autonomy and the choices exercised by those elected in the boroughs remained.
entries.8ab2a8f9189b0f1f899d6355a2793fd6d5a05712: The debate continued with statements by Councillor François Limoges and Councillor Véronique Fournier, who agreed on the best documented practices to be retained and safeguarded as democratic pillars, in support of those described by their colleague, Mr Demers-Dubé.
entries.5c11fbbe8a39a4792aa26a2720f4126f4c8ff267: In turn, the members of the Administration, Councillors Caroline Braun and Christine Black, and Councillor Luis Miranda, emphasize, among other things, the importance of protecting democratic choices expressed by the population at the local level in the borough.
entries.1791e20e9a30d25ccf6ca49aa430769928906886: At 9:22 p.m., the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde, asked the Chair of Council that Mr. Miranda focus his intervention on the motion under consideration, and the Chair took note of it and closed the debate.
entries.42a7d89f70f03269d61113d5530ffe5760d9d076: After the intervention of Mr Miranda, the leader of the majority, Julien Henault-Ratelle acquiesced in the comments of the members of the Administration and presented examples lived in his borough.
entries.31b8508cee9dcab29badccab388493d3a74921b6: to continue its work until the conclusion of this motion.
entries.9272162cabcb1e01b639d548b1c0f54ce8ec056b: The deputy leader of the majority, Alexandre Devaux-Guizani, adds his voice and testimony to those of his colleagues in the Administration.
entries.17006e1c278dcac78229050e459a3463c9c0fe19: The proposer of the motion, Olivier Demers-Dubé, concluded his presentation by stating that he would have liked to be approached in advance by the Administration to discuss the content of the motion before today's municipal council.
entries.1b71dbe4f2cb227033e720a6a7498a9d7beab695: The debate resumed with the following members in order: Councillors Émilie Brière, Stephanie Valenzuela, Sarah V. Doyon, Julie-Pascale Provost and Councillor Dimitrios (Jim) Beis.
entries.4c9c398d98a249330d095aa1bda3c30c4b47b1cc: These statements by the members of the Official Opposition and the members of the Administration, respectively, defend the views of the two political groups.
entries.cb25ee2fd0107285f528876c8f9eb3cec45d0048: Also, during these interventions, the Chairperson asked Councillor Julie-Pascale Provost to remove the false word from her remarks. Ms. Provost replaced it with an incorrect one and the Chair thanked her.
entries.82e6ceb6a174737f1537f4251bdc8a15740394c0: To close the debate, Montreal Mayor Soraya Martinez Ferrada argued that this motion had intentions to the detriment of the facts and suggested that it should be withdrawn and worked with all Council members in order to strengthen democracy in Montreal.

entries.81b2376c63d6e85430be6efbe908abfcfa542961: At 2:08 p.m., Council resumed its work and, pursuant to section 119 of the Municipal Council Assembly Procedure and Rules of Internal Economy Regulations (06-051), Council Chair Chantal Rossi invited Ms. Blanchet to make her report, which indicated that the Committee of the Whole had sat for 90 minutes, 13 members spoke on a total of 42 questions, adding that the work of the Committee of the Whole had been properly conducted and thanking all members of the Board who had intervened, as well as the Auditor General and her team.
entries.98b8f956e18f78fc90f3a596ed3c41fecc84bf24: The Chair thanked Ms. Blanchet for chairing this committee and said item 7.08 was tabled.
