entries.9ca8c6c23e42bb618a38a5fc2f54406e3dcee688: 1- Commemorates the Armenian Genocide and the commemorative day dedicated to it on 24 April 2026;
entries.25676d940118830bbedb2ed4876cc99e0432830a: 2. Underlines the commitment of members of the Armenian community to the work of recognizing and commemorating genocide on the international scene;
entries.bec46b1f277455d0a1ac01735a6d2c017e56d45d: 3- recalls the importance of preserving historical memory and invites all Montrealers to show solidarity with the Armenian people;
entries.4fbe014ad636f631157813d78d804cbca96cf3f8: 4- recognizes the important contributions of the Armenian community to the vitality of the metropolis, particularly in terms of cultural and social economic policy.
entries.ea8cc2d38807c79318ed13ad9fa27ec0c59382e0: Whereas on 24 April 1915 almost 600 people, mostly from Armenian intellectual circles, were arrested by the Ottoman authorities in Constantinople before being deported or murdered;
entries.f5efc69bb1ad89ad5c721588b89e04c3c44fa7e2: Whereas a United Nations Sub-Commission on Human Rights first recognized the Armenian genocide in a resolution in August 1985;
entries.4391619943fbad2e24fc7f06c36156d2cc351bb5: Whereas the City Council of Montreal recognizes 24 April as the Commemorative Day of the Armenian Genocide since 1997 condemning the massacre of 15 million men of women and children, as well as the deportation and uprooting of survivors of their territories;
entries.c3ac12d28acfd4e2ffa5688e5e2173743823833d: Whereas the National Assembly of Quebec passed a law proclaiming April 24 each year as the Day of Remembrance of the Armenian Genocide on November 28, 2003;
entries.776c18dbf63feab6c884ce439e138d077cde3dba: Whereas on 21 April 2004 the Canadian Parliament adopted a motion recognizing the Armenian genocide;
entries.ee6f43d03d11873ee39866dc41a50baf7571443f: Whereas the City of Montreal is committed to combating racism and discrimination as well as promoting harmonious intercultural relations by adopting the Montreal Declaration against Racial Discrimination, the Montreal Declaration for Cultural Diversity and Inclusion, the Declaration to Recognize the Systemic Character of Racism and Discrimination and the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities;
entries.57d8fe22e5d5e4828193166749b7ca0934d8323a: Whereas Montreal has been a place of welcome for Armenian refugees and the Armenian community now gathers more than 50,000 Montrealers;
entries.2f8f2227125b36fc10c630edabfbcf791fa9047a: Whereas the memorial The repair at the corner of Henri-Bourassa Boulevards and Acadia in the district of Ahuntsic-Cartierville was erected in memory of the genocides of the twentieth century and their victims;
entries.5782152d9cfd269ec2959809c556c4859792951a: Whereas members of the Armenian community of Montreal descendants of survivors of the genocide are actively involved in the construction of the metropolis thanks to their cultural and social political commitment.

entries.6fd42228096ac0f00b56fa620efb37c9cd2e3943: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Vana Nazarian for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.ffb73c21f8aeb324502df412dd830b4c297b4dec: At the start of the game, she greets the guests present on the balcony. She presents herself as a proud Montrealer of Armenian origin, whose children were born in Montreal, a city where her family found a real home.
entries.572b07dcce7cd771de10a734fb313433c892622f: Nazarian then cites three people of Armenian origin who have deeply shaped Montreal's history through their commitment and contribution to the host society that they fully adopted. She starts with Noshig Eloyan, first mayor of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and former president of the executive committee. As a woman of conviction, Ms. Eloyan was committed to officially recognizing the Armenian genocide in municipal institutions and was the instigator of the La Reparation monument, located at Marcelin-Wilson Park.
entries.749beb73aa21eafc7d16c4a01d2b6c526937a058: The Councillor also highlighted the contribution of Harout Chitilian, the youngest president of the city council and vice-president of the executive committee, who introduced the concept of a smart city in Montreal, as well as contributing to the organization of the March for Humanity, which brought together more than 10,000 participants.
entries.113be90ef7d37aedd7c74543d40b12b938d33f41: Ms. Nazarian goes back to the recognition given to Mary Deros, honoured by the municipal council the previous month, for her outstanding commitment, which she said had paved the way for many immigrants. Finally, she mentioned that there were more than 50,000 people in the Armenian community in Greater Montreal, who were actively working to build intergenerational ties and enrich Montreal society.
entries.3872a0646bf6902f518fd6b266c8f905a73810d3: The President then gave the floor to Councillor Effie Giannou and the Official Opposition Chief Ericka Alneus, respectively.
entries.452c96dceb7115f170770cbdaabc9d6b323ad5a7: In her turn, Ms. Giannou stressed the importance of this day of commemoration and also greeted the guests present on the balcony. She was of the opinion that April 24, the 111th anniversary of the Armenian genocide, constituted a collective duty of remembrance. She highlighted, among other things, the remarkable contribution of the Armenian community to Montreal's cultural and social wealth. She invited all Montrealers to join in the commemorative march which would take place on Thursday, April 23 at 5 p.m. and which would conclude at the La Reparation monument, Marcelin-Wilson Park.
entries.b90835b91df42880e58b8d501c65cfaf171ddfea: For her part, Ms. Ericka Alneus rose by thanking the people present on the balcony and stressed in particular the importance of remembering events such as the Armenian genocide. She believed that living in a democracy implied the collective responsibility to denounce these atrocities so that they would never happen again, while recognizing our duty to do better. Ms. Alneus also invited the Montreal population to visit the La Reparation monument.
entries.6aabaa8f6ff9c4b45619d11c897d229b62d3eb70: The Chairperson thanked the three elected representatives for their interventions and confirmed the names of all members present on the City Council as supporters of this Declaration.
entries.62536b1e30e0a12377e33cd82a828d49e9cf4cf9: 1- Celebrates Asian Heritage Month in May 2026;
entries.9a622ee1bc2b0f6684dc339e986a499ce5dd6734: 2- highlights the invaluable contribution of communities of Asian origin to the development and outreach of Montreal;
entries.0b1239e47b02cbe3cec1dcb805c8ef1d0e892ff4: 3- continues to support the preservation and vitality of the Chinese Quarter, an emblematic place for Montreal and Quebecers because of its heritage, cultural outreach and unique history at the heart of downtown;
entries.29afab12a55426d082866b6c3740903829fdf65a: 4- Continues to work with its partners to combat racism and systemic discrimination, promote inclusion and recognize the different Asian cultures that bring out the city.
entries.a3850093f13bf440cb3b06c22fd8948bddc9c01d: Whereas Asian Heritage Month has been celebrated in Canada since the 1990s and the federal government signed an official declaration in May 2002 to make May Asian Heritage Month;
entries.680aadf3ba06b899a701ef3108db63329c27f648: Whereas in April 2004, the City of Montreal, in turn, proclaimed May as Asian Heritage Month;
entries.23446d41189af92f32c837e5254b737196e00d68: Whereas Asian Heritage Month is an opportunity to recognize and celebrate the invaluable contributions that Montrealers of Asian origin have made and continue to make to the identity, prosperity, history, economy and culture of the metropolis;
entries.b52e8db02f62087c6b15734a26cccecbdbbca993: Whereas Montreal Asian communities make a significant contribution to key sectors, such as entrepreneurship, international trade and scientific innovation, and are very active in the academic and cultural spheres;
entries.e302a89d4045f7571b3d2a2393b4cdb45f05b2dd: Whereas Asian communities, still to date, face issues of under-representation in management positions, barriers to career advancement, racism and persistent discrimination;
entries.f671e47b347654db04f609e9952a2e05de4e7f1f: Whereas the City of Montreal is more committed than ever to combating racism and discrimination against Asian Montrealers and is in action to combat this problem on several fronts;
entries.1fd2ec4a7c46820241ac8292a8982f6357d7e501: Whereas for more than a century Montreal has been a historic territory of welcome, gathering and solidarity for people from Asia;
entries.7176478bab5239f400cb28f33884b3e9eff88b34: Whereas Asian Heritage Month makes it possible to correct the lack of visibility of Asian people in Montreal history and to create spaces for dialogue and representation;
entries.b4769a965c13c59b362f6752ef62bb4f4581a10e: Whereas the arrival in Montreal of refugees from South-East Asia, beginning in 1975, led to the passage into Canada of the Immigration Act of 1976, which, combined with private sponsorship and the Quebec sponsorship program, then inspired the City of Montreal to develop a welcoming strategy;
entries.03222cec9509ebfdda48bc49dfa66404ed7fedc2: Whereas since the 1980s, the arrival of refugees from India, including Punjab, Pakistan, Bangladesh and Sri Lanka, in Montreal has intensified as a result of political and religious instability in their countries of origin;
entries.1aadc294478d92c424738a9778325370dbd1783c: Whereas the Chinese Quarter of Montreal is the only significant historical district in a preserved Chinese community in Quebec and eastern Canada, and the only French-speaking Chinese neighbourhood in America;
entries.246d6e54ddbbc888cdbcfec31e1f7cf7a614ce0b: Whereas the Government of Quebec and the City of Montreal have joined forces to protect the heritage character of the Chinese Quarter of Montreal by adopting measures aimed at maintaining its historic and unique character;
entries.8cdc43e6f930c159ccb06462c7678d3ece2ba8c3: Whereas the Chinese Quarter of Montreal became, in 2024, the first area designated by the City of Montréal as a historic site under the Cultural Heritage Act.
entries.efd60aaf7c566e0cc10418cf61f87e2056f98c24: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Milany Thiagarajah for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.9282bdb2bfe67d5adbfecf87ccb1f6a0371f3949: From the outset, Councillor Milany Thiagarajah highlights Asian Heritage Month in Montreal and across the country as a moment of special significance. She says that Asian heritage is not limited to a single history, language or culture, but rather constitutes a vast mosaic of communities and pathways marked by resilience. In particular, she indicates that Asian communities have been established in Montreal for more than a century and are actively contributing to the history, economy, cultural vitality and influence of the Montréal community, as well as in the fields of scientific innovation and academia.
entries.7bb86f32351f402cda7b106f8da3de873c56b166: Thiagarajah explains that, through her trips to Asia, she is always touched by human warmth, a sense of hospitality and cultural richness through memorable gastronomy. She also admires the beauty and diversity of traditional clothes, whose colours, fabrics and know-how express deep identity and pride. She recalls that Asian Heritage Month reinforces inclusion, respect and living together. Councillor Milany Thiagarajah concludes by thanking organizations and volunteers committed to celebrating Asian Heritage Month in Montreal.
entries.742b40a346be3fb02b127e56a7ef63e446992fe6: The Chair thanked her and gave the floor respectively to Councillor Cathy Wong and to Councillor Claude Pinard.
entries.e76528975dbd9da8124f5c65de1068129bea9bf6: In her turn, Ms. Wong points out Asian Heritage Month as a time of celebration, but above all a time of memory, transmission and recognition. She says that through her children's curiosity for Asia, she conveys to them the pride of their roots through language, arts and culture. However, she mentions that this heritage also carries wounds, marked by racism, exclusion and historical injustices, while remaining a history of resilience and creation and that cultural initiatives are proof of a vibrant culture within the community. Councillor Cathy Wong concludes by expressing the hope that children from the Asian community in Montreal may grow up without having to choose between their origins and their affiliation.
entries.f13ea3257acdb396570fbedf2d5dee195d492a73: Pinard, for his part, pointed out that since 2004, Asian Heritage Month had been officially emphasized in Montreal to recognize communities that had been present for more than a hundred years and were essential to the rise of the city. He affirmed, among other things, that diversity remained one of the greatest riches of Montreal and that this wealth must be protected by concrete actions to combat racism, discrimination and under-representation still experienced by Asian communities. Finally, Councillor Claude Pinard invited the population and his colleagues to celebrate in May the exceptional contribution of Asian communities.
entries.1440bafe0164a5ab0fd622fc683b75bf31e52d74: The Chair thanked those elected for their interventions and then confirmed the names of all members present on the City Council as supporters of this Declaration.
entries.e55969623cbee6dba751f371f78747fd7804d73c: 1- recognizes World Book and Copyright Day and celebrates the talent of authors, as well as that of book actors in the metropolis;
entries.1469a03558165eca1b173f708bfdd22bc6660955: 2- recognizes the expertise of public library staff in managing the selection and dissemination of collections made available to citizens;
entries.36379898af3a516fda2f49ab96ae8686f0208332: 3- recognize the power of books as a bridge between generations and cultures;
entries.e4fb9ce6504ff8cc13e2112f9d66f80436e8fb6f: 4- encourages the entire population, including its youngest readers, to read Quebec and Montreal books throughout the year.
entries.59b2345a15a9362b6550849752087db98d5a8234: Whereas World Book and Copyright Day, celebrated on 23 April, is an initiative of UNESCO aimed at promoting reading and publishing, defending copyright and paying tribute to writers, writers and all actors in the book industry;
entries.4149a81a35d6db5d03be7e8067d44b1c3f4909b1: Whereas the date of 23 April was chosen to mark the birth or death of major authors on that same date, in particular the death of William Shakespeare, Miguel de Cervantes and Inca Garcilaso de la Vega in 1616;
entries.210454321731a1226f2792333a031b1a603e349d: Whereas the world capital of Book 2026 is Rabat, which has committed itself to integrating literacy into its policies and proposing a wide range of activities throughout the year aimed at strengthening the role of books in sustainable and inclusive development;
entries.5295133b993dd946caab16526735d84071aaa620: Whereas UNESCO is committed to promoting indigenous and local languages as part of the celebrations around World Book and Copyright Day for the decade 2022-2032;
entries.53e3463926fb8335ca034f191f675abc2ae33fdc: Whereas the City of Montreal annually presents the Grand Prix du livre de Montréal and the Prix du livre jeunesse des Bibliothèques de Montréal to celebrate the richness of the talent of the authors of the metropolis;
entries.afd5d9424df6185597cc00e0404fe1a7a0a71a2a: Whereas the City of Montreal can count on the annual Montreal Book Fair, the most important event of its kind in the province, which attracts more than 100,000 readers each edition and has a significant impact on the entire Quebec book ecosystem;
entries.cfabf8dbf5eca6c6cc1b269c30d3c378b507c9da: Whereas the Festival de la BD takes place in May of each year in Montreal and, for the occasion, rue Saint-Denis becomes a pedestrian in order to welcome many authors, illustrators and illustrators who come to meet their readers of all ages;
entries.67c060f7a78f9a2b50e6e2025717044b41da1c67: Whereas Montrealers can count on a network of public libraries that acts as a driving force for social, economic and cultural development;
entries.b2ffcb9108309e2f207f46bfaf4a27cbf9f03be4: Whereas Montreal public libraries are places where a relationship develops with knowledge of exploration, exchange, knowledge, culture and enrichment that fosters citizen engagement.
entries.a4adbd2ee02971e55db724b963042e46db4bae4f: Christopher McCray Sylvain Ouellet Véronique Fournier Josefina Blanco Carla Beauvais Cathy Wong Jocelyn Pauzé Jean François Lalonde Alex Norris Nathalie Goulet Martine Musau Muele Sarah V. Doyon Peter McQueen Catherine Houbart Olivier Demers-Dubé Elvira Carhuallanqui Émilie Brière Maeva Vilain Sterling Downey Élise Tanguay Céline-Audrey Beauregard Nancy Blanchet Richard Deschamps Laura Palestini Andrée Henault
entries.346e7e9ba27f51661e3b77357e0d5966aaeb55e9: Counselor Josué Corvil emphasizes the central role of reading and bookmaking in Montreal's cultural life, particularly on the occasion of World Book Day celebrated annually on April 23, an initiative created by UNESCO in October 1995. Mr. Corvil continues by recalling the historical events of the world of literature that led to the choice of this date as well as certain international traditions and recognitions related to the world of books. He then highlights the vitality of the book ecosystem in Montreal and Quebec, and more specifically, the structuring role of the Salon du livre de Montréal, whose 49th edition will take place from November 25 to 29, 2026.
entries.2f0fb8a8b65b2fe5fbd08499ca406f007cb33edd: Subsequently, Councillor Josué Corvil highlighted the cultural contribution of Quebec authors, notably by mentioning Télisson Aurélien, Chantal Guy and Paulette Valcour. Finally, he closed his speech by stressing the importance of Montreal libraries as essential services and inviting the public to devote more time to reading.
entries.8bcd8ef0bcc96771b2517eb640419378e005572e: The Chair then gave the floor to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde, and the Chief of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, respectively.
entries.5aaee7281bbeba82b9e7c9ad8581de8ab17482da: For her part, Mrs Plourde supports the comments made by her colleague and particularly highlights the essential role of school libraries, stressing the commitment of volunteer parents to their work and contributing to children's cultural and intellectual awakening. She recalls the lasting importance of the book in a context marked by instantaneity, then stresses the social and cultural significance of literature through its adaptation on stage, including the work Let Our Joy Remain of Kev Lambert, and invites people to celebrate World Book and Copyright Day.
entries.28a4915fe42bda97651842e337fe69d48b1a224f: In turn, the head of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, salutes the City of Montreal's commitment to promoting the book, the authors and the Book Fair. She follows by addressing, among other things, the role of libraries as places for learning, knowledge and democracy, then reiterates the importance of copyright and artistic and literary freedom as foundations of imagination and democratic vitality.

entries.1edcf8fd63ae657618c3c36aeeab0ee23517f925: 1 - maintains or strengthens the current regulations by continuing to limit short-term rentals in principal residences during the summer months of its territory;
entries.a95bf3e9f6539e4143baf0fb460380a93bd0cf7a: 2 - Continue and intensify enforcement efforts, including through strengthening inspection teams and monitoring mechanisms;
entries.c00cab00ad9804f8a90274348c9249a9f6c3ab65: 3 - clearly reaffirms that the protection of the rental park and access to housing for the Montreal population are more important priorities than tourist accommodation;
entries.bffbb1b65c5a0676b2571fafb934fb8f709e6497: 4 - continue its representations to the Government of Quebec in order to obtain the necessary powers and tools to ensure effective and consistent supervision of short-term rentals.
entries.965666484cfa7b0f2ccd1049b65afe9e3763cfbd: Whereas the housing crisis in Montreal results in a marked shortage of accessible, affordable and safe housing for an increasing proportion of the population;
entries.4d8c1dcd8836221892a41df55742cf4e2b47be59: Whereas this situation particularly weakens tenants, many of whom spend an excessive proportion of their income on housing, thus increasing their residential insecurity;
entries.5249f15d62dd1b5cdff1fdc9c850544c734683e1: Whereas the maintenance and protection of the existing rental stock is an essential and immediate lever to respond to this crisis, in addition to efforts to build new housing;
entries.47231af17ab64275114d60f20a22b7bf26f190ac: Whereas the conversion of residential housing into short-term rental units for tourists has the effect of removing dwellings from the traditional rental market and exerting upward pressure on rents;
entries.3f6823c281d1aac039a655a5d6b213892127fe26: Whereas the City of Montreal has recently put in place a stricter regulatory framework for short-term rentals to curb this phenomenon and protect the residential vocation of its neighbourhoods;
entries.85319727b0d47454cc8c5218583cf997bbace910: Whereas the City of Montreal has already carried out a pilot project to allow short-term rental by limiting residents to 90 days throughout the year to rent their house or apartment;
entries.6442a76a82af27bd7f6f2b1314e4f73ca8d481a1: Whereas this pilot project by the City of Montreal has shown that it is impossible to implement such a regime, both in terms of the scope of the inspection task and in terms of evidence;
entries.9110f6d21a942e7dfa58be3db1a4e6dec3fd9ee4: Whereas the City's resources are limited and the pilot project has proved ineffective both in terms of compliance with regulations and enforcement;
entries.b5b3ec6cb45be6ae571910310d78187e9118e535: Whereas any relaxation of the recent framework adopted by the City could jeopardize the gains achieved and increase the scarcity of housing available to Montrealers;
entries.32dc334a4c0d54a16d7244ba03b9ea1632f4015c: Whereas the municipal government's priority in terms of housing must remain the protection of the right to housing and the response to the needs of the Montreal population, prior to the economic interests associated with tourism rental;
entries.52012ad5d9c44666c2b5c4b2115eef5915e35e11: Whereas the proliferation of non-compliant short-term rentals may lead to the establishment of de facto tourist accommodation facilities in residential areas, at the expense of the quality of living;
entries.672905accec164f66564b39145ce44d6a73d6543: The Chair of Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, Councillor Élise Tanguay, for her presentation.
entries.a4f2b3e9ce6af526b243cd579d2922a5a3a69bc1: Ms. Tanguay began by hoping that the Regulations concerning tourist accommodation facilities would not be altered in order to prevent the erosion of Montreal's rental stock. She, in particular, presented several pitfalls during the analysis work and the reasons for the settlement. Finally, in this crisis of affordability, she was of the opinion that there could be no further victimization.
entries.7f39959436beaaa54d9f200ff483e51c15dd6aaa: He then spoke to Councillor Alex Norris and the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada.
entries.a521341115e7f067230e899da9e334d30fa0ea7b: Mr. Norris referred to the experience experienced in the boroughs of Plateau Mont-Royal, Ville-Marie and Sud-Ouest and reported on the difficulties encountered by the inspection squads. As for the Mayor of Montreal, she referred to the Administration's commitments, which included eliminating any commercialization of housing and introducing more restrictions on the version of the previous Administration's regulations. In closing, she wished to see real solutions to the issue of short-term rental and added that she disagreed with this motion.
entries.448911af05afaf69692f2d7b6c3e1a4c1ee6029b: Mr Norris took the floor for a few clarifications and Ms Tanguay followed up on her right of reply.
entries.d35533cdb835841db40330a5875f3419a6651a5e: 1- that the transfer in whole or in part of the terrain of the Hippodrome be conditional on the establishment by GALOPH of a governance which integrates within its decision-making bodies the presence of the relevant elected representatives, both within the executive and in the borough Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, representative.es of the community milieu of Côte-des-Neiges and expert in the field of out-of-market housing, in proportions which will ensure that the development of the site will be guided by the public interest;
entries.65127e69a4bc209fb71942b79a795215621dd8b4: 2- that the City of Montreal take steps with the Government of Quebec to incorporate amendments to PL 22 to ensure that such governance is in place;
entries.dff6f0ea12962805ee2d0a492849209d4c0164b9: 3- that the City of Montreal establish concrete guarantees with GALOPH to ensure that the development of the site is carried out in accordance with the Management Plan for Development and Development (PDAD) presented in 2024;
entries.38a3a28171562ebccf6e814bafcb7afe599a7bd5: 4- that land tax leave, the transfer of federal grants and other forms of assistance required for the development of the site to the organization shall not be at the expense of the financial capacity of the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce or that of the City, and that a time limit and procedure be established for planning the termination of property tax exemptions, in particular in the case of sales of lots to undertakings covered by the Municipal Grants Prohibition Act;
entries.86fe800d5bb19cc51d067c74836e9aa164c455ed: 5- that the City of Montreal requires from GALOPH, as soon as the land is transferred, an annual reporting to the Commission sur les finances et l'administration (CFA), like any other paramunicipal body - for example the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau, the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) or the Corporation d'habitation Jeanne-Mance (CHJM) - taking into account the exemption from property taxes and the delegation of full authority to manage the assets of the City which will be granted to it.
entries.9461ad4b2d8632492746c5a88e964cff77e9775e: Whereas the Hippodrome site is a valuable asset belonging to all Montrealers and all Montrealers, and that the development of a comprehensive living environment on this site must meet the community's aspirations, particularly in terms of social and affordable housing, mobility, proximity services and green spaces;
entries.41255aec9a145af2188c41bf73e60cba8b7a7284: Whereas, following several years of consultations, consultation, planning and analysis, the City adopted in 2024 the Master Plan for Development and Development (PDAD) for the future neighbourhood, providing for the construction of more than 20,000 housing units, half of which are dedicated to out-of-market housing;
entries.69b233d7f0ad19a59b0af6329a354441830b7919: Whereas the federal government has invested $130 million through the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund (CILIF) and the City has set aside more than $190 million for its IDP to launch Phase 1 work on the site;
entries.4e52a8d743e92dbab93d411db06f543b625fac1c: Whereas Bill 22 of the Government of Quebec, if passed, would authorize the City of Montreal to transfer, in whole or in part, the land it holds in the Namur-Hippodrome sector to the OBNL GALOPH (Accelation Group for Optimization of the Hippodrome Project), which would be exempt from property taxes on such land during the redevelopment phase;
entries.19817d69e6c31e4650ed3fe120fedc81fe1e41ee: Whereas entrusting the development of this project to a non-profit third party entity is an innovative and relevant approach for better risk management and agility in developing the site;
entries.376b8bcdd53e7783e984abe26dd6de2786044169: Whereas such agility should not be won at the cost of abandoning the principles of sound and collaborative governance, and of rigorous and transparent public interest management;
entries.b667ab5a6936f1f013594e23fec4f6ef5bba852d: The Chair of the Board, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, Councillor Émilie Brière, for her presentation.
entries.0d59bb15d602543028f03ae4813b02024cc225b7: In opening, Ms Brière hopes that the project of the Hippodrome site will be able to meet in concrete terms the housing needs of the population of the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce. She also describes some historical elements of the project. Finally, she highlights the work of the GALOP and hopes that all actors will be around the table in the development of this project which will take place over a long period of time.
entries.efa476b580b099e3a2c0de0a2b123fb17490c1bd: At 5:29 p.m., the council suspended its work for dinner break.
entries.e1546ed20dc93edf65b3cc411e9a0764988c7f99: At 8:36 p.m., Council resumed its consideration of motion 65.02.
entries.aa8d1a6648ad30549caaa1cca3a8cc545f2e2130: The Chair gave the floor consecutively to Councillors Caroline Braun, Élise Tanguay, and Councillors Claude Pinard and François Limoges.
entries.6359952b7ab73b4cd593f6cd0b523941b55c1ec8: Counsel Caroline Braun, the Authority's representative for this matter, provided a different view and argued, in particular, that the premises do not reflect the reality of the project. This motion will not be supported by the Authority and concludes by indicating that several requests made in this motion are already provided for in the existing legislative framework.
entries.363db0b61e82e5a6d898676ef657b0484588b00f: Élise Tanguay appreciates the opening of the Administration and would like it to be delighted to support this motion. As for Councillor Claude Pinard, he insists on the mobilization of civil society in his project, on the commitment of the Administration to deliver housing to the most vulnerable and to innovate so much on ways of doing things. Second, Councillor François Limoges suggests a joint work between elected people in order to arrive at a consensual version of the motion.
entries.7ad6b08a0be92485608d71238ed7c788ddb9675e: In conclusion, the majority leader, Julien Henault-Ratelle, confirmed that the Administration would not vote in favour of this motion and Councillor Émilie Brière exercised her right to reply.

entries.1cbe2d188e4b1bada7512dd298f16d233fbc97c6: 6 - maintain its goal of carbon-neutrality by 2050, which goes, in an integral way, through the decarbonisation of the passenger and freight transport sector;

entries.3640ef2b8551d906a7599c12c70e330929e54093: Councillors Catherine Houbart and Gabrielle Rousseau-Bélanger tabled a new consensus version of 65.03. The new version reads as follows:
entries.b6965055b1806b134c21f4c352de0d67fb133d64: Whereas the climate crisis acts as a multiplier of risks to the many crises in the metropolis, exacerbating existing social and economic vulnerabilities;
entries.037aa8cdb7e89b58cc56205ef582ffdd2a256811: Whereas Montreal is exposed to challenges specific to large densely populated cities, such as areas of wells suitable for discharge during rains and floods, significant mineralization of the territory and increased vulnerability to heat islands in increasingly hot summers;
entries.9ef1010fbe1319325be8eea0cbd24035590bce38: Whereas, in the current housing crisis, climate resilience is a sine qua non for the sustainability of the existing housing stock and the viability of future construction projects, in order to protect citizens from damage and material loss;
entries.4b6f4eee13191095d5bb11771a5023f2a301f136: Whereas increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events (torrential rains, ice episodes, heat waves) requires a proactive and accelerated adaptation of our urban infrastructure;
entries.a0614182f702ba959173735500edfc3480e0c4a7: Whereas science recognizes green infrastructures (ponge parks, vegetated nudes, urban canopy) as suitable solutions for surface water management and thermal regulation, and also contributes to Montreal's biodiversity at a sustainable cost;
entries.59d58f2afe3aee5d4b267513f2d0c1a7ed0d533b: Whereas the Montreal Water Strategy, adopted unanimously by the City Council in 2024, recommends that green, resilient or sponge infrastructure be systematically developed prioritizing more flood-prone basin areas in order to reduce pressure on the sewer system;
entries.874c1b0a356dffff9772c434787a4266e3704e6c: Whereas in order to act coherently and responsibly in response to the climate crisis, it is important to invest our efforts both in reducing the GHG emissions of the Montreal community and in adapting the territory to these climate changes;
entries.873244ffc37b6e13358b9362fdc76d527b25acbb: Whereas the 5th Montreal Climate Summit highlighted an unprecedented mobilization of civil society and the socio-economic community, demonstrating high expectations for the City to maintain and strengthen its climate ambitions;
entries.247b2bcb12b571b58dc0600f59c213f970e2a5e0: The chair of the board, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the motion's proposer, Councillor Catherine Houbart.
entries.5322174819ae992ab3b0b98a9df9da223d9960da: In summary, she stressed the importance of the Climate Plan and shared responsibilities, as well as the need not to save money in order to protect the environment. Concerned about climate risks today and for future generations, she said that the financial burden of the climate emergency remained higher than climate action and concluded with the common priority of making this socio-ecological transition in the fight against climate change.
entries.462459b3cdb525838e3541ef6ea93c8c2577c32b: As a result of the talks by Councillor Sarah V. Doyon and Councillor Alex Norris, they reiterated, inter alia, the need to achieve the objectives of the Climate Plan and to respect the roadmap in order to achieve it for the resilience and adaptability of our metropolis.
entries.0326beb66cbaba41bbdcc1b3f31e12e3db41c27a: Then, the Administration's representative for this issue, Councillor Gabrielle Rousseau-Bélanger, spoke in particular about the increase in risks within this climate crisis, exacerbating existing social and economic inequalities. Finally, she cited some changes to this new consensual version of the motion.
entries.93d8dbb5ab5c4fa0469e9dab4839bdcf050d52cb: At 10:03 p.m., Council resumed its work.
entries.52d5c6757f77c309afecacbb80b1ddfcc3bb206b: On her return, Councillor Carla Beauvais referred in particular to the state of alert in her district due to spring floods and reported on the concerns of the population. In this regard, she relied on concrete actions such as measures to integrate permeable surfaces during the renovation of the streets in order to retain and slow down the water.
entries.d786a788b6f03e3f06ff3d7c38521abcab341730: In conclusion, counselor Gabrielle Rouseau-Bélanger pointed out that climate resilience must be a matter of fairness, security and accountability to future generations.
entries.9c1ce259d4fc1fd9cc87ab5b9ab82f337f2f053b: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, thanked all Council members for their interventions and gave the floor to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde.

entries.b1e42d2f5480a017a0a558f340b7c23b228c5fe6: 1 - the City of Montreal celebrates the 27th anniversary of the Week of Action against Racism and for Equal Opportunities and invites the public to participate in the many activities offered from March 21 to 31, 2026;
entries.fc9e16d383416d34b014bc9cfdd7a9d34761df6e: 2 - the City of Montreal strongly reaffirms that racism is a violation of human rights and freedoms, and that, in the face of direct, indirect or systemic racism and all forms of racism and discrimination, zero tolerance is required;
entries.8b831d9f053843531ebee26a667180a76043e88f: 3 - the City of Montreal reiterates its commitment to local, community and citizen initiatives that combat racism and promote intercultural dialogue in all boroughs;
entries.a74b16fca72db9c419267359c667a518f8a9a38d: 4 - that living together proves to be the union that unites all Montrealers, regardless of their skin colour, ethnic origin or religion;
entries.252eaa51ea6c13556bbceef7d26b749ac6bf3a5e: 5 - that the City of Montreal reaffirm itself as a city with a policy of access to municipal services without fear;
entries.a26cc5bf3b453ac4b4546451ac20afb129b246db: 6 - that the City of Montreal requires the exemplaryness of all central services and boroughs in establishing healthy, safe and non-racist and discriminatory working environments for all employees of the City.
entries.3a0cb44ad100eb16cefd773aa7373764856063b0: Whereas the 27th Week of Action against Racism and Equal Opportunities (SACR) will be held from 21 to 31 March 2026 under the theme "Resisting and Uniting: Rethinking tomorrow's society together";
entries.7a933722b0a773c278ccd368e8ec66c03b02b2b3: Whereas the Week of Action against Racism and for Equal Opportunities was established in 2000 to mark the International Day for the Elimination of Racial Discrimination, proclaimed by the General Assembly of the United Nations;
entries.5e558a668e0d61c39c744e784687e4edbbd2ad1c: Whereas the Second International Decade for People of African Descent 2025-2034 calls for the elimination of racial discrimination and respect for the diversity of Afrodescendant peoples and their undeniable contribution to the development of humanity;
entries.fa82be842d7db1a8da1ea8d7f0905c30110adc64: Whereas the main objective of SACR is to prevent and combat exclusion based in particular on skin colour and ethnic or national origin, by proposing activities that promote informed public dialogue about racism and diversity and that aim at bringing together all persons living in Quebec, regardless of their origin, whether they are first peoples or from immigration;
entries.c3eec97250b6292ef9dc7d43147a16e084d5d7d3: Whereas there has been a resurgence of racist violent acts throughout the world and the situation requires constant vigilance;
entries.f62917503d8c61601b36284cd19d1da97c80e052: Whereas Article 2 of the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities states that the dignity of the human being cannot be safeguarded without constantly and collectively combating poverty as well as all forms of discrimination, including on grounds of ethnic or national origin, colour, age, social condition, civil status, language, religion, sex, sexual orientation or disability;
entries.1cfbf58a8984b376d23c8252bdfb78b4052236a5: Whereas on March 21, 1989, the City of Montreal adopted the Montreal Declaration against Racial Discrimination to take all necessary measures to combat discrimination based in particular on race, colour, religion and ethnic or national origin and to promote harmonious racial and intercultural relations with respect and understanding;
entries.957e123182363b5ae9b99e094cd34b0b6cf9828d: Whereas Montreal is a city rich in its diversity, and that it must be continuously protected and valued through concrete actions promoting inclusion, living together and equal opportunities;
entries.0cc809b6ccb65fa07344d57cbfb15af7261a96dc: Whereas on 15 June 2020, the City Council adopted the Declaration to Recognize the Systemic Character of Racism and Discrimination and committed itself to combating them;
entries.1dc47ae0cb62fc20964a18f6c9791002dbbcebf1: Whereas the City of Montreal adopted, in 2020, following several years of cooperation and collaboration, the very first Strategy for Reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples and recognizes the millennial Aboriginal history of the Island of Montreal and the place that indigenous communities occupy in its cultural fabric;
entries.5af11bcc8a5e2a0a66fb015f36d642a2d4ccdd28: Whereas in April 2021, the City of Montreal amended its Montréal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities to incorporate the recognition of the systemic and intersectional nature of forms of discrimination and the endorsement of the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples in its preamble;
entries.d31403cf499948f3fc8c82651ac3460f5c1022d9: Whereas, since December 2023, the City of Montreal has been operating a Centrale d'accompaniment des personnel en matière de complaints.

entries.5d28d43fe115dbfc4d3197f589aa413984ebcdf2: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Arij El Korbi for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.8e0c3508822cc67b0359074aeae029cce819f716: At the outset, she highlighted the 27th Week against Racism and for Equal Opportunities, recalling the importance of thinking about our common history and the inequalities that persist despite our principles.
entries.ba41ed8ae91a1ec2a5e11e616638e0ad69b827be: It then stresses that it is the responsibility of elected officials to build a society where everyone lives in safety and dignity, through constant, concrete and measurable actions. Racism must never fuel stigma or populism, but encourage higher debate, better understanding and effective action against this scourge.
entries.cdd06b1c128d25ba90068f37d2447a28e351160c: In closing, Ms. El Korbi invited the public to participate in the activities organized within the framework of this 27th edition and thanked organizations and volunteers for their involvement, concluding by recalling that resisting racism remained a shared responsibility among all.
entries.918bb8c080518b7418caf38b5130980aa0211145: The President of the Council gave the floor consecutively to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus and the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada.
entries.49003f79680f60e836de1a62af293fea444fe700: For her part, Ericka Alneus highlights the first speech by Councillor Arij El Korbi, whom she considers to be a victory, especially for this declaration. She also salutes partner organizations and volunteers present. She recalls that every conversation can combat racist, Islamophobic and anti-Semitic discourses, as well as any form of discrimination. In her view, the dignity of each human being must guide the action of all elected people.
entries.72c377825f4b8809b9dc04b09f5858ff734b0ac1: The Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, joins her voice with those of her colleagues on the board, highlighting both the remarkable work done by the organizations and the richness of the journey that the City has built over the years in the fight against racism. However, she regrets that in 2026 it is still necessary to adopt such a declaration, which sadly reminds us that much remains to be accomplished.
entries.68b469a305762a1b0bb2c816b7b91092f8fec1fa: She then welcomed the dedication of partners, organizations and volunteers who had for so many years devoted themselves to combating racial injustices and believed that it was necessary to have the courage to recognize the continuing existence of this scourge, which still affected too many people through the manifestations of systemic racism, and above all we must seize the present moment to act.
entries.f1565bcd621b23f694c06cb1b48cb09dc7827554: In conclusion, the Mayor of Montreal reiterates that there is still an important road ahead and she hopes that everyone can live in a city offering dignity and respect and real equality of opportunity to the entire population. She recalls that this is a deeply collective commitment.
entries.391616706c388d0eaf87a9e3281a46f607442ec6: The Chair thanked the elected officials for their interventions and then confirmed the names of all members present on the City Council as supporters of this statement.
entries.80fc859d0b0db407f1489be7289848dd79f29819: 1 - expresses its solidarity with the Lebanese people and with the entire Lebanese community in Montreal at this particularly difficult time;
entries.3ee30a7218938446aea061772f5ed1bf7c2501a0: 2 - reaffirms its commitment to this relationship of friendship, solidarity and collaboration with the Lebanese community and continues its dialogue with it;
entries.04e33e0ecc555810faad34f3e8a9231d059b9419: 3 - reaffirms its support for efforts to promote de-escalation, dialogue, respect for international law and peace in the world.
entries.bca17c03fd26161e10da16658a5a021450cb1251: Whereas Lebanon has been drawn into the war in the Middle East and the Lebanese people are severely affected by the conflict;
entries.cccb1def090a35249ff332ebac1cf34b90a34ceb: Whereas, according to a provisional assessment, thousands of Lebanese civilians have been killed or injured, and more than 1 million Lebanese have been forced to travel within the country, including thousands of children;
entries.0df70d755e6f1dd8793e27adaebc37d8195ca67f: Whereas the international community calls for avoiding further escalation and constructive negotiations with a view to finding a lasting political solution;
entries.b5324aa326af3040816855b186f1c2d6fc997247: Whereas the hostilities taking place in Lebanese territory affect civilian populations and plunge the Lebanese people and their diaspora, particularly in Montreal, into a period of uncertainty, fear and sorrow;
entries.6b10d50e72f7742eccc91a9561b0d7d70d72fe2f: Whereas the Lebanese diaspora is an important part of the Arab-Canadian diaspora, with more than 400,000 Lebanese-Canadian people living in the country, half of whom live in Montreal and the major metropolitan area;
entries.2733b40b8f1b82b14dd8df44611a3ca94fd94012: Whereas Montreal recognizes the essential contribution of Montrealers of Lebanese origin, whose involvement and leadership bring undeniable dynamism to the economic, political, artistic, cultural, sporting and scientific spheres of the metropolis;
entries.f162020086dcc9d566ecfddab538ba38a8216d2c: Whereas the City of Montreal and the capital of Lebanon, Beirut, have for several years maintained a friendly relationship, sealed by the signing, in 2017, of an agreement of friendship and cooperation;
entries.c8ab525ac1eceb8ff9aa4cee36928c43ae473b6e: Whereas Montreal is a city of peace, a member of the international network of cities Mayors for Peace, and will continue to support any efforts aimed at achieving lasting global peace;

entries.7bcbc4ed7ce9aaf9add7f834a947973772bbdc7d: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Youssef Hariri for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.1f7fb1c90476a196a453d8f1c63946ccb3a58c68: First of all, Councillor Youssef Hariri recalls that in Montreal, the Lebanese community is numerous, committed and deeply rooted, contributing to the cultural, social and economic wealth of the City of Montreal for a long time. For him, Lebanon is more than one territory; it is also a land of history, diversity and coexistence, marked by centuries of civilizations and resilience. He mentions, inter alia, that today this country is going through an extremely difficult period, hit by war, bombing, loss of life and the displacement of hundreds of thousands of people. Mr. Hariri indicates that many Lebanese families in Montreal are living in mourning and anguish, while their loved ones are suffering destruction, exile and dramatic conditions of survival.
entries.9533de7ce47ab0606e712176bcdabfa0e5d57191: In conclusion, he stressed the need to put an end to war, respect international law and recognize every person as a citizen of humanity. With the solidarity of all, he was convinced that despite the darkness of war, peace and justice would eventually triumph.
entries.b423ea46c18f519fe5a6cca64f45196fd3ce7b07: The Chair gave the floor to Councillor Céline-Audrey Beauregard and Councillor Aref Salem respectively.
entries.85fc0604f4470b6dd8b1115b71811f4f3ca32639: From the outset, Councillor Céline-Audrey Beauregard denounces the continuing violence in Lebanon, recalling that this country has gone through many periods of war and divisions throughout its history. She reports, among other things, the indiscriminate brutality of the attacks and the death of innocent people unrelated to the conflict. She expresses the hope that one day Lebanon will again be associated with its gastronomy, landscapes, historic cities like Byblos and a resilient and welcoming people. Mrs Beauregard concludes by inviting members of the council to join their voices in this Declaration in solidarity with the Lebanese people.
entries.ae2eafed21555d21d1cd16f7989d72096ae21d17: In turn, Councillor Aref Salem expressed his support for this declaration, which revived in him the memories of a childhood and adolescence marked by war and loss of loved ones. Like many Lebanese of his generation, he was among those who had left Lebanon and compared it with uprooted trees, replanted in new soil to restore a calm, stable and peaceful environment. He recalled that wars did not only cause material destruction, but mainly loss of human life, while nearly 3,500 people had died or injured in Lebanon. Finally, Mr Salem expressed the hope of lasting peace for Lebanon and for the entire Middle East.
entries.58cc62ef38e26e33dc70d3e0789cb56d4852c8a8: The Chairperson thanked the members of the Board for their interventions and then confirmed the names of all the members present on the City Council as supporters of this Declaration.
entries.b175512afa3c2ed147bb90b15f179afa658e278d: 1 - highlights the contributions of the Irish community to the economic, cultural, social and artistic development of Montreal;
entries.fcf112c7249a6c75708a4b90dd52e9335e39499b: 2 - pay tribute to her and acknowledge that she is one of the founding peoples of Montreal, as represented on her flag;
entries.51f9c87d6498e51206596b875dd341b44f3513c0: 3 - attests, through the annual St. Patrick's parade in Montreal, to respect for Irish origins in Montréal history and the sense of metropolis festival;
entries.767fa4bedfb51950f201d38fdfbefb6b627d5c6b: 4 - highlights the work of the United Irish Societies of Montreal for nearly 100 years, which help keep Irish culture alive in Montreal and perpetuates the tradition of the parade that has lasted more than 200 years to the delight of hundreds of thousands of spectators.
entries.6bf6f94a05cee4ada7199c3ad58e92f55b929e23: Whereas Irish workers played a key role in the construction of essential infrastructure in Montreal, including the Lachine Canal (1821-1825) and the Victoria Bridge (1854-1859), thus contributing to the industrial and commercial development of the city;
entries.2753e8ad78247d335e45e57b97a76c4290336b99: Whereas the Irish community has been involved in the growth of many neighbourhoods in Montreal, such as the Southwest, founded by visionary entrepreneur Mary Griffin, where thousands of Irish people have chosen to settle and continue to live today;
entries.f6b61d0b693fcc82a02a0eace8e31d48283195a4: Whereas the major contributions of the Irish community in Montreal were highlighted, inter alia, by the addition of the Irish clover on the flag and coat of arms of Montreal, as a sign of respect for and recognition of our common history;
entries.9aa8542d95626205ac5f14d0f6b571a1193eee6b: Whereas the Black Rock Historic Monument, located at the foot of the Victoria Bridge in the Pointe-Saint-Charles area, commemorates the death of more than 6,000 immigrants of Irish origin who were victims of typhus between 1847 and 1848, and that an Irish Monument Park in Montreal is currently being prepared for an opening in 2029;
entries.678bcc4beb7b21da392423279e8c9843f1d1d515: Whereas the Irish community of Montreal has given birth to several major political figures that have marked the country's political history;
entries.7955cc99095bdadc5766fdbed72cc8b3c149f884: Whereas the 201st St. Patrick's parade, held on March 22, 2026 in downtown Montreal, is an event that marks the beginning of a new century of Irish heritage in the metropolis;
entries.a51b14142b4191c282811b9ebd010099c3351154: Whereas the first St. Patrick's parade in Montreal took place on March 17, 1824, making it the oldest in Canada and one of the largest in the world;
entries.49f363dd6a5a42551ae88413ea4b1185c9c2455c: Whereas this event attracts thousands of participants, as well as hundreds of thousands of spectators of all ages, who attend the travelling show of allegorical tanks, bandes and artists celebrating Irish culture;
entries.738dd099440a133c5269ffaa3c13df61865cd9a0: Whereas the parade is organized by the United Irish Societies of Montreal, an organisation created in 1928 whose work extends to the selection of the Grand Marshal and the queens of the parade, as well as to support Irish studies and children's charities;

entries.f8aaee5b3793fb9c888f345ef7f09e7c5c8b91e2: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Leslie Roberts for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.6a574e7f55e70e31b87373e6a540f062e37f8e8a: From the outset, Councillor Leslie Roberts highlighted the decisive contribution of Irish workers and families to the building of Montreal, particularly through their role in structuring projects such as the Lachine Canal and the Victoria Bridge. He also highlighted the symbolic significance of Black Rock and the future commemorative park, which aimed at preserving the memory of thousands of immigrants who had died from typhus in 1847. Roberts emphasized the resilience and founding spirit of this community, illustrated in particular by the St Patrick's parade that brought together a large audience annually. Finally, he thanked the Irish organizations in Montreal for their constant work and their contribution to the cultural and social vitality of the metropolis.
entries.d7ee35df9bf47003044d267e38f8a828b55fa0fb: The Chair gave the floor to Councillors Sterling Downey, Peter McQueen and Véronique Fournier respectively.
entries.7f2f7fb1e416aeda4b01e11ba184e079cb1a6456: Counselor Sterling Downey first mentioned that Irish Heritage Month and the St. Patrick's parade set out the historical and cultural importance of the Irish community in Montreal. He then greeted the resilience of Irish immigrants who had arrived during the Great Famine, as well as the solidarity gestures of groups such as Aboriginal communities and Grey Sisters and former Mayor John Easton Mills. Mr. Downey concluded by thanking the Irish volunteers and communities for preserving this heritage and supporting community life in Montreal and elsewhere.
entries.e0be01cd85af26d3a17a66a9b5a5e3fa57315951: For his part, Councillor Peter McQueen evokes the history of the Irish community of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce by linking his family journey to the various English-speaking parishes in the neighbourhood. He highlights the value of these churches as Irish community hubs over the decades. In closing, Mr. McQueen also thanks the Irish families and organizations in Montreal for their lasting commitment to community life here.
entries.c9a63afac500fa31f5ce4b6fc0a6cb578a427c5b: In summary, Councillor Véronique Fournier continues by recalling her visit to the Roche Noire Memorial, or Black Rock Memorial, with Irish representatives and local dignitaries. She then describes the symbolic reach of the Roche Noire and explains that this place occupies a prominent place in the project of the future park of the Irish monument of Montreal. She hopes that this place will become a space of inescapable memory and boasts the collaboration of volunteers and partners.
entries.ce23ce5e2ab453b29d0201716484714515cb27d0: 1 - that on April 13 and 14, 2026, the City of Montreal recognize Yom HaShoah, Day of Remembrance for All Victims of the Holocaust, in solidarity with survivors of this genocide and as a sign of vigilance to ensure that such crimes never happen again;
entries.968fa6104536ddbbff593450ddb2fcdd81c15b70: 2 - that the City of Montreal reaffirm its commitment to combat anti-Semitism, and that it strongly and unequivocally denounces any anti-Semitic gesture and attack against Jewish persons, their property and places, while reiterating that hateful acts do not belong in the metropolis;
entries.9f4a33a360691efcd7c6e2592f1af08321a43410: 3 - that the City of Montreal continue to raise public awareness against extremism and intolerance, as well as promote openness to others, listening, benevolence and solidarity, so that never again a tragedy like the Holocaust will occur.
entries.3feea41d4deb9d6c85bb4fb3b19297a5e6ea60b4: Whereas Shoah Victims Remembrance Day, Yom Shoah, will be celebrated from 13 to 14 April 2026;
entries.82559951709448b2b01e0e5a9839d09c8ce8a214: Whereas the Shoah, i.e. the systematic extermination of Jewish communities in Europe by Nazi Germany and its collaborators, marked the history of humanity with the singularity of its horror;
entries.5a26fbcd5c7a8502ce2b66e862d777973624c3d3: Whereas six million Jewish people were victims of the Holocaust during World War II, creating one of the darkest chapters in history;
entries.72f945c7b46845a5742ce6292ff033d9d5519c30: Whereas after the Second World War, Montreal became the host city of more than 30,000 survivors of the Shoah, who actively contributed to the development and outreach of the metropolis;
entries.b3d094de1d1233f07e49efd006dfde9dfea92d85: Whereas Montreal is the third largest city in the world with the most survivors of the Holocaust;
entries.e3a32e23448a251a3c90f6c35b052efadbaf3fcf: Whereas the City of Montreal proclaimed, on March 25, 2002, Yom HaShoah the Day of Remembrance for All Victims of the Holocaust and undertook to mark this commemorative day on a recurring basis;
entries.70012d8fa32fc969294eba5678d172f4469589d3: Whereas, in memory of the genocides of the twentieth century and their victims, the memorial La réparation was erected in 1998 at the corner of Henri-Bourassa Boulevards and Acadia, in the district of Ahuntsic-Cartierville;
entries.d58e13b4e291c603d21cbe487bd7a64baa34fd3b: Whereas the City of Montreal has financially supported the construction of the Montreal Holocaust Museum;
entries.69f6213c6477df4985454d65e4708d5552e605c1: Whereas Yom HaShoah encourages never to forget the Holocaust and to remain vigilant and vigilant against all forms of prejudice and hatred, so that no more such atrocities are committed;

entries.7c29b5c1ff52e60768934bf1f9c9b2451e74bf89: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Sonny Moroz for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.7eddfb95c8e97bdafed43115c2bc59ab797ac9a6: First of all, Councillor Sonny Moroz greets the people present on the balcony and affirms that the Declaration for Shoah Victims Remembrance Day represents a day of memory. Among other things, he believes it is important to remember because when we forget our history, it repeats itself. He points out that more than six million Jewish people were exterminated during the Holocaust in just a few years. Moroz also refers to the Babi Yar massacre and specifies that this site was once again affected during the Russian aggression war started in 2022.
entries.816fa0d3b6e5e5fa1ef9f220a1a903cda9e210b9: Subsequently, Councillor Moroz indicated that Montreal had been home to the largest number of Jewish survivors and that it was today the third world home for these people still alive. Finally, Mr. Moroz is relying on educational actions and our institutions to understand and honour this story.
entries.9cba580ae6184a4a50f972d1f3c52e23ae30559f: The Chair of the Board gave the floor consecutively to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus and Councillor Émilie Brière.
entries.442642824b51cad3b5ee36f14c6e6db6f97d5312: Ms. Ericka Alneus began by joining Mr. Moroz's voice and also greeted the guests present, recalling the importance of remembering this tragedy which has profoundly affected human history, including that Montreal is fortunate enough to host the Holocaust Museum on St. Lawrence Boulevard, a place marked by the historical implantation of the Jewish community, visible in particular through Yiddish inscriptions on certain buildings. The Chief of the Official Opposition concluded by reaffirming the need for this exercise of memory, stressed zero tolerance against anti-Semitism and reiterated that "never again" must be declared.
entries.2dc9e16d4f33890f9ea5d6757f0af979eb8f52cc: In summary, counselor Émilie Brière points out that in Montreal this day is dedicated to the commemoration of the victims of the Shoah and to the tribute paid to the six million Jewish people murdered by the Nazi regime, as well as to all other persons persecuted and killed on account of their identity or beliefs. Ms. Brière stresses that the Shoah demonstrates how far racism, dehumanization and indifference can lead, fuelled by prejudice, trivialization of hatred and silence. She concludes by calling for vigilance, denouncing hate speech, defending human rights and the duty of memory transmitted through education, dialogue and commitment, in order to build a more just, inclusive and deeply humane Montreal society for future generations.
entries.98e858afac2a880f3b00a20683f031410f9cc120: The Chair thanked the three elected for their interventions and then confirmed the names of all members present on the City Council as supporters of this Declaration.
entries.c0e75718ef2c30b81b26fc32ddd6564bcf8242aa: 1 - highlights the International Visibility Day transgenderes on 31 March and raises public awareness of the importance of combating all forms of discrimination against trans persons;
entries.a0f5d6672fbde483bbaba02699f5c443881ed912: 2 - continue to defend the rights of trans persons and persons of sexual or gender diversity;
entries.71e3be46f255753921567762cea45bdc8bc4a53c: 3 - Continue to provide training for municipal and police personnel, as well as develop awareness-raising tools and guidelines to improve the integration of gender diversity communities within its services and those in the boroughs through the application of ADS+;
entries.af9beeb5e53500faf4dc687ba9f74bc4b511fd07: 4 - commits itself to combating all forms of transphobic discrimination and violence in the public space, supporting community-based prevention initiatives and drawing on good practices in policies and municipal commitments towards LGBTQIA2S+ communities.
entries.4a5b773cc802981a6e8032ac0f6108a820161b5c: Whereas International Transgender Visibility Day takes place on March 31 of each year and was created by American activist Rachel Crandall-Crocker in 2009 in response to the lack of LGBTQIA2S+ celebration day dedicated to trans people;
entries.64a7a5bb0cf7006b7fcff568dd5acee84532bb93: Whereas a decline in the rights of trans persons is observed in several countries of the world, trans people are experiencing a prevalence of street harassment and violence in public places, and data confirm an alarming increase in transphobia;
entries.07b51858cc6c421d1ec966b257568941a7bea691: Whereas all citizens of the City of Montreal enjoy the fundamental rights proclaimed and guaranteed in 1975 by the Charter of Human Rights and Freedoms of Quebec and the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms adopted in 1982;
entries.394fbec1968a6f698cc30f06241615a3530ca2dc: Whereas the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities, adopted in 2005, includes a commitment to combat all forms of discrimination, including those related to gender diversity, and that this commitment has included since 2021 discrimination based on gender identity and expression, including transphobia;
entries.588170d06945b0cf2dd5d067a0189a686a3e3f2c: Whereas the City of Montreal adopted, in 2007, the Montreal Declaration on the Rights of Gay, Lesbian, Bisexual and Transgender Persons, proclaimed at the closing of the International Conference on LGBT Rights, held in Montreal in 2006;
entries.17c2670744ad88b7c2f40bc2c1ab784387077d58: Whereas the City of Montreal recognizes the importance of the work done by organizations working to support, accompany, equip, defend and represent trans people;
entries.51791a5d446956c1ff366aab05ab01dd3066c71a: Whereas the City of Montreal supports many community-based initiatives supporting communities of gender diversity that are more vulnerable and at risk of social exclusion, such as support groups for parents and close friends of children and young people who are creative in the genre, security activities for LGBTQIA2S+ Aboriginal youth and support projects for LGBTQIA2S+ migrants or refugees;
entries.d0ef9da1f75adf28825e0cb9da06abe3622b861e: Whereas the City of Montreal is contributing to many cultural initiatives that highlight and celebrate LGBTQIA2S+ communities, such as Fierté Montréal, Pride Literary and Pride Trans festivals;

entries.90ff0ce9d15ad9e751d078db48824cdd229c62d1: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Claude Pinard for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.4f2812e53203dd8b5f2cb1abdadec68cdcdd7407: At the outset, Councillor Claude Pinard was of the opinion that March 31, International Trans Visibility Day, was an opportunity to celebrate the richness of trans journeys and identities. He pointed out that Montreal was a welcoming city where every person could live in dignity and security, but noted that the rights of people were changing in several regions of the world. Mr. Pinard continued by noting that discrimination was increasing, that hateful demonstrations had recently taken place and that trans people remained particularly affected by homelessness and the housing crisis, which required vigilance and action on all sides.
entries.2241446d19b548c8cca974d079bd590002bb9240: Subsequently, Mr. Pinard highlighted the essential role of community organizations for the City and referred to funding issues for them, while indicating that the Authority supported their projects and increased resources allocated for the year 2026. He concluded by welcoming the courage of trans people, thanking agencies for their work and inviting board members to adopt the declaration.
entries.c80bb217746a8626e2520f2309a1995b0fa70761: The Chair gave the floor to the Deputy Leader of the Official Opposition, Christopher McCray.
entries.f2ad7591fbf88b56cfe5058c4146c1e4c8f159b6: In turn, he welcomed the organizations present and recalled that the first statement on International Trans Visibility Day had been adopted a year earlier, in a context marked by significant setbacks in the rights of trans people, both in the United States and Canada. He went on to highlight the increase in hate acts, the rise in calls to Interline and the presence of political speeches deemed dangerous. He believed that elected persons were responsible for being exemplary and that Montreal should reaffirm its support for trans people. The Deputy Leader of the Official Opposition thanked the Administration for its openness in this common approach. Finally, he reiterated that visibility and support were essential to ensure the dignity, security and inclusion of trans people.
entries.65de698955880a11ab86bf14ff3b53f90f079774: The President of the Council gave the floor to Councillor Benoit Langevin and the Chief of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, who joined with this Declaration in order to highlight the work of community organizations and express the City of Montreal's commitment to combat all forms of discrimination.
entries.68ef2d5e4b0dde32a590b83ba69a31c379cd6b0f: The Chair thanked the four elected for their interventions and then confirmed the names of all members present on the City Council as supporters of this Declaration.
