entries.5b862761a7dde63bfd0c30bc67dad21d7ea22c2d: 1- that the City of Montreal reaffirm that any decision on mobility and road safety must be based on evidence, in accordance with the motion unanimously adopted by the City Council on February 16, 2026;
entries.9e1d144edf88e92452d5eccb0699add4770ab5c4: 2- that the City of Montreal conduct a new audit of the arteries and intersections identified as presenting high risks based on consolidated collision analyses, so as to ensure that priority interventions truly target the most dangerous areas, whether for persons travelling on foot, by bicycle or by car;
entries.5aa2d33b33427f70368efdba35ae262d3d130235: 3- that the City of Montreal compare, in a public statement, the bicycle routes subject to the announced audits and the intersections recognized as presenting significant risks, to ensure alignment between intervention priorities and objective data;
entries.5a6634891e8473afc608a8a680de66af03f499ad: 4- that the Urban Planning and Mobility Service be mandated to integrate all available safety data – including collisions, severity of incidents, modal share of modes of transport and documented risks – into a uniform decision-making grid that will guide future interventions;
entries.f6a3d6460347c0fdddfadaa74ce836189a11c4b8: 5- that the City of Montreal prioritize security interventions at intersections and on arteries presenting the highest risks, including measures to appease, reduce usage conflicts and improve visibility;
entries.494817a7619872aef0a4ffeb0a5db46e236dfff6: 6- that the City of Montreal submit to the City Council, within six months, a consolidated report presenting:
entries.9109a206eaee7198bfe93fdd785d1baedf1271e8: Whereas the City Council of Montreal unanimously adopted on February 16, 2026 a motion reaffirming that public decisions, particularly with regard to urban planning, mobility and road safety, must be guided by science, evidence and recognized best practices;
entries.4fc410a745d33eaa53759c65637dacb7b45e0572: Whereas the same motion stresses that ignoring recommendations from rigorous analysis undermines user safety, the credibility of public institutions and the City's ability to effectively address mobility and security issues;
entries.72ba6ac22defd19b89b912b11089c8adc78092f8: Whereas the municipal administration has recently announced targeted audits on certain cycle paths, based on criteria such as registered collisions and citizen complaints, in order to improve the safety of existing and future developments;
entries.f4aa80b39ad96d6d56af707daaa4a1f620c481ee: Whereas these audits aim to examine bicycle routes considered problematic by the administration, in particular due to issues of visibility, conflicts between users and local conditions which deserve a thorough reassessment;
entries.4eaff321ad079d94109150b536c5d31c2af342b9: Whereas the analysis of consolidated data on road collisions in Montreal also identifies several intersections and sections of streets presenting particularly high risks to user safety, all modes, and whereas these places also require priority attention according to the principles promoted by the scientific motion adopted by the Council;
entries.d2b8c8ab3a75ec14684d26d8f9ba84f11bdc1bb3: Whereas according to a study led by researchers at Polytechnique Montréal, in collaboration with INRS and Université Laval, published in August 2024, the majority of streets and intersections in Montreal present a high risk of collision for pedestrians, especially children;
entries.3df4c8cec98a06af289591d67f28bbe8c9f73a7e: Whereas, according to the City of Montreal's Zero Vision 2025-2027 Action Plan, three out of four collisions with death or serious injury occur at one intersection and nine in ten collisions with death or serious injury occur on a blood street or collector;
entries.6236bc11ca285cafe84e6e2097c9f0cdf647db4a: Whereas the consistency between the principles adopted by the Council - to base public decisions on science - and the concrete actions of the City requires that audits and re-evaluations take into account all areas with significant risks, including those identified by the most recent collision analyses;
entries.6e360790032d7d87a2fb08207147c3ab286ef9d9: The Chair of Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, the Deputy Leader of the Official Opposition, Christopher McCray, for his presentation.
entries.962cda2ab27543be51a6ff812c16a6ff0dd1c6d7: In terms of mobility and road safety, Mr. McCray began by advocating the expansion of the announced audits to include dangerous streets and intersections, with evidence from Vélo-Québec indicating that almost all cyclist deaths occur on streets without safe accommodation. He also outlined statistics on deaths and seriously injured people in Montréal, stating that 50% of this group was moving in motorized vehicles and 40% on foot. He supported his comments with figures from the City's Vision Zero Action Plan. In conclusion, McCray hoped that internal expertise and academic experts would be used to ensure consistency in the Administration's priority interventions by targeting the most hazardous areas, whether for persons travelling on foot, by bicycle or by car.
entries.bbc01a4765d886dcaafa0c593e911b10a044e098: The President thanked him and gave the floor respectively to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde, and to Councillor Sylvain Ouellet.
entries.0235591d225cea94b2c1489c562cb65f10ddb2bf: Both agreed to improve sustainable mobility in Montreal. They stressed, among other things, the importance of taking priority actions such as safe accommodations for all people on foot, by bike, by car, travelling on streets and arteries identified as dangerous in Montreal.
entries.c9d0d01c5acbdf55e2ade6181d3db03888dba56d: The Authority's representative for this matter, Councillor Alan DeSousa, spoke on the motion, stating in particular that the Administration would not vote in favour of it. He explained that the Authority agreed with several statements made in previous arguments. However, he pointed out that the City's planning took these issues into account, notably in Vision Zero 2025-2027, which the Authority would not make changes to and based on which steps were taken. He concluded by pointing out that the actions under way were based on the same objectives and obligations as the motion under consideration.
entries.561e178dbaebcca0e6ec4d5c9e7e217eb7293b1d: The Chair thanked them for their interventions and gave the right of reply to the Deputy Leader of the Official Opposition, Christopher McCray.
entries.e20701694046ff8a77cbadc6e0d21839f9f78c1f: to take a recorded vote on item 65.01.
entries.bbb5e288b4e7620b276711189a37445299c59e9e: the City Council reaffirms that the permanent closure of the former Lachin marina is maintained in order to ensure the complete transformation of the site into a riparian park accessible to all Lachinese and Lachinese;
entries.5f76a2ea4e074e628097aca343d815af43e38ea1: 1 - confirms its commitment to continue the planned work and development, including the final removal of obsolete infrastructure and the establishment of announced facilities, with a view to fully opening up the riparian park as soon as possible;
entries.71a56ad5abaf51721f776173c8a0b154888b88b9: 2 - reaffirms the principle of universal access to banks, and therefore any plans for future development or revision of the site exclude privatization, motorization or any initiative that restricts public access;
entries.2c7ca939fa28496faef2f54d1f69f5f6a4d4db65: 3 - undertakes to maintain a transparent and inclusive dialogue with the public, including community and environmental organizations, in order to ensure that the development meets the real needs of the Lachinese community;
entries.3bf93db27dc25873e24034a60837295ebf873c57: 4 - mandate the administration concerned to produce an annual report on the progress of development, the state of access to the banks, uses of the riparian park and needs for improvement, and that this report be made public.
entries.31ba5711c423de24241ccb18200c63fd7d08fafc: Whereas public access to the banks is an essential collective asset for Lachinese and Lachinese, allowing recreational activities, active transport, enhancement of riparian landscapes and strengthening the community link;
entries.6d06bc5e4d86dfc9a56cf5845bd1ebca2da39a3f: Whereas the closure of the Lachine marina in 2020, and its gradual transformation into a riparian park, was explicitly aimed at "making the banks accessible to all" according to the municipal administration;
entries.46266d2b392ca3b6a295c2f5c7debdf58c332056: Whereas the City of Montreal confirmed, in 2025, the deconstruction of the old marina's obsolete infrastructure to prepare for the development of a large water park accessible to the public, consistent with its objective of democratizing access to water for non-motorized water sports and bathing activities;
entries.d557c94afdcf256f19226eba5886b9bc91974e0d: Whereas, despite some challenges from boaters, a significant part of the local community has for several years been supporting the transformation of the site into a public space, in particular in the name of better access to the riverbank for the general population and environmental concerns associated with the presence of hundreds of motorized boats;
entries.5ab5de06027eba132c5ebd7c6168aa8229b59d58: Whereas the closure of the marina has been the subject of an important public debate, but that in 2025 the City reaffirmed its intention to move forward with the project, thus marking a decisive step towards releasing the site and making it fully accessible to all;
entries.1d77e5eb5dcf0d87c399bebafd5229acabd0c248: Whereas new administrations, both at the central and borough levels, are now in place and there is a need to clarify their position regarding the future of the site and the continuation of the riparian park project;
entries.9ca2af43a967522af9f2e5c28ded93b7d4dbc7a9: Whereas the development of a riparian park in Lachine represents a unique opportunity to consolidate an accessible, safe and inclusive natural space that meets the needs of the present and future community;
entries.57155d697e24bde73b15dc63457be4a49539c1b7: Whereas major measures to protect and strengthen the banks are planned to counter erosion, which receive $40 million from the federal government in addition to a contribution from the Great Parks;
entries.e2c1dc5beade04ccf291501b8270a61af52ce171: Whereas the water body in a low current area adjacent to the site is an exceptional place for learning and practicing non-motorized water sports - rowing, paddleboarding, sailing, canoeing/kayak - and is used by hundreds of people each year;
entries.22b9969545606bb7c09c7c5b6fb4402b328778b3: Whereas several of the former marina docks are now optimally used by the Lachine Sailing School, enabling the support and structure of non-motorized water activities on site;
entries.1a71081a3d1f9debf98503643eb327112cc1a431: The Chair of the Board, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, Councillor Danielle Myrand, for her presentation.
entries.f30b07ab23df6413c52da63a58313813d4655165: To begin with, Ms. Myrand boasts the benefits and the chance of this access to water in the Lachine district by insisting on the historic opportunity to preserve, restore and make it fully public over a distance of twelve kilometres from the banks. She supports, among other things, the collective desire for more inclusive and safe contact with water within a less private and less motorized area. With the ongoing process of transforming the site and democratizing access to water, she believes that it is essential to maintain an open dialogue where people will be involved, heard and respected. Finally, she presents a plea about all these water sports that can be offered to young people and families, in a safe area, citing the example of the sailing school. She hopes that the Administration will commit itself today to continuing the planned work and development.
entries.ee9d07bd6e539ff8a15be1047b73716837e8a541: The Chair thanked her and gave the floor consecutively to Councillors Céline-Audrey Beauregard and Catherine Houbart. In turn, the two Councillors mentioned, among other things, climate issues such as increasing the number of heat waves, making it necessary to increase access to the banks in order to support Montreal's population during these extreme heat episodes, and they hoped that all members of the Board would come into tune with this motion.
entries.dc636d7170e3d9791e54c0a58f8718201d2de0c0: The Chair thanked them and gave the floor to the Authority's representative for this matter, Councillor Julie-Pascale Provost.
entries.2c54d8c5c7239475774df3eea7562abd2e3f1a9b: First of all, Ms. Provost pointed out that this issue was not a priority for the Lachine District at this time, and added that, despite the polarization generated by this project and the division it engenders within the Lachine community, she understood the impatience of everyone. In addition, she undertook to mobilize resources in order to carry out an in-depth analysis of the site, to listen to the expectations of residents and to build a grouping, structuring and producing positive and lasting benefits for the entire territory of Montreal. In conclusion, she invited Council members to vote against the motion.
entries.034bb778490765667a23eeb06c51b254b12aafa3: The President thanked Ms Provost for her speech and invited the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde, to speak.

entries.1ce9e7a0ec6408073126f987f2d25b78943ed3ae: 1 - that the City of Montreal celebrates International Women's Rights Day on March 8, 2026, and continues to combat inequality every day through its various programs and policies;
entries.7513e2e65b776ab935e516d780195e984604eb50: 2 - that the Montréal administration continue its initiatives on work-family reconciliation within the City, as well as its initiatives to promote the full participation of all women in all spheres of Montreal life and ensure their safety.
entries.bcf03685c7dd8cf722b03d29c568b83444de0ad0: 3. Continues its support to community-based organizations dedicated to women in its territory, including emergency shelter centres for women in vulnerable situations;
entries.b9a7c2bf6ece4b048cf57bb015414799ca1d5184: 4. Continue to support community-based initiatives to prevent gender-based violence and promote egalitarian relations, and accelerate the deployment of ADS+ within the municipal apparatus to create an ever more egalitarian and inclusive city;
entries.36c71f316dea5cd4b2f290c764aa4ee746cc11f4: 5. Reiterates the importance of continuing the fight for equality, justice and respect for the human rights of all women.
entries.61a3b087bb7b5549acc4c43db9669bda97fdedc0: Whereas the International Women's Rights Day is held annually on 8 March, and has as its theme in 2026 "Rights. Justice. Action. For ALL women and girls";
entries.2d9f9779ed37c82f318580a24c45cb84b52ad3e1: Whereas the second quarter of the 21st century begins when equality between women and men is not achieved;
entries.e99bd7c8c2e8bea3cfad351cac6b7111875f0af0: Whereas women enjoy only 64 per cent of the legal rights enjoyed by men worldwide in fundamental areas, such as work, money, security, family, property, mobility and retirement, since the law systematically disadvantages women;
entries.ab07913a0e2abeba26ac991c4c113d5313e59f67: Whereas, at the same time as legal progress continues, according to UN Women, it will take 286 years to bridge disparities in legal protection between women and men, which is tantamount to capitulation;
entries.ac37822f105a791f7c255492feba0d4827b879fb: Whereas, according to the report on femicide 2025 of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and UN Women, based solely on the data recorded, more than 60 per cent of the 83,000 women intentionally killed in 2024 on the planet died under the blows of their intimate partner or close family, i.e. a woman or girl every 10 minutes;
entries.ce50db9f2e0018a20964946566988df43f667829: Whereas women and girls are subjected to femicide in all regions of the world, and six femicides have been registered in Quebec since the beginning of 2026;
entries.16eb4e533e76826665ed5f4e67785d8dcfc29589: Whereas, according to Statistics Canada and the Ministère de la Santé et des Services sociaux du Québec, more women are still subjected to violence, living in poverty and earning lower wages, despite equivalent skills, and that racialized, immigrant, refugee, disabled, elderly, Aboriginal or LGBTQIA2S+ women are more likely to suffer systemic discrimination;
entries.11cc0315af53a09948b4d374928d238d3c879cca: Whereas homeless women remain particularly vulnerable and at increased risk of violence, including physical, sexual and psychological violence;
entries.35a06e3e28b9668bbfb64455847180ebdafa8fcb: Whereas, in order to develop policies and programmes that achieve equality and parity, it is essential, from an intersectional perspective, that the bodies implementing them fully reflect the society they represent;
entries.937448af5b1a006092d5108b3f93f9f15644c7ea: Whereas the City of Montreal continues to deploy gender-based analysis from an intersectional perspective (ADS+), which is the internationally recognized approach to preventing and correcting inequalities between women and men, and among all women;
entries.660563e9caf166dd721b7c8f639d871abfa47e3b: Whereas the City of Montreal can count on the support of the Conseil des Montréaliennes and many community partners as well as members of civil society to advance women's rights and improve their living conditions in the metropolis;
entries.607943a5d66f0e241126bef050f0343e722244c9: Whereas the Table des groupes de femmes de Montréal, supported by the City of Montreal, enables projects and initiatives to promote equality between women and men;
entries.bbf3280baec7c75f29fe3909e273ca78b0c59fc4: Whereas the Fédération des femmes du Québec is conducting an awareness campaign entitled "Generations poissate" in tribute to the newspaper "Québécois poissatte", which was published more than 50 years ago by activists of the Front de libération des femmes du Québec in a context of questioning the social system of the sexes and patriarchal violence against women;
entries.dfe4b65b0a567643e79762eb63e6f7b6baa68185: Whereas the theme of International Women's Law Day 2026 is a call for action to remove obstacles to fair justice, such as discriminatory laws, lack of legal protections and harmful social practices and norms that undermine the rights of women and girls;
entries.b7ac4f46a6038574442158ca569bbda1bcebc6eb: Peter McQueen Catherine Houbart Olivier Demers-Dubé Danielle Myrand Elvira Carhuallanqui Émilie Brière Maeva Vilain Sterling Downey Élise Tanguay Céline-Audrey Beauregard Nancy Blanchet Richard Deschamps Laura Palestini Andrée Henault
entries.050dac5b6fb5afb2425c3c43718bc81177a67a24: First of all, the Mayor of Montreal mentions the global recognition of International Women's Rights Day, which recalls that the fight for equality remains essential. As the City Council will not be sitting by March 8, Ms. Martinez Ferrada would like to highlight this day now. The struggle for rights is progressing through a daily, shared and constant commitment. The theme "Right. Justice. Action. For All." reflects the breadth of the road ahead.
entries.9da2a6607e3ccdf0ffa8c31c416ce7fbb886ff7e: Moreover, still alarming, the reality of inequality persists: on average, women reach only about 60% of real equality, and estimates project 286 years before full equality becomes a reality. The right to abortion is receding in several regions of the world. Also in Quebec, gender-based attacks (and especially on social networks) are aimed at reducing the position of women in public spaces.
entries.e520b3da5f7b4bed3b34c51c681f6bbba7576c1e: Equally deeply disturbing, the situation of violence against women requires a strong response. Since the beginning of the year, six femicides have been identified in Quebec. Every ten minutes, a woman is subjected to violence. The call is therefore launched to redouble efforts, break silence and improve access to resources, especially in shelters. The achievements remain fragile and must be constantly protected.
entries.890325f38fc3cff84830f3b035f0e48ac2b353e6: Recognizing the commitment of many elected representatives, the Mayor of Montreal thanked Ericka Alneus, leader of the Official Opposition, for her contribution and invited the entire city council to support this declaration. She concluded by saying that progress requires vigilance and determination.
entries.53df046b7a3ad660abc31e3bb59254a2a0ecddc1: The President of the Council gave the floor consecutively to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, Councillors Nathalie Goulet and Élise Tanguay, as well as to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde.
entries.ca36e49d6247b1026562f9a893013e3caf95317b: Wishing to preserve the memory of feminist struggles, Ms. Alneus stressed for her part the importance and the strong symbol of this declaration, paying tribute in particular to the groups that had shaped progress on equity. Half of the planet was made up of women, so it is our duty to denounce injustices against women, as with regard to abortion. The taking of positions by elected representatives represented a necessary gesture; an invitation was issued for all to support this statement.
entries.8c2347182fed1bc11809b08599cb860025840363: Counselor Nathalie Goulet, among other things, continues and emphasizes the importance of gender analysis in an intersectional perspective (ADS+). The examination of generation data and the development of cross-cutting strategies within the municipal apparatus are considered essential. As an employer, the City must also act in traditionally male settings, such as blue collars. Ms Goulet invites us to read about recent testimonies from women who live in these environments. In closing, she believes in the need for systemic change.
entries.10da128810c81a4c1a18d7e36fd710804f4d8503: Then, with a personal conviction, Councillor Élise Tanguay stressed that every act of violence against a woman affects all women. She was of the opinion that online attacks were conducive to the rise of systemic violence. She called for, inter alia, increased support for homeless women and hoped that everyone would show determination in this ongoing struggle. She concluded by saying that women did not constitute a minority, which gave them powers and responsibilities.
entries.f999c0c6d2804108226e75bfa080e0df440aadfd: Finally, aware of the growing concern, the leader of the Official Opposition, Marie Plourde, admits that she has sought reassuring words, but without success. In several parts of the world, women's rights are regressing "like a skin of grief." A recent chronicle illustrates how the inacceptable tends to become acceptable. Faced with the alarming number of femicides, immediate action is required, according to her. She affirms that this action must begin here, among colleagues, in the city council. In conclusion, Ms Plourde hopes that all elected officials will engage in a firm and lasting way for equality, justice and respect for the fundamental rights of all women.
entries.f81658d5b91a3356abdcde4b2c087a2d567dd051: 1 - Invites the entire population to celebrate the Month of La Francophonie in March;
entries.dc38113b26923387d268e6b0facdf0415ea478af: 2 - celebrates its status as a Francophone metropolis of the Americas and continues to promote its leadership in international networks for the promotion of the French language;
entries.2607751f1b64dd6ae960b7f285e618ebe2da55cc: 3 - celebrates the unifying character of the French language, the official and common language of the metropolis of Quebec;
entries.75918e59f405307479df5bcdb9d8315be7fc1095: 4 - continue the work begun in terms of valuing the French language and continue to encourage, every day, the use of this common language in all spheres of Montreal life.
entries.7ba99a48adc9dd5e5c64137d9903c571afbf08d2: Whereas the Mois de la Francophonie is held every year in March, and is an opportunity to celebrate and promote the French language throughout the world;
entries.b246523f86601ec90ac3bf06d0383f5c4f0e59ca: Whereas International Day of La Francophonie is celebrated on 20 March each year to celebrate the importance of the French language and the cultural diversity that exists in Francophone communities around the world;
entries.20b286a6f0344b8dccfadc1ec822a42fc3e24750: Whereas Montreal, the French-speaking metropolis of the Americas, is a cosmopolitan city, open to the world and inclusive, which celebrates French as an official and common language, pillar of its unique identity and vector of cohesion in public space;
entries.d660a09a02fc2b23b9fcd104ce673012f5065e9a: Whereas the City of Montreal is taking concrete steps to protect, promote and promote the French language in the Greater Metropolitan Area, as well as outside Quebec and internationally;
entries.c64091bf3d9ad6e75137f53a08a0d58f9a48299a: Whereas the City of Montreal has created the Office de la langue française, whose mandate is, among other things, to ensure the implementation of the provisions applicable to municipal governments provided for in the Act respecting the official and common language of Quebec, French, as well as to ensure that the action plan is implemented and to provide its strategic vision within the municipal apparatus;
entries.2e4b886f4775eaf2e4e0c758e1eff7dcee0cdfb8: Whereas the City of Montreal annually awards the Prix de la langue française to five recipients in order to recognize their involvement and excellence in their work on the promotion of the French language;
entries.ab063fe8bf69abe9f9a79c46664ff02f6c665fb2: Whereas the City of Montreal collaborates with its partners, including the Government of Quebec, the Office québécois de la langue française and community, economic, cultural and academic organizations, to make French the social link of the metropolis;
entries.68590e1930b4973c792ec1c55891cd49c992230b: Whereas the City of Montreal has set up a committee on the French language whose work led to the publication in 2024 of a second report, many of which are already in place or are in the process of being implemented;
entries.7e9fbaeb77d058386d5a8a2163637c882841dd6d: Whereas the City of Montreal, in collaboration with the Government of Quebec and the Réseau succes Montréal, supports the francization of young newcomers by working together with the day camps of the metropolis;
entries.ead00218bba7b847a89a710584ba3252e7db6719: Whereas the City of Montreal is developing programs within its facilities, such as libraries and cultural houses, aimed at enhancing the French language to the general public;
entries.ac953e75dfbd5e80583c078d4beb9e0fe0a99fcf: First of all, the Mayor of Montreal pointed out that the month of la Francophonie, which began in March, was of great importance to the Montreal community. She said that when she arrived in Canada, she did not speak French and that this language had shaped her identity as a Francophone Montrealer. Among other things, she said she was proud to be at the head of this great French-speaking metropolis in North America and to say that she was a woman who came out of law 101. She recalled this year's theme for Le Mois de la Francophonie: "Active ta francophonie", an appeal to get on the move, to meet, to gather together and to create opportunities to live the French language.
entries.d55985dd945211bdd5fa8698c1b75199c0e60fe4: In addition, Mrs. Martinez Ferrada boasts artists, authors from here and elsewhere, who have been able to give the Francophonie all its depth, diversity, modernity, wealth and audacity. She wishes to value the French language and believes in particular that it is our responsibility as a community to protect, promote and shine it. Ms. Martinez Ferrada concludes by inviting the population to create opportunities to live this language in various cultural and community places.
entries.313bdad4fd744ce0efb713f7776b33a3a4378a78: The Chair of the Board gave the floor consecutively to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, Councillor Jocelyn Pauzé and Councillor Andréanne Moreau.
entries.75e952d80c90021b5d8d4f1ad49be0c0893e344c: From the outset, the official Opposition chief Ericka Alneus is of the opinion that culture can create a deep attachment to a language. She mentions the importance of the work done within the City of Montreal in terms of the French language, notably by a French-language committee led by Louise Harel and several elected officials. She describes Montréal as a Francophone, polyglot and Francophile metropolis. Ms. Alneus hopes that our metropolis will continue to welcome groups of different languages and convey to them the desire to appropriate French.
entries.dd41f2cb5c5b075b6d8d1a3d1a8a671685dc1e37: In turn, Councillor Jocelyn Pauzé states that French plays an essential social role, unifying generations and facilitating integration and inclusion in Montreal and Quebec. He looks back at the creation of the Bureau de la langue française in 2025 and the involvement of Mrs. Harel. Mr. Pauzé concludes by stressing the need to protect what constitutes the heart of Montréal's identity: the French language.
entries.279f83f28b8a0c65194f8bd7f0166661b96f35ea: As for Councillor Andréanne Moreau, she also felt that the month of la francophonie was a highlight for Montreal and for the affirmation of the French language. She described French as a distinctive element shaping the metropolis and its community. She mentioned in particular the measures put in place to preserve and strengthen French, such as the prices of the French language. Finally, Ms. Moreau reaffirmed the Administration's commitment to continue these actions in cultural, community and international circles.
entries.da7c9fc78062b3d8b60e47e788d453c9fa9ccb15: 1 - Celebrates the Chinese and Vietnamese Lunar New Year on February 17, 2026, and conveys its best wishes to Montrealers of Asian descent;
entries.f488aac0f8922d74e83a474ee978dde779c704f5: 2 - highlights the important contribution of communities of Asian origin to the development and outreach of Montreal;
entries.51f30f6365aaeda8c75eca3defc54c44719fb986: 3 - continues to work with its partners to combat racism and systemic discrimination, promote inclusion and recognize the different Asian cultures that shape the metropolis.
entries.3b3f5d3703e204ecbdb5761f59975619516ca884: Whereas the Chinese and Vietnamese New Year will be celebrated this year on February 17, and will mark the beginning of the Horse Year;
entries.a63370c68b5f494648abab0b373d59001acb73bb: Whereas the Chinese and Vietnamese New Year celebrations are an opportunity for the general public to recognize the important contributions that Montrealers of Asian descent have made and continue to make to the identity, prosperity and culture of Montreal;
entries.67705d31b94bdd103f6ae6d376068101293cf2d3: Whereas activities marking this day will be held throughout the metropolis and will provide an opportunity to learn more about Chinese and Vietnamese cultures;
entries.20792f61ac63ad08b122a910c466b4dbc0371a48: Whereas Asian community organizations and institutions play an essential role in the preservation of cultural heritage, the intergenerational transmission of language and traditions, support for youth and seniors, the promotion of volunteerism and citizen engagement;
entries.46b628da4e0496f039275cf6552ba071cb0b3b3b: Whereas the Chinese Quarter of Montreal is the only significant historical district in a preserved Chinese community in Quebec and Eastern Canada, and the only French-speaking Chinese neighbourhood in America;
entries.c4978893ae70f3f9d06fb8a62160d1c16244a717: Whereas the Chinese and Vietnamese communities enrich Montreal's diversity, which is firmly rooted in the collective identity of the metropolis, shaping Montréal's unique character;
entries.114cc67d7d5018687bdfdb9157a79f45c9e63e38: Whereas the City of Montreal is more committed than ever to combating racism and discrimination against Asian Montrealers, and is in action to combat this problem on several fronts;
entries.3fdbbc61b9bb5208313796a7ef649fb28f746f7d: Whereas Chinese and Vietnamese New Year is a symbol of renewal, and it is an opportunity for the City of Montreal to renew its friendship vows with China and Vietnam: long-standing relations based on respect, mutual aid and solidarity.
entries.0ea48ef7b83aca951a747b8356654787b47afe50: The Chair of the Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Claude Pinard for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.294e3ca558fbe722ec50a96be4f77db506ddd4f5: At the outset, Mr. Pinard mentioned the essential role of Chinese and Vietnamese communities in the cultural and social life of Montreal and recalled the lasting friendship based on respect and mutual support that binds them to the metropolis. Councillor Claude Pinard continued by putting forward the richness of the traditions associated with the lunar New Year and the importance of recognizing the contributions of people of Asian descent in Montreal. Finally, he expressed wishes for happiness, prosperity and solidarity for the Cheval's year.
entries.b4d2f42f39474db9d81813080150600838c8f7e1: The chair then gave the floor to Councillor Cathy Wong.
entries.d90b532d76ebee9b15980868a89356a712b3008d: From the outset, Councillor Cathy Wong refers to the symbolic significance of the lunar New Year, which she presents as a moment of memory, transmission and intergenerational gathering within the Chinese and Vietnamese communities of Montreal. She believes that the cultural richness of these celebrations, as well as the historical, social and community role of Chinatown and organizations, contribute to preserving these traditions. In conclusion, Ms. Wong recalls the importance of solidarity and the fight against racism, hoping that the year of the Fire Horse will be that of collective courage that chooses cooperation rather than division.
entries.9c15f46994416cd73cabc5e91871df4ccfa6e9bf: The president of the council gave the floor successively to Councillors Alan DeSousa and Dimitrios (Jim) Beis, who, in turn, also stressed the importance of Chinese and Vietnamese communities for the City of Montreal and expressed their best wishes on the occasion of the lunar New Year.
entries.cd38d74be7bd107777e2200999d0898c52f25f98: 1 - reaffirms its support for the Ukrainian people in connection with the fourth sad anniversary of the Russian illegal invasion into Ukraine;
entries.2ea7c85c484c1cf6393448d04db9ca8e21bd7729: 2 - expresses its outrage at this military invasion and condemns the illegal invasion of Russia in Ukraine, while reaffirming the right of the Ukrainian people to live in peace and security;
entries.84dfc7a983f941fa5cbd8bb7baca7754788259bf: 3 - reiterates its solidarity with the Ukrainian community in Montreal, as well as with its peers in local and regional Ukrainian governments;
entries.52d091950bc142b6b4414cad8482525f9b54b616: 4 - Reiterates its support for the governments of Quebec and Canada in coordinating host efforts as well as in their efforts to address the issues raised by the war in Ukraine;
entries.10150675b034b29904dd00d9aab27515104732a6: 5 - invites Montrealers to continue to show a spirit of mutual support and solidarity with the Ukrainian people and community, as hostilities continue for a fifth year.
entries.205658f86913bac7e04927859d8d8e79cddc5c92: Whereas the illegal invasion of Russia into Ukraine, which has continued since 24 February 2022, constitutes a serious violation of international peace and security, leading to a major international crisis and disastrous consequences for the Ukrainian people;
entries.bdc20f729448092e00e22722dfe873899f577e59: Whereas this invasion entails unacceptable infringements of the human rights, sovereignty and territorial integrity of Ukraine, as well as of the Charter of the United Nations and international conventions;
entries.258889eb79bbc3410ef0a56a5fa0260e9e398091: Whereas a study by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) revealed that at the dawn of the fifth year of war, the Russian invasion into Ukraine had resulted in 1.8 million injured, missing or killed victims, stating that no great power has suffered as many casualties or casualties in any war since the Second World War;
entries.d0d848c63f27882e07a234595e0b0b1e770c0031: Whereas in the event of continued hostilities, the number of victims of war in Ukraine would exceed two million by spring 2026, and that thousands of Ukrainian children had been abducted by Russia;
entries.79cd49e5dbafcde98d6a09b8931cccca15779f50: Whereas nearly seven million Ukrainians have been forced to leave their country since the beginning of the Russian invasion, and Canada has welcomed 300,000 of them since the start of the war;
entries.affd0a9ab4d8a6fec4eacdd287e5d1be7b7bdbbb: Whereas Quebecers of Ukrainian origin have contributed greatly to the economic, social, cultural and artistic development of Montreal, and that the Ukrainian community has left part of its cultural capital to the City of Montréal by leaving its mark on several levels, including associative life and municipal toponymy;
entries.ec33e03f4070861f1b6612da5e52f41309664468: Whereas the Ukrainian Montréal community is very mobilized to support the Ukrainian people, and Montrealers continue to show great generosity in terms of humanitarian assistance.
entries.1d572c027694fd93acbed1a75c65499d26801b94: Recalling that the City of Montreal is a plural city with various communities that contribute to enriching the collective environment, Mr. Josué Corvil underlines the strong presence of the Ukrainian community in the neighborhoods and boroughs of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Pointe-Saint-Charles and Lachine, communities which actively participate in the different spheres of activity of the metropolis. The presence on the balcony of the consul of Ukraine, Eugene Czolij, is welcomed.
entries.d8c322d5d4bb9751760179b4e8453507489fe4ed: Then, referring to the events of 24 February 2022, when Russia carried out the illegal invasion of Ukraine, the adviser recalls that this aggression plunged the Ukrainian population into a prolonged conflict. The international community, which condemns this attack, has still not achieved any convincing results in the peace talks undertaken since then.
entries.da974040091040524755cea9d05d4e09b1be4411: The City of Montreal, which has clearly positioned itself against this invasion, renews its solidarity with the Ukrainian people. As we approach the sad anniversary of the beginning of the war, which will occur in four days' time, it puts forward that this conflict constitutes a direct violation of human rights, territorial integrity and international standards. The Ukrainian population, whose daily life is marked by a persistent humanitarian disaster, faces a situation that continues to worsen.
entries.4495cc676595eb4eadc7f208322a85c9df02b77f: Finally, based on the constant mobilization of the Montreal Ukrainian community, which played an active role in promoting peace, democracy and living together, Mr. Corvil pointed out that the City of Montreal was collaborating with the community and continuing its efforts to welcome those who needed it. Support for local partner governments was also expressed.
entries.3708fa1ceede0e1d50550a0adce9418fdc6952e0: The chair of the council successively gave his word to Councillors François Limoges and Sonny Moroz.
entries.8ff60034a3b9699bc15048ae17838d1a06e458a6: Underscoring the chance, as mayor of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie district, to know the Ukrainian community well, François Limoges recalls that this community, which has been rooted for many years in the borough, is one of the building forces that contribute to the dynamism and vitality of the environment.
entries.ef4809b5022e4a5d9e270383ca144d0ce31a964b: In closing, he reaffirmed the support of the municipal government and assured that the City of Montreal would remain in solidarity with the Ukrainian community and would continue its support efforts.
entries.1183fd5c86377cfc7d40613ae5b684d86ffc0cb3: Subsequently, Councillor Sonny Moroz recalled that the large-scale invasion of Ukraine had led to forced exile and marked for nearly seven million Ukrainians during the last four years of war, which was why it was important for him to recognize the scale of the conflict. Moreover, he affirmed that the Ukrainian people must be able to freely choose their future, he reiterated his solidarity and mentioned that this war directly affected several people living in Montreal.
entries.f86d46304d8e27e8835d87346d0ac1e134257f96: By way of conclusion, he said that the resilience of the Ukrainian people, supported by international solidarity, enabled Ukraine to hold, and believed that each community had the power to affirm the principles underpinning democracy and human dignity.
entries.08039961554b502b2ceb6f8afedca60ed467fdcd: 1 - reaffirms its commitment to the values of peace, respect for fundamental rights, security and dignity for all;
entries.611097cd8e3a5cdc6aaad512c2100bc6f26fe4e2: 2 - in collaboration with community and institutional partners, continue its efforts to support the communities concerned and recognize the essential role of Iranian community organizations in supporting those affected by the repression of demonstrations in Iran, while combating all forms of stigma and discrimination;
entries.feb7d51d9d029c9bc952b36123049fbda1587486: 3 - maintain an open dialogue with organizations and members of the Iranian community in order to better understand their needs and integrate them into its municipal actions;
entries.2d49dd68380a21e871fbfbf5f1422df8cadcf481: 4 - expresses its solidarity with the Iranian communities affected by the repression of demonstrations in Iran.
entries.db7f2ea06d71b75a7fc085c724c48392d9171c72: Whereas many people of Iranian origin reside throughout Montreal, work there and actively engage in it, contributing significantly to the social, cultural, scientific and economic vitality of the metropolis;
entries.ba4a344f97e8310243ec73c8722fb7f8ed763218: Whereas, according to Statistics Canada's 2021 census data, more than 23,000 Iranians are located in the Montreal metropolitan area, including some 12,000 Iranians on the Island of Montreal;
entries.14f8d11bc667525bd28ed03e9df1a61b5a167ffb: Whereas the repression of demonstrations in Iran has significant human consequences and gives rise to serious concern among Iranian communities in the diaspora, particularly as a result of insecurity, violence, violations of fundamental rights and separation of families;
entries.5a2a05ecb4dcf20e74ea813d74dcf20473d8e175: Whereas several people of Iranian origin in Montreal are directly affected by the impact of repression in Iran, whether because of the presence of their relatives in that country or because of the impact of this situation on their own emotional and psychosocial well-being;
entries.728f109c569002c30b36e3bf586ad94859998c15: Whereas the City of Montreal recognizes the importance for local public institutions of listening, solidarity and sensitivity to communities affected by international conflicts and crises;
entries.ae85263e0a11b9ed871ff1a8dfa442a6e5176f92: Whereas community organizations and voluntary networks frequented by Iranian communities play an essential role in supporting, dialogue and strengthening social harmony;
entries.ae4aac3f25be31d396883c539db9b053a90dc425: Whereas the promotion of peace, human dignity, respect for human rights and living together is a foundation for municipal action by the City of Montreal.
entries.2acadca4229175eab37ca0e41902bb72eb11d4e7: The Chair gave the floor to Councillor Sonny Moroz for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.7f65e90dc6f23a1279d26b617d243c47695ae5da: At the outset, Mr. Sonny Moroz reaffirmed the city council's willingness to show visible and consistent solidarity with members of the Iranian-Montréal community, who were experiencing a period of anguish because of the current situation in Iran. He mentioned that several thousand people of Iranian origin were actively involved in Montreal life, and that many of them were now deeply affected by the loss of their lives, arrests and communication cuts affecting their loved ones in Iran. Councillor Sonny Moroz went on to stress the extent of human rights violations, noting, inter alia, that those who had expressed their opinions paid for their freedom or life, which was unacceptable. Finally, he pointed out that the council did not take a position in Iran's internal political debates, but reiterated the universal importance of protecting human dignity and affirmed that the City of Montréal must stand alongside its communities in difficult times.
entries.3c40c0da646a5f3f4149eb79fd0c077ee202872b: The Chair gave the floor to Councillor Céline-Audrey Beauregard and then to Councillor Peter McQueen.
entries.9594a930ad333dce6b805d8b77d58ba742a8c6c7: First of all, Mrs Beauregard expresses her solidarity with the Irano-Montréal community and recalls the ties that she has developed with its members, especially in her district of Verdun, where many live today anxiously for their loved ones. Then, she stresses the importance of publicly supporting this community, referring to the testimonies received and recent mobilizations, in order to affirm the need to defend the freedom and dignity of the Iranian people. Peter McQueen also supports the Irano-Montréal community, welcoming, among other things, the courage of those who demonstrate for their rights, while wishing peace and justice for the Iranian people.
entries.8279a89b3f6bc91403f42af98d957557957ae354: 1 - recognize the week of February 16-20, 2026 as the Weeks of School Persistence;
entries.36a47b521def40d8c86704921752eb90c0609f99: 2 - supports this campaign and invites elected persons to participate in it;
entries.3776adc47502d88f6007aad13e3c1545e85337ca: 3 - invites the whole community to mobilize around school perseverance, for educational success and to break the cycle of inequalities.
entries.c75056fdc69324b87d738ad161e1f30def902800: Whereas the 22nd edition of the Days of School Perseverance (JPS) will be held from 16 to 20 February 2026, this year's theme, "Perseverance leads far away", is intended to highlight the efforts and attempts that lead to achievement;
entries.bc43f1fef08438471bc09a4593c3eda99093baeb: Whereas the JPS is an initiative of Réseau succes Montréal (RRM), whose mission is to mobilize all Montreal partners around concerted actions aimed at supporting young people, parents and stakeholders, in order to foster perseverance, success and school hang-up;
entries.7eebe660484d6ed4ceec532944abb2a89fbb3d62: Whereas school perseverance and success are among the concerns of the City of Montreal, and that education is essential for the Montréal community;
entries.9d4dcd4087b4cfeda7912cf98463ec1f5257075c: Whereas the municipalities, through the establishment of sports platforms, cultural spaces and financial assistance programmes dedicated to youth organizations, have the skills and powers to directly influence the quality of life of young people and enable them to develop their full potential;
entries.9a0c7d1e40fd6901d56a378fa63a0d09f5c3a4a1: Whereas the City of Montreal has set aside $100,000 in its 2026 budget to allow young people to enjoy extended programming in the evening, after class, at certain municipal sports, cultural and recreational facilities;
entries.2a063b4b604569e700f628eeeaa19403b83a7610: Whereas the dropout rate in Quebec is declining, but the proportion of young Montrealers who drop out is higher, while nearly a quarter of young Quebecers who dropped out in 2022 were in Montreal;
entries.4cedf25ff53a03b7735fb998963d57812c345a36: Whereas it is necessary to intensify actions and adapt interventions to the needs of pupils at risk of dropping out in order to ensure the graduation of more young people;
entries.c91f96ab6282bf0e4e8791223af43bccb5b32103: Whereas, according to the most recent data, Montreal has nearly 84% of Quebec primary school students living below the low income threshold and under conditions of disadvantage;
entries.010d96613fd7d325ef68b46ac088639622f8cb33: Whereas pupils from disadvantaged backgrounds are at greater risk of difficulties and drop-out, and that the whole community must be mobilized around school to break the cycle of inequalities;
entries.24d9e36d66f3b43e6c6035ddbb922329df24c0f1: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Christine Black for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.2c8a055cb1346d601c72cf941baae68903d0d334: From the outset, Councillor Christine Black highlighted the 22nd edition of School Perseverance Days under the theme: "Perseverance leads a long way." She said that it was with pride that the official launch was held for the first time at Montreal City Hall, and recalled, in connection with the theme, that constant efforts lead to lasting achievements. Ms. Black stressed the importance of valuing the progress made as much as the results achieved in a world marked by instant gratification. She indicated that challenges, trials and errors shaped success and that perseverance was built over time; school paths were rarely linear, each young person deserved support and confidence.
entries.5eecdbb0390867d9e4ccba7cc5e470e58f6ddd1c: Ms. Black welcomed the presence of those invited to the balcony and said that school success remained a collective responsibility and that the City of Montreal played a key role in the development of young people. She concluded by inviting board members to continue to mobilize to encourage the perseverance and success of young people by voting in favour of this Declaration.
entries.7b308a63af939c98bc29b42e66bc41f8dc68bd12: Then, Councillor Céline-Audrey Beauregard spoke and told us that school perseverance was based on a collective effort, carried out by teachers as well as by professionals, educational institutions and community organizations. She mentioned, among other things, that the Quebec school system is undergoing a period of transformation, making the accompaniment of young people more complex in everyday life. As a teacher, she stressed the importance of adapting practices and building on quality of life, notably through access to green, sports and community spaces. Finally, Ms Beauragard invited the various levels of government to take concrete steps to support school perseverance and welcomed the essential commitment of organizations working against dropping out.
entries.b2ee9bd8b76ec1851cec8ef358d708a143d9bbfb: In her turn, Councillor Andréanne Moreau begins by sharing a personal anecdote to illustrate that perseverance is learnt from an early age through small gestures in everyday life. She sees how perseverance takes root early and influences the confidence and autonomy of children. Ms. Moreau believes that perseverance is one of the most valuable learnings on the school journey. She concludes by thanking teaching staff and encouraging parents to support their children in their educational success.
entries.6ba2f25373b85f5425335f3bcf735ce914023b34: The Chair thanked the three Councillors for their interventions.

entries.157418adaed5a2515b73e33ba272db3b58d1f952: that the City Council reaffirms the importance of basing its decisions on evidence, scientific recommendations and the priorities of the citizens of Montreal, including public planning, public and road safety, public health and climate resilience;
entries.06db3f594d532278389d1809328e59ce2f9ae651: 1 - commits itself to strengthening its scientific consultation mechanisms and integrating recognized best practices into public policies and projects;
entries.0d99908adb08fcad5c8376562ad0d0274135048e: 2 - develops and maintains these agreements, partnerships or participations with research institutions and experts to ensure informed, fair and sustainable decision-making.
entries.9864fda4daf67a5f294fcebdeb18d9b70579b1a6: Counsellor Émilie Brière and Councillor Alexandre Teodoresco tabled a new consensual version of point 65.01. The new version reads as follows:
entries.b74e9b55d12d75d7fb11d4200f8fce7a6bbb4b3d: Whereas decisions on urban planning, road safety, public health and climate resilience have a major impact on the quality of life of citizens and on the sustainability of infrastructure;
entries.759b7b01b49015366ae3099d2a0ea0dd3bcfc779: Whereas science and evidence are essential tools to guide effective, safe and responsive public policies while being fully anchored in the priorities expressed by Montreal citizens;
entries.a227d489070be124195c3f8920bd0695bcfc22b3: Whereas the Montreal population is concerned about the shift observed in the United States, and elsewhere in the world, particularly in a global context of polycrises, including the environmental crisis, and that it wants public decisions to be guided by best scientific practices;
entries.263b3a6c557d4c43f34ee9b87e9d9de221a102b7: Whereas Montreal, as a major university city and economic metropolis of Quebec, hosts world-renowned researchers, in particular, but not limited to: Daniel Georges Bichet, Yoshua Bengio, Laurent Mottron, Line Chamberland, Catherine Morency, Marguerite Mendell, Anne-Marie Mes-Masson, Farah Alibay, Julie Bruneau and Samuel Pierre;
entries.ca3b44a61a8da9e063ad9478bb2d5851bcdb408e: Whereas the City of Montreal can rely, from its public service, on high-calibre experts who stand at the forefront of progress in their field and through whom it can make informed decisions;
entries.1c0cee83e64eb0df995ab4fbbb707b62a1bcbd89: Whereas ignoring the recommendations of experts and rigorous studies undermines user safety, the city's resilience to climate change and the credibility of public institutions;
entries.d57f79d643b6a473975ead770aa3652e9226c89a: Whereas the City of Montreal, as a metropolis, must be exemplary when it comes to integrating science into its public policies and projects;
entries.012c91f9d6e1b3126dd0e73392ad3abce73baf7e: She offered a plea for science and the leading role she must play in public order decisions, cited many examples to support her position, and considered it essential to take note of decisions in the world that did not always go in the direction of best scientific practice.
entries.cdb6f384623c0a29c52636908186c343a1a9b546: The Chair then invited the Authority's representative, Councillor Alexandre Teodoresco, to speak on this matter.
entries.e714298ef033a34428ce5b69527e0a6f4d4d238c: Mr. Teodoresco considers Montreal to be a city of knowledge. In this regard, he presents the Administration's approach committed to go further to consolidate this status and even exceed expectations. To this end, he appoints some of the partnerships and research chairs with universities and affirms in particular that the Administration is positioning itself as an engine for scientific research. He concludes by stressing the importance of including both the scientific recommendations and the priorities expressed by the Montreal population in public decision-making.
entries.ee513b2ac6a8354f5a4aae6ebff0a423a9f62dd4: Then, Councillor Émilie Brière confirmed that there was no objection to this new version of the motion.
entries.26898e310eadd4efc4434fef967f562b83014526: The chair of the board gave the floor successively to Councillor Catherine Houbart, Councillor Christopher McCray and Councillor Sarah V. Doyon.
entries.b24cd07e58f3623761257eed69648c20a3b66c78: In turn, the two councillors and the adviser reiterate their commitment to take into account scientific evidence and available expertise in public decision-making, as this includes a responsibility that elected people have towards the population.
entries.e8501343ef4368597d20e41f060dbb38401bfeff: 1- the municipal council reiterates its commitment to transparency, sound financial management and the fight against corruption;
entries.57f8f69cffa1222c891bbec7e2589cc058d8c5e8: 2- the municipal council affirms that elected officials and public managers must respect the highest standards of integrity and ethics in the performance of their duties;
entries.ded694104a81518162b9ae0689de3afcf6567956: 3- that the City of Montreal continue and strengthen its efforts to implement mechanisms for monitoring, accountability and ongoing training in ethics and governance;
entries.6fa56256cf795f67afc21201370498d21a31a0e9: 4. that all elected members of the municipal council undertake to respect the rules of integrity in the course of their duties;
entries.c1e014f5d46fd170b07a53daf000fa1098fda21e: 5- that this motion be forwarded to the National Assembly in order to emphasize the importance of maintaining and improving the measures resulting from the recommendations of the Charbonneau Commission.
entries.f5ad600c3b1b618a9c4fa8c938d7770e862e9b68: Councillors François Limoges and Claude Pinard tabled a new consensual version of point 65.02. The new version reads as follows:
entries.0a21ccaae717132193b4e06b994650be6dd6433e: Whereas the Commission of Inquiry into the Granting and Management of Public Contracts in the Construction Industry (Commission Charbonneau) was established in 2012 to shed light on practices of corruption and collusion affecting public administration in Quebec, particularly with regard to the financing of political parties;
entries.3a1cd51dfd16287a3aa54a3d2a73462adf689bd1: Whereas the City of Montreal has been a victim of collusion and corruption in the past and some elected officials at that time have been found guilty;
entries.3b6332b429109dc195b419eab6f24b7eae597aee: Whereas the work of the Charbonneau Commission has led to major recommendations aimed at enhancing transparency, sound financial management and combating corruption in public institutions;
entries.a27eae1af6cfea8a4f3c37097a97c597119c3357: Whereas we have a duty of remembrance towards this sad part of our history so as not to repeat the mistakes of the past;
entries.4035fe4f1fe38438f5fedf5b66fc2705772475d4: Whereas citizens' confidence in their institutions is based on the integrity and ethics of elected officials and public managers;
entries.70fbf1587a146c8076bc410d94595debce29c867: Whereas the City established an Office of the Inspector General in 2014 following the revelations of the Charbonneau Commission and its mandate is to monitor the integrity of municipal contracts and combat corruption still today;
entries.18332102793e121491773546b5de4eb4d1f09f30: Whereas ten years after the publication of the Charbonneau Commission's report, it remains essential to maintain high standards of governance, accountability and prevention of fraudulent practices;
entries.c455fd54774b738c405973547c4915ee6c1e5c40: Whereas Ms. France Charbonneau is a key figure in the history of justice in Quebec and that the City of Montreal, at the initiative of Mayor Valérie Plante, emphasized her important career by appointing her Commander of the Order of Montreal at the inauguration of Place des Montréaliennes in 2025;
entries.a2c057db59ee41bfd246746957edbbae98c5d540: Whereas the City of Montreal, as a metropolis, must be exemplary in managing public funds and applying the principles of transparency and integrity;
entries.8aa697542f63913627a1033f806a4da63846c9d5: The Chair of Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the proposer of the motion, Councillor François Limoges, for his presentation.
entries.25b94e2bdd4e65c494e2e4da698021af9f620958: Mr Limoges began his presentation by declaring the importance of the duty to remember. To mark the tenth anniversary of the publication of the Charbonneau Commission's report, it was unequivocal that it remained essential to maintain high standards of governance, accountability and the prevention of fraudulent practices.He mentioned in particular the leading role played by the city council at the time and hoped that this would continue in that direction.He concluded on the rigor and exemplary nature to be retained in public administration, which should constitute the most constant duty of elected persons.
entries.3d1fe3210362c5cf84d4f2179e6feb008123a28e: In addition, Councillor Véronique Fournier stressed, among other things, the important contribution of Louise Harel, who was chief of the Official Opposition from 2009 to 2013, and who worked hard to ensure that a commission of inquiry came into being and looked at the granting and management of public contracts in the construction industry. She concluded with the duty of transparency, ethics, access to information and rigour for sound public financial management.
entries.105edca43a4586baf426f4467f492ed224ee76ae: The representative of the Administration for this matter, Mr. Claude Pinard, took the floor, indicating in particular the precision of the Administration to the Fifth Resolute so that this consensus motion could be transmitted to the National Assembly. He acknowledged that there was a possibility of drifts in the award of public contracts but recalled that structural and robust measures had been put forward to counter them. To this end, he cited the work of the Inspector General's Office. Finally, the Administration reiterated its commitment to maintain high standards in ethics and to strengthen the tools that protected the public interest.
entries.da6282cb351da5cb49f2f2679214646bba2be9e1: In conclusion, Mr Limoges exercised his right of reply.
entries.53f2e6e51dfc87dbd4cb02026f739cd7a3424aa2: The Chair thanked Council members for their interventions.
