entries.66ccbe6b592787e42dd6827c3e09feda1cbcb046: that the City Council of the City of Montreal:
entries.b3226c55adb174fec9984ead5406c70eeffde0fc: 1 - recognize the essential contribution of temporary residents to the vitality and development of the metropolis;
entries.9cbc4c3acaaa528663bda9371cc034a3c6b91655: 2 - calls on the Government of Quebec to put in place, without delay, a right clause for persons established in Quebec and holding a temporary immigration permit at the time of abolition of the EQP;
entries.2df1013a7c51b0c263663e739a0f890821cd6ba9: 3 - calls on the Government of Quebec to ensure predictable, humane and consistent access to permanent residence for persons already integrated and established in Montreal;
entries.d2e690266c4290cccbcb6f3411a2a7f3f89c5d25: 4 - joins hundreds of people, organizations and municipalities who ask the Government of Quebec to reconsider the abolition of the PEQ or offer an alternative to individuals and families already established and integrated in Quebec;
entries.a53324589c30cece92a925cc806378bfeb3bffa5: 5 - forwards this statement to the Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Integration and to the Quebec National Assembly.
entries.f1a1f2185b8545163b4e4644b1c0fd8a913ef709: Whereas the City of Montreal is an inclusive metropolis whose economic, social and cultural vitality depends largely on the contributions of immigrants;
entries.f860aed98eb7c5435d2bf7a9288b1766c04da035: Whereas thousands of temporary residents are studying, working and rooting in Montreal, actively contributing to the prosperity of the city and the vitality of its neighbourhoods;
entries.7425e5cc0c4c05b276e3d1a085565ae898636451: Whereas the Program de l'expérience québécoise (PEQ) was abolished on November 19, 2025, thereby limiting access to permanent residence for thousands of non-permanent residents based in Montreal;
entries.07c852ffb72aa5b2b29e0cad1a810cd777201401: Whereas by providing temporary workers with the opportunity to quickly access permanent residence, the PEQ allowed the Quebec labour market to benefit from graduates, trained locally, already housed, and actively contributing to the social and economic life of the province;
entries.c1e741c67253237c241ce7736cb924368fc07a6a: Whereas the Programme was intended for French-speaking persons whose mastery of French had been attested by tests or diplomas recognized by the Government;
entries.3219eed489de3cebc9c07f31b50f88af6ef1a2d7: Whereas the abolition of this fundamental program, without transitional measures, already has a dramatic impact on affected individuals and families (financial and residential instability, family separations, exoduses to other cities or regions, etc.), and that these impacts are particularly felt on Montreal and its population;
entries.d0ab27fc8955c89ea927485e4821ae741766db5c: Whereas the removal of the PEQ undermines the attractiveness of the City of Montreal, the retention of talent, the outreach of higher education institutions and our ability to attract and retain the international student community;
entries.d39efcb7942e9eb26fa656dfbd74478a2b94be83: Whereas the Qualified Worker Selection Program (QWPP) is now the only way to access permanent residence in economic immigration, and the latter favours applications established outside Montreal;
entries.a907496672c64bf9b52068a819ae17ad85bcf0b2: Whereas the lack of predictability and barriers to access to permanent residence resulting from recent changes in immigration programmes and regulations contribute to weakening immigration routes and increase the precariousness of immigrants, in particular those with temporary or waiting status;
entries.6aedd16d371a4f9f9e81857e4971760724fc8742: Whereas the PSTQ could lead to a loss of attractiveness and competitiveness for the metropolis, both for its enterprises and higher education institutions;
entries.de6f7ac78441dc9cf56c96dd2d257538644af246: The Chair of the Council, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, and to the Leader of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.e649faacd989905f425d192a0ecc596f68c4054b: The Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, said she was pleased to join Ericka Alneus, leader of the Official Opposition, in presenting this one-vote statement concerning the abolition of the Quebec Experience Program (QEP). She wanted to launch a message because she believed that the credibility of Québec and Montreal was at stake. She hoped for humane and consistent access to permanent residence for people already living in Montreal. On November 19, the Government of Quebec abolished the QEP without offering transitional measures and that it was a lever that allowed temporary residents to gain faster access to permanent residence, while they lived, worked and contributed fully to the development of the metropolis.
entries.3a5337f7b6418d0c8a867df4219797cddde3bba4: Martinez Ferrada points out that the consequences of this news are already being felt in Montreal. She demonstrates, among other things, that it is talents and brains that will be lost, which will damage the attractiveness and reputation of the city and Quebec. In conclusion, the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada asks the provincial government to review the way to permanent residence so that it is predictable, humane and coherent for those who have already been established.
entries.696f83119ee9e5d77e07da760a3c704773e42b88: Later, the official Opposition leader Ericka Alneus mentioned that there are non-partisan issues, such as this one, which lead elected people to put their role at the service of the humanities that make up the City. She indicated that this joint statement is intended to be a clear response to asserting that it supports and defends this cause. She emphasized the privilege of welcoming high-quality people who choose to settle, work and study here. Ericka Alneus, head of the Official Opposition, concluded by reaffirming the humanity of the Montreal community and the desire to build this strong link that builds Montréal.
entries.04662e81ff6c2e46fd0f6e9de3d6a3af5c93796b: The Chair thanked them and gave the floor successively to Ms. Maeva Vilain, Mr. Christopher McCray and Ms. Émilie Brière.
entries.2dd199e1b77beb97ef2f6c5f04278f3ce9f82496: Councillor Maeva Vilain thanked the entire municipal council for this statement, explaining that she had arrived in Montreal 20 years ago, with the equivalent of the Quebec Experience Program, and had been able to access permanent residence and give back to her community as a city councillor. Ms. Vilain pointed out that behind these programs there were colleagues, neighbours, friends, student relatives, nurses, community employees, educators, traders and entrepreneurs who moved Montréal and Québec forward. Finally, Ms. Vilain asked the Government of Quebec to respect her word, apply a grandfather clause so that people could integrate and settle permanently within the Quebec community.
entries.63000ac0f10e52f0aa8e4de9eafd1397ebe25d09: McCray, in turn, said that he had arrived in Quebec in 2015 with a study permit. He met people from all over the world. He stated, among other things, that many, like him, quickly fell in love with Montreal, Quebec, his culture and the French language. Many chose to stay there, establish there and work there. McCray noted that the new program penalized Montrealers by favouring those who had lived outside the city. Councillor McCray was proud to support this joint declaration calling for a grandfather clause, because beyond the programs, it was about human lives and the future of the city.
entries.b3560acf6fb460f7b170b47e3213e86260a421a1: Second, Councillor Émilie Brière put forward issues related to economic development, the scientific vitality and the influence of the metropolis, all of which were greatly affected by this government shift. Ms. Brière pointed out that it weakens confidence and creates instability that directly affects Montreal's businesses, organizations and institutions. She recalled that the end of the PEQ was detrimental to the attraction and retention of talent, including at universities. Ms. Brière felt it essential that Montréal ask the Government of Quebec to put in place transitional measures and maintain access to permanent residence.
entries.a829c057a6b957ef41d2aa665d447ea38d04b374: 1- Strongly reaffirms that zero tolerance is required in all its bodies, services, units and districts when it comes to racism, discrimination and hate speech in all its forms;
entries.43e0cdd49841bb1b40f592186ceb9e17cb740e57: 2- recognize the essential and exceptional contribution of Black communities to the history of Montreal's development and outreach;
entries.6d3b59c41d25fbede3da8c45badf1d5c7da06960: 3- highlights the 35th edition of Black History Month under the theme "Let's Raise Our Voices Together", recognizes the essential contribution of the Roundtable to this organization and invites Montrealers to mobilize and participate in activities as early as February 1, 2026;
entries.60cff76edd65f69364bac5ad3d08d62070ca8a4f: 4. explicitly recognize that employees of the City have experienced situations of discrimination and racism and reaffirm the importance of creating and maintaining safe, respectful and equitable workplaces;
entries.84a7a0c71b04b54e443fb836fac7a21ebe00f6d3: 5- Reiterates its commitment to continue and strengthen actions aimed at preventing racism and discrimination, for example by more transparently disaggregating and disseminating data on the communities targeted by the City of Montreal's employment equity program in order to be able to draw an analysis that the City can use in its fight against racism and discrimination.
entries.542ad67143907779b8fa93f8e5a9dd89f8263ce9: Whereas Black communities play an essential role in Montreal life, whether it be their contributions as citizens, artists entrepreneurs, community leaders, elected persons or employees of the City of Montréal;
entries.42ccefbf34dd891ae217fb7a3c43cc664b9e5691: Whereas the current social context is marked by an increase in hate speech, increased polarization and worrying setbacks to equity, diversity and inclusion, which underlines the importance of a clear, courageous and united voice for public institutions;
entries.535bcf51f547737bafeb5e9748ddf21658decc80: Whereas in 2026 the 35th edition of Black History Month in Canada will take place from February 1 to March 1, 2026;
entries.5af32df4f3dfe700b173a34026252f62dc8671a2: Whereas the Round Table of Black History Month has been organizing activities for 35 years that allow Quebecers to discover the richness and diversity of black communities, while paying tribute to black people who have distinguished themselves in different areas of expertise;
entries.d439d1901deb1046c928cf63dc750bb3295dc30c: Whereas the theme of Black History Month 2026 is "Let's raise our voices together" and calls for collective, responsible and solidarity in order to recognize the realities lived and contribute actively to a more just and inclusive society;
entries.fba19361c9e9fd1b8cfad0069eddbb73ca5c458a: Whereas on November 23, 2006, the National Assembly passed the bill to make February Black History Month, and that the historical contribution of black communities to Quebec society has been emphasized since February 1, 2007;
entries.9c6b580cffa052ece12a32ced658795e18382bb0: Whereas, following the receipt of the report by the Office de consultation publique de Montréal (OCPM) on racism and systemic discrimination, in June 2020, the City of Montreal recognized the existence of the problem and committed itself to taking action to combat it;
entries.2c9e5b746f9ce960209b2ef4f71ad26061061437: Whereas in June 2020, the City Council of Montreal unanimously adopted a Declaration to recognize the systemic nature of racism and discrimination and committed itself to combating them;
entries.ccc076a67fb2e7ed54f4ea4fee02dffe38611a3b: Whereas the City of Montreal recognizes that situations of racism and discrimination have been experienced within the municipal administration itself, including by black employees;
entries.7587d6ec02894a7fad4cc27539e8e87eceff7cb5: Whereas the City of Montreal condemns all forms of racism and discrimination in all its bodies, and encourages all its employees to denounce and combat racism in all its forms;
entries.fb47ef3d662b41d64cfe6e08385a48a166d406b0: Whereas the City of Montreal has established the Office of the Commissioner for Combating Racism and Systemic Discrimination, whose mandate is to accelerate the City's transformation to be more fair, inclusive and egalitarian, as well as a dedicated line of call and mandatory training;
entries.4a6063f119908a561d0553fb51effc833aabecc9: Whereas measures to combat racism already in place should be maintained and strengthened, while promoting rigorous evaluation with a view to the continuous improvement of our practices;
entries.e4a4b73967f97c686e09fe3d6d4f51912d01cf54: Whereas municipal elected officials have a collective responsibility to demonstrate leadership, coherence and exemplaryness in the fight against racism and discrimination;
entries.e05ad9bc5f87f922333f768192a2b5b3f7c52b4d: Whereas the City of Montreal is taking concrete and measurable action to make the municipal public service more representative and inclusive of Montréal's diversity, including black people, and to combat racial and social profiling that disproportionately affects black people;
entries.6d0201223701dac368763bf73f2a623f329a3e1e: Whereas the City of Montreal will assess measures taken to combat racism and discrimination within its ranks, and encourages all directorates and their managers to make tangible efforts to combat racism;
entries.eb4ddbd4bf3f554b4aaad70619477869ece2efe9: To mark the 35th edition of Black History Month, the Mayor of Montreal recalled the importance of recognizing the contributions of black communities to the social, cultural and economic vitality of the metropolis. She then reaffirmed the City's commitment to combat racism and systemic discrimination, including by applying a zero-tolerance policy and building dialogue, solidarity and dignity. Martinez Ferrada concluded by sharing her personal experience which confirmed the need for collective action to build an inclusive city.
entries.f4b7dffa461646ee8f519d5da7a0249ba0e5d2fd: The chair of the council, Chantal Rossi, thanked her and then gave the floor to board members who wished to speak on this Declaration: Joshua Corvil, Ericka Alneus, Nancy Blanchet, and Carla Beauvais.
entries.a44e4142d291cd4cb27d329e21ff7a1dcef527f3: From the outset, Councillor Josué Corvil presented a historical reminder of Black History Month, from its origins in the United States to its recognition in Canada, Quebec and Montreal. Subsequently, Mr. Corvil emphasized the plurality of Afro-descendant communities and the importance of their multiple contributions to the spheres of Montreal society. In conclusion, he recalled the democratic advances made by the election of people from black communities to the city council and reiterated the importance of continuing efforts to eliminate systemic racism.
entries.c1b08536337042b7a2cdf2de01d302563e211908: In her turn, the chief of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, emphasizes the importance of symbols and memory in recognizing the contribution of Black communities in Montreal. She also mentions some Afrodescendants who were honoured by the Order of Montreal thanks to their contributions to the City and then refers to the symbolic value of the name of the future station Vertières of the Montreal metro. In closing, Ms. Alneus thanks the Table du Mois de l'histoire des Noirs for her essential work and reaffirms the city council's commitment to respect and integrity for all.
entries.24df4fd70fe3184e8b4e914f637f7a9775be4f01: For her part, Councillor Nancy Blanchet shares with her colleagues a number of actions undertaken by the Borough of LaSalle aimed at recognizing the contribution of black communities to the metropolis, notably through programming developed both with local bodies and with committed people, who contribute to strengthening the social fabric and enhancing diversity. Ms Blanchet confirms her borough's support for an inclusive and open society, and to this end she asks that the names of members of her political formation be added in support of this Declaration.
entries.3ece1e98892a847fb9d47510b50da0c2ddc0b6d4: In joining her voice with those of these colleagues, Councillor Carla Beauvais recalls her 12 years of commitment to the coordination of Black History Month and states that, despite the celebration of the essential contribution of black communities in Montreal, racism and discrimination remain very real. She continues by hoping that this commemoration will become a moment of awareness, calling for transformation of institutional practices and zero tolerance against racism. Ms. Beauvais welcomes the long-standing work of the Table du Mois de l'histoire des Noirs.
entries.5092fe03bc5c8a56c2fd94ca924797e60a05effa: The Chair thanked members for their interventions and confirmed the addition of all members present as supporters to this Statement.
entries.2b8a7f89b822a399605e9a7a4ba3e88f835fd26e: 1 - marks the International Day of Remembrance for Holocaust Victims, which will take place on 27 January 2026;
entries.f48b1ce55bf6b7a90b54a16e723e48c2a5f650ff: 2 - reaffirms its commitment to combat anti-Semitism and denounces firmly and unequivocally any anti-Semitic gesture and attack, while reiterating that not all hate crimes and incidents are in the city;
entries.241d8d694e1af8fe0107dc6c66127b4fd7e93d80: 3 - continues to raise public awareness of extremism and intolerance, as well as to promote openness to others, listening, benevolence and solidarity, so that never again a tragedy like the Holocaust occurs.
entries.449bd67ad23217c378f16501ad7a19a56aafbf4b: Whereas the International Day for the Remembrance of the Victims of the Holocaust is held annually on 27 January in order to mark the liberation of the Auschwitz-Birkenau camp on that same date in 1945;
entries.8de11b8994365fd298e71a90fd806dac3cf12b83: Whereas millions of people were killed during the Second World War, including more than six million Jews, Gypsies, Slavs, Jehovah's Witnesses, political opponents, artists, persons with disabilities and those from gender diversity, making the Holocaust one of the darkest chapters in human history;
entries.dbd777502d6a9a37139355eedf9f09b9bbe6c534: Whereas after Tel Aviv and New York, Montreal is the third largest city in the world with the most survivors of the Holocaust, a community that has contributed greatly to the development and outreach of the metropolis;
entries.0e2a3f6e3bfd6398b2dee79fa2216c7fa20ab4ab: Whereas the Montreal Holocaust Museum, founded in 1979 as the Montreal Holocaust Memorial Centre, has been working for nearly 50 years to educate and raise awareness about the genocide of millions of Jewish people;
entries.da7da30b8b802d54071770b4dd48d1685f2359eb: Whereas the museum institution will be moved to new premises on Saint-Laurent Boulevard in order to enable it to meet the growing demand of the public, a major project financially supported by the City of Montreal;
entries.80066341834cb607c5572181ccd8889a1d53ffb0: Whereas the City of Montreal undertook to combat, on 21 March 1989, in its Declaration against Racial Discrimination "all forms of racial discrimination and to promote full access and participation by all citizens, regardless of their race, colour, religion, ethnic or national origin, in the various spheres of municipal life";
entries.633258bee49752267b0d79ac577a9cd0a6020dcc: Whereas in June 2020, the City Council of Montreal unanimously adopted a Declaration to recognize the systemic nature of racism and discrimination, and committed itself to combating them;
entries.c8393fd966fa21bf142433b0e2947412595cfa40: Whereas the City of Montreal proclaimed, in 2002, Yom HaShoah Day "Day of Remembrance for All Victims of the Holocaust", and committed itself to recognizing this day on a recurring basis;
entries.641636ae79854c51363e176959311def5bcaf54a: Whereas in recent years there has been a resurgence of anti-Semitic attacks and incidents in Montreal, Canada and around the world;
entries.8bb05fd44b591890ad9d1bb0a4f993114a39fcf2: Whereas, following the Round Table on Combating Anti-Semitism in Montreal in 2015, the Service de police de la Ville de Montréal established, in 2016, a Unit for Incidents and Hate Crimes allowing it to investigate more effectively reports and complaints received regarding incidents and hate crimes;
entries.8c0b5480032e1806917690ee9f37b88f4e28e0b8: Whereas the City of Montreal has established an Office of the Commissioner for Combating Racism and Systemic Discrimination, whose mandate is to put in place structural and measurable measures to combat racism and discrimination in a cross-cutting manner and to make Montreal a more just and inclusive city;
entries.c643adbc1361981e9ce428840667963a9f5420d2: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada.
entries.b58de4eb553a21d4ba4ab093b924641ef52ca12f: The Mayor of Montreal spoke and recalled that on 27 January each year the international community gathered to honour the memory of the victims of the Holocaust and to mark the liberation of the Auschwitz-Birkenau camp in 1945. To commemorate the victims of the Holocaust, she said, is to reaffirm that the fight against anti-Semitism must be constant and determined.
entries.1a5db38e08bdbc4da540df0571b872750a85de7c: Martinez Ferrada states that Montreal is the third largest city in the world for Holocaust survivors and survivors after Tel Aviv and New York. In addition, in Montreal, we also have the chance to host the Holocaust Museum, an essential place of memory, education and transmission for present and future generations. The Mayor of Montreal mentions that for several decades, Montreal has taken a number of concrete steps to combat racism and anti-Semitism. Despite the actions taken to counter anti-Semitism, our duty is to continue to denounce hateful acts, raise awareness and support our Jewish communities.
entries.f54d48c9a26dc8889e582022428d97d999d8a54d: In conclusion, the Mayor of Montreal invites all Council members to vote in favour of this Declaration, to reaffirm together our unwavering commitment to fight anti-Semitism, to defend human dignity and to make Montreal a city of memory, justice and solidarity. She highlights the presence on the balcony of members of the Jewish community and the CJA Federation.
entries.8448654a82693d441761fd3079e2edb6c25852c7: Then, Ms. Alneus took the floor and said that for the Official Opposition there was no tolerance for anti-Semitism. She recalled that Montreal was the third largest city in the world with one of the largest Jewish communities, a community that had contributed to our city, metropolis, social fabric, heritage and history. She continued by inviting people to visit the Holocaust Museum in order to discover the history of this community, better understand this tragedy so as not to recreate this type of hatred.
entries.737d698a733e41e9ca65f0a87cc42ce270bf7c06: In conclusion, as leader of the Official Opposition, she joins her voice in this Declaration to emphasize the importance of commemorating moments like these and saying loud and clear that anti-Semitism is in no way tolerable in our society.
entries.1a7f25632a265b5468acef3e34ba6b043d8b4342: Moroz, in turn, greets the members of the Jewish community present on the balcony. He continues by reiterating the remarks of the Mayor of Montreal and adds that the action to remember herself alone is not enough. Anti-Semitism is very real. In this regard, he quotes that on average 17 anti-Semitic incidents are recorded daily in Canada. He mentions that condemning anti-Semitism is not taking a stand against an international conflict but it is defending human dignity, it is protecting our fellow citizens and refusing hatred in any form. Moroz believes in particular the importance of acting upstream, educating, preventing and working with communities.
entries.835fd1e91c88fd334de2f9ab91495f28ff2a72cc: In closing, Mr. Moroz said that countering anti-Semitism remained a collective responsibility and more than ever Montreal had the capacity and power to act.
entries.60a9dfcb216c537cdb028aa7b8062fbb524b6f48: 1 - Commemorates the victims, on 29 January 2026, of the Islamophobic attack on the great mosque in Quebec City, honours the memory of the victims, salutes the courage of the survivors and expresses its solidarity with the entire Muslim community;
entries.4efefa3cb9e8453fc60f5c4cd30725084aca28d4: 2. Continue to combat Islamophobia and all forms of racism, systemic discrimination and hate speech;
entries.f0ca0a52660d0f9b7d8689e49e952a1e83851f48: 3 - continue its daily struggle against the manifestations of hatred, intolerance and violence in our society.
entries.60a8c6eda611ea68b02d5de172f91a413d04ed63: Whereas the City of Quebec experienced a great tragedy on January 29, 2017, when the Grand Mosque of Québec was the target of an Islamophobic attack that killed six people of Muslim faith and made a seventh paraplegic victim;
entries.778772caad1a8598753775e53b30f9c8ddd212f1: Whereas the attack on the great mosque in Quebec has shaken the entire Muslim community and upset the entire population of Quebec;
entries.92a537ac1f8004b5695db6cde5c25f1d311c23d4: Whereas Montrealers showed great solidarity in the aftermath of the attack on the Grand Mosque in Quebec City by organizing a gathering of thousands to pay tribute to the victims and support the Muslim community;
entries.71d5563ce9c595166eebaf5dfeccbab4cacd74d0: Whereas every year the City of Montreal commemorates the victims of the attack on the Grand Mosque of Quebec and reaffirms its commitment to combat Islamophobia, racism and discrimination, and organizes an annual ceremony in memory of the victims at the Montréal City Hall, in collaboration with the Canadian Muslim Forum;
entries.fb44fea2b203da3d464925f749446ad27400a76e: Whereas in September 2015, the National Assembly of Quebec unanimously adopted a motion to condemn Islamophobia, calls for hatred and violence against Quebec women of Muslim faith;
entries.4e4575baa4759754298558ffdd915a1d1da810cd: Whereas in March 2017, the House of Commons of Canada passed a motion to contain the climate of hatred and fear, condemning Islamophobia as well as all forms of systemic racism and religious discrimination;
entries.38b3b965678471f04e999d323fb2a20c7781e00a: Whereas UN Secretary General António Guterres declared in August 2017 that racism, xenophobia, anti-Semitism and Islamophobia are poisons for our societies;
entries.badbb37b49889dba19588dc581f0f4ad245a93f6: Whereas in 2021, the federal government proclaimed January 29 as the "National Day of Commemoration of the Attack at the Québec Mosque and Action against Islamophobia" in order to honour the victims of this tragedy and continue to fight against Islamophobia, hatred and discrimination;
entries.5e5d1b2a3ff102d7fad6f56d2765f0823a042af1: Whereas the City of Montreal has committed itself, with the Montreal Declaration against Racial Discrimination, the Montreal Declaration for Cultural Diversity and Inclusion, as well as the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities, to combat discrimination and exclusion and promote harmonious intercultural relations;
entries.5a60a23722df33a7153db9ab42b9ee5966846e8c: Whereas in June 2020, the City Council of the City of Montreal unanimously adopted a declaration recognizing the systemic nature of racism and discrimination and committed itself to combating them;
entries.01c54cbfcde10b18f858cbe097a042d99f9be440: Whereas the City of Montreal has established an Office of the Commissioner for Combating Racism and Systemic Discrimination, whose mandate is to put in place structural and measurable measures to combat racism and discrimination in a cross-cutting manner and to make Montreal a more just and inclusive city;
entries.b16eddbd2166426b4c40a95e6310bed8205ffea7: Whereas the City of Montreal Police Service established, in 2016, a Hate Crimes and Incidents Unit to more effectively investigate reports and complaints received regarding incidents and hate crimes;
entries.86270a61fcf5623fdee710e4e9d7d32b782cc97c: Whereas Muslim fellow citizens still face threats, discrimination, hate crimes and incidents and violence on account of their religious affiliation; whereas such attacks and hatred must be denounced loudly and strongly; whereas concrete actions must continue to be taken to combat them;
entries.22b0d4777f5d5b8af1785e7d9ef40f562dcc744c: Whereas the City of Montreal is working tirelessly to combat Islamophobia, racism and discrimination, and to promote the inclusion of all its citizens;
entries.2b57233a353444f4635a008e72fc95d09a27e866: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.84e0b917c2e48d99b02bad71ca286914b114279b: From the outset, the Mayor of Montreal, recalls that on January 29, it is the commemoration of the victims of the attack on the grand mosque in Quebec and an opportunity to reaffirm our commitment to fight Islamophobia. She continues and indicates that six Muslim men were torn from life and a seventh person was seriously injured during this tragedy.
entries.24526cb5fc189477cc83145ef8694d3171d6e24a: Ms. Martinez Ferrada mentioned that everyone deserves to live in dignity, respect and security; diversity is not a threat; it constitutes a wealth that we have the right and duty to protect. The Mayor of Montreal reiterated that this commemoration also represents an invitation to action, to reaffirm our commitment against Islamophobia, racism and all forms of discrimination, to strengthen our awareness-raising efforts, to build bridges between communities, to open dialogue and to bring down prejudices. She took a moment to appoint victims so that they would never be forgotten.
entries.b33054a0cec77c30662e6451074d93676a489d5a: In conclusion, the Mayor of Montreal invited Council members to fight Islamophobia, defend human dignity and make Montreal a city based on respect, solidarity and peace.
entries.0c0ac269d04f6993c1b03e2e72c60d83d00bec55: The chief of the Official Opposition, Ericka Alneus, remembered the same day on January 29, 2017, where she was present at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts for the exhibition on couples from different communities by Marie-Christine Ladouceur. This exhibition reflected today's Quebec, this plural Quebec, which is based on love, tolerance and openness to each other. When such a tragedy occurs, the entire population is affected by it. Finally, she believes that it is important to commemorate these moments to ensure that tolerance takes precedence over any form of discrimination.
entries.8145f49477248e8962539ab1add16c0d15101592: Subsequently, Councillors Sophie Mohsen and Céline-Audrey Beauregard also spoke about the growing rise of Islamophobia in public discourse, and both felt that hatred did not belong to it. Ms. Mohsen said that she was wearing the green square as a way of solidarity with families, victims and survivors. They also recalled that beyond commemorations and tributes to victims, there was a common responsibility to act to prevent such violence, through the knowledge of others and dialogue. In closing, Councillors Sophie Mohsen and Céline-Audrey Beauregard stressed that it was essential to unite in the fight against all forms of discrimination for the preservation of our most fundamental rights.
entries.e32dea86a091e70463ff8cfbb59d5dba884903bc: 1 - recognize Tamil Heritage Month in January in Montreal;
entries.6b942cbfd399d949ee2a789868a895de0e5d5251: 2 - encourages citizens to participate in Thai Pongal celebrations throughout the city in order to highlight the richness of Tamil heritage.
entries.889688fb2482ada1ab775249d9155c9e19a6471f: Whereas the Tamil community of Montreal and Quebec has a rich cultural, linguistic and historical heritage based on one of the oldest classical languages still alive;
entries.ed427cb0a485415f9c967ed9fc03c8d2f76a6797: Whereas, beginning in the early 1980s, Montreal and Quebec provided many Tamil families fleeing civil war in Sri Lanka with an environment based on human dignity, security, the rule of law and respect for fundamental rights, enabling them to establish themselves, rebuild themselves and participate fully in collective life;
entries.f2432c442b6fb3e313fada3a6d8fa6452b421cf7: Whereas the Tamil community of Montreal and Quebec reflects a diversity of backgrounds, origins and experiences, and is united by common cultural traditions, including language, as well as a deep commitment to the values of justice, solidarity and peaceful coexistence;
entries.b15f3f7f84092c7cdd65ce200e5506a6e4e242dd: Whereas January is marked by Thai Pongal, a traditional Tamil harvest festival celebrating gratitude, renewal, family and harmony with nature, and giving rise to inclusive cultural and educational activities in Montreal and Quebec;
entries.c05c1785dd83784d69f5f1c0e2232a27a3d82647: Whereas the festival of Thai Pongal is celebrated during four days in January of each year by many Tamil communities around the world, the occasion being often marked by the boiling of milk and rice, the "pongal", whose overflowing of milk symbolizes abundance and prosperity for the coming year;
entries.cd37cd587455f28f2368e15adc172ae704cac8e8: Whereas members of the Tamil community actively contribute to the social, cultural and economic development of Montreal and Quebec, in particular in the areas of health, education, entrepreneurship, public service, arts and culture, science and technology and community leadership;
entries.c5d49c148036449233a592f3f8a2e339cf83b787: Whereas Tamil community organizations and institutions play an essential role in the preservation of cultural heritage, the intergenerational transmission of language and traditions, support for young people and seniors, the promotion of volunteerism and citizen engagement;
entries.3260e7ab941a63dc431381a0075e8941f5625715: Whereas the recognition of Tamil Heritage Month in January is part of the City of Montreal's commitment to promote diversity, inclusion, collective memory, respect for human rights and living together;
entries.8274cc4f44d7cce995c1834ece5728260310dd33: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Councillor Milany Thiagarajah for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.dd73563964da9564cce700dba63e1d6616ff63c8: Ms. Thiagarajah greets the guests who are present on the balcony, highlighting the significant nature of this day, marked by a first official speech at Montreal City Hall by an elected member of the Tamil community. She thanks the Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, as well as the members of the city council for their support for this recognition.
entries.82156e8bc8abf5dd991c7c6f3e41bab9721ed63d: She mentions that this Declaration is part of an important cultural period, which coincides with the celebrations in Thai Pongal, celebrating gratitude, renewal and community solidarity. She concludes by expressing her gratitude to members of her community.
entries.886c08a3b73e3ef0610e52c9e6e053fcc78f0f6d: Elvira Carhuallan, who spoke later, cited a few examples and highlighted the valuable contribution of the Tamil community to the vitality and cultural richness of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension.
entries.2ee5a06b0516675510c3326923882ec2f860c03f: The Mayor of Montreal, Soraya Martinez Ferrada, continues and clarifies the historical character of the moment, recalling that Ms. Milany Thiagarajah is the first elected member of Tamil origin in Quebec, and congratulates the entire community on their contribution to the metropolis.
entries.e93d98108705bc26f076061afe5947f0c3d0b9dd: For her part, Ericka Alneus, Chief of the Official Opposition, greets those present on the balcony and thanks Ms Thiagarajah for the presentation of the Declaration. In closing, Councillor Alan DeSousa acknowledges, among other things, the considerable work of the Tamil community in Quebec society, both economically and culturally.
entries.c0e9a6bf66ecfaeea6ba7b1e717d20ad3bd2e3bc: 1- only on the occasion of Cancer Awareness Month for firefighters, the City of Montreal wishes to pay tribute to the SIM firefighters and their exemplary courage;
entries.2ae4c9efa42fe278cfc99c272491661cbb80d139: 2- the City of Montreal reiterates its commitment to support firefighters in the performance of their duties, to provide them with the equipment and resources necessary to ensure their safety and to ensure that their working conditions reflect the unique responsibilities and risks inherent in their profession;
entries.a16d063f02d873c04aae421ebfd43e5c2711ca28: 3- that the City of Montreal would like to sincerely thank all those who, through their commitment and sacrifice, protect the life, health and safety of the population.
entries.1398dd25555c76edb81b307582e7a9b8fad54498: Whereas Firefighters' Cancer Awareness Month is highlighted each year in January and aims to increase public understanding of occupational cancer in fire departments, while providing front-line workers with the information and tools needed to reduce risks;
entries.aad66d70fa2b50db13c9746d8c58a3aa09d99309: Whereas in 2023, Canada passed the National Framework for Fire-related Cancers Act, which provides for the development of a national framework to guide awareness efforts and improve firefighters' access to care;
entries.d3c9a95503da4cf319c8978f2e3c95b540ef51f7: Whereas, in the course of their work, firefighters and firefighters are exposed to fire, smoke and toxic chemicals, which significantly increase their risk of developing cancer;
entries.b002d8109060d6dca78ad2ce4fc2a7ac5a317367: Whereas occupational cancer of firefighters and firefighters is the leading cause of death in service in the fire department, and that by 2025 almost 80% of deaths in service among members of the International Fire Fighter Association were due to professional cancer;
entries.1236687ac3a5a173d51df354ed4ae7a278437e67: Whereas members of the Service de sécurité feuille de Montréal (SIM) are exposed to significant risks on a daily basis, and it is essential to provide them with compliant protective equipment and a safe working environment;
entries.a3f308ef334bcfa4b2146566dc5c802a380660f1: Whereas SIM is one of the largest fire services in Canada, with more than 2,700 members in 66 barracks;
entries.ac1cdd45ee9a57534b671c463bfc86c41c5e29f2: Whereas IDP 2026-2035 provides $67.3 million for the replacement of fire personnel equipment, including combat clothing;
entries.2398c286df3fb09801e4ad5bfd94579d8af6986d: The Chair, Chantal Rossi, gave the floor to Council Dimitrios (Jim) Beis for the presentation of the Declaration.
entries.c5bd2f913a7f67cd6efae44cc302fe9c2adacb8c: Mr Beis pointed out that January was Cancer Awareness Month for firefighters and recalled the high risks to which they were exposed in the performance of their duties. Counsellor Dimitrios (Jim) Beis continued by putting forward the essential work and dedication of the staff of the Montreal Fire Safety Service (SIM), particularly during the recent incident near Jacques-Cartier Bridge and during operations carried out during periods of severe cold weather. He reiterated the importance of providing them with adequate equipment and mentioned the investments planned for this purpose. In conclusion, Mr Beis welcomed the courage of SIM employees and invited the Board to adopt the statement unanimously.
entries.b6ccc82e4ba916b2cf556b450d1863266ec6295e: The Chair thanked him and gave the floor to Councillor Carla Beauvais and then to Councillor Sterling Downey.
entries.11d893dc93051d27a16a4540f88b81c98e9e8702: For her part, Ms. Beauvais highlighted the contribution of firefighters and firefighters in recent events, including periods of ice, major fires and door-to-door operations during power outages. She then highlighted the increased risks of cancer associated with the profession, which had been scientifically recognized since 2022, as well as gaps in recognition and prevention in Quebec. She referred to Montréal's particularly worrying data on the number of diagnoses and deaths attributed to a more demanding intervention context. Councillor Carla Beauvais wanted to improve their protective equipment and invited those elected to action in order to better protect SIM staff.
entries.729ec496d795d0721818d87cdaf9bf7308416b98: Mr. Downey began his intervention by thanking firefighters and firefighters for their commitment, as well as their families, knowing that they live with the risks associated with this profession on a daily basis. He referred to the less visible dangers to which they were exposed, including chemical contamination that remained in the equipment despite repeated interventions. He stressed the need to increase prevention efforts and improve the decontamination of equipment in order to better support firefighters. Counselor Sterling Downey concluded by asking to add his name to the Declaration.
entries.2e7dee3dec306b7667541e1b6351b59fdfa266d2: The Chair thanked Board members for their interventions and confirmed the addition of Councillor Sterling Downey as a supporter.

entries.d1c4f1980db9763b8b6f125e11443bfe06de3e7b: The 1359-2026 Order in Council of the 7 September 2026 sets out regulations amending the Regulations imposing conditions for the award of certain supply contracts by municipal bodies (RLRQ, chapter 19, r. 2.2). This amending regulation, which came into force on the 8 last September, introduces new requirements to encourage the acquisition of Quebec or Canadian goods, materials and equipment under municipal contracts. Specifically, the Regulations imposing conditions for the award of certain supply contracts by municipal bodies (hereinafter the Provincial Regulations) now provide a new requirement, in section 6.1, that a municipal body must, in certain prescribed circumstances, ensure that a minimum of 15 % of the total value of materials and equipment acquired for the performance of a contract originates from Canada.
entries.84d4a07988208abc9dd4c2caa330cf117d73e2b8: In 2022, the City of Montreal hired the consulting firm Marsh (Mercer) Canada Limited* at the end of Call for Bids No. 21-18851, to provide employer representatives with ongoing professional support in pension plans other than police and police. The environment of municipal pension plans has evolved significantly over the past few years and the various changes require specialized expertise and tools to continuously implement strategies and interventions in the administration and financing of pension plans. This collaboration, with an initial duration of five years (5), notably enabled the implementation of restructuring agreements, the continuation of legal remedies, the revision of investment policies and more recently representations for the renewal of different collective agreements.

entries.fc061226c970e5156cd7e3294340101ef2184057: On August 27, 2026, the City of Montreal (CG26 0472 / GDD1260590001) awarded to Mission Old Brewery, hereinafter OBM, a contract of $149,520, all taxes included, ending on October 19, 2026, by which OBM undertook to render the following professional services: Regular attendance at the L-Anonyme stop-respite, located on the wasteland of Notre-Dame, in the district of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, in order to direct persons living in homelessness to appropriate resources, to provide support in certain administrative or residential procedures and to make known the offer of available services; Unleashing and identifying the supply of housing available, including documentation of eligibility criteria and characterization of the services offered; Creation and integration of a tool for collecting housing needs of persons referred to the intervention team; Monitoring and sharing of data, including the regular production and transmission of statistics and follow-up information to the City.
entries.9460d07048dcf37824b93c8621c11984eec941a8: On April 30, the deadline for filing an application for a review of new three-year roles 2026-2027-2028 for cities in the agglomeration was met. Under section 138.3 of the Municipal Taxation Act, an application for a review filed before May 1 following the coming into force of the role must be answered by the assessor no later than September 1st. For roles 2026-2027-2028, this deadline is September 1, 2026.
